text: Conference de presse du 27 juin 2007 Press conference of 27 June 2007 Presentation du Rapport du Comite d'Etude sur le Vieillissement Presentation of the report of the Study Committee on Ageing by Guy QUADEN, Governor of the National Bank of Belgium by Guy QUADEN, Governor of the National Bank of Belgium I am pleased to present the annual report of the Study Committee on Ageing, which I now chair as Vice-President of the Higher Council of Finance, accompanied by Jan Verschooten, Vice-President of the Committee and Deputy Commissioner of the Federal Planning Bureau. You all know the general problem. There's good news: we're going, you're going to live longer. And there is bad news: it will be expensive for public finances, at least if we want to live longer in suitable conditions. The 2007 report of the Study Committee on Ageing (CEV)  the sixth of its kind  confirms the magnitude of the challenge that the ageing of the population will entail for Belgian public finances over the coming decades. Under the assumptions of the central scenario adopted by the CEV, demographic developments would result in a co-budget of ageing of 4.4% of GDP between 2006 and 2030 and 6.2% of GDP between 2006 and 2050. The expected increase in public expenditure on pensions and health care added together is 5.8% and 8.0% of GDP respectively for the periods 2006-2030 and 2006-2050, while expenditure on chage, family allowances, incapacity for work and early retirement is reported to be declining. You know the good news: we are going to live longer and the bad news: but that will be expensive for public finances. The 2007 report of the Study Committee on Ageing (SCVV) - the Commission's sixth report - confirms the scale of the challenges posed by the ageing of the population to Belgian public finances in the coming decades. Under the assumptions used by the SCVV in its baseline scenario, demographic developments would cause the budgetary costs of ageing to rise to 4.4 % of GDP between 2006 and 2030 and to 6.2 % of GDP between 2006 and 2050. The expected increase in public expenditure on pensions and health care together is 5.8 % and 8.0 % of GDP respectively for the periods 2006-2030 and 2006-2050, while expenditure on unemployment, family allowances, incapacity for work and early retirement would decrease. Compared to the SCVV's estimate in 2006, the budgetary costs of ageing were revised upwards, namely by 0.6 % of GDP by 2030 and by 0.4 % of GDP by 2050. This revision can be explained by the impact of a number of new measures on the one hand and by the reassessment of certain evolutions on the other. On the other hand, the hypotheses regarding demography, the labour market and productivity have remained virtually unchanged. Among the new measures (including the implementing rules for certain measures previously decided), mention should be made of the possibility of awarding the pension bonus to beneficiaries of the guaranteed minimum pension - a particularly important modality in the case of the pensions of self-employed workers -, the resumption by the State of the payment of SNCB's pensions (however compensated by additional revenue in terms of social contributions), the significant increase in the income guarantee for the elderly and a certain relaxation - negotiated in the framework of the last Interprofessional Agreement - of the restrictions on access to early retirement that result from the Pact of Solidarity between Generations. The reestimation of the evolution of certain expenditure has also contributed to the increase in the budgetary co-budget of ageing. It concerns the pensions of the civil service and those of La Poste. The new methodology for projecting public expenditure on long-term care for dependent elderly people did not lead to a significant change in the results. Given the uncertainties surrounding the underlying assumptions of any very long-term projection exercise, I believe it is important to assess the sensitivity of the results to changes in those assumptions. The 2007 edition of the CEV report includes sensitivity analyses of assumptions about productivity growth, employment trends and "healthy" life expectancy. I thank the secretariat of the Committee for carrying out these exercises. With regard to labour productivity, which is 1.75 % per hypothesis in the SCVV scenario, the impact of a reduced (or increased) average growth rate of 0.25 % per year was studied. The increase (or decrease) in the budgetary costs of ageing is 0.5 % of GDP by 2030 and 1 % of GDP by 2050 under the assumption that the parameters of the welfare adjustments remain unchanged compared to the baseline scenario (0.5 % increase per year in non-flat-rate benefits, 1 % increase per year in flat-rate benefits, increase of 1.25% per year of the wage limit). These results illustrate the sensitivity of the budgetary costs of ageing to productivity assumptions when the generosity of welfare adjustments is not adjusted to fluctuations in productivity growth. In a scenario in which these fluctuations have an impact on welfare adjustments, the impact on the budgetary costs of ageing is about two-thirds smaller. As regards employment, the baseline scenario assumes an increase in employment which would result in a structural unemployment rate of 8 % would be achieved gradually by 2030, representing a sharp decrease compared to the 13.9 % unemployment rate recorded in 2006. I would remind you that the concept of unemployment used in the SCVV reports is based on administrative data. It includes all persons registered as unemployed jobseekers and the older unemployed who are not looking for work. This concept differs from the harmonised unemployment rate, which is based on the data from the "labour force survey". A stricter definition of unemployment is used which does not include the older unemployed who are not looking for work. The harmonised unemployment rate, which we use in the National Bank's reports and which was 8.2 % in 2006, is therefore considerably lower than the unemployment rate mentioned in this report. In an alternative scenario, the impact of an increase in employment was studied where unemployment would fall to 4 % in 2030 and remain at that level until 2050, at the same time the number of early retirees would be reduced by half compared to the baseline scenario. In this alternative scenario, the employment rate would be increased by 3.6 percentage points. This corresponds to around 230,000 jobs in 2050 and to an economic growth rate that would be higher on average by 0.12% per year over the projection horizon. In this scenario, the budgetary costs of ageing would be 1.4% of GDP lower. In a reverse scenario, where structural unemployment would only fall to 12% by 2030 and the number of early retirees would be 50% higher compared to the baseline scenario, the budgetary costs of ageing would increase by an additional 1.5% of GDP. The budgetary costs of ageing therefore appear to be particularly sensitive to employment prospects. To reduce the bill for aging, or facilitate payment, it is therefore clear that three actions are necessary simultaneously: -accelerate the reduction of public debt and related burdens through the creation of structural budget surpluses, in order to free up resources for age-related expenditure; -stimulate productivity gains; -increase the employment rate. Increasing productivity and employment at the same time is a huge challenge. There was a time when productivity gains in Belgium were among the highest in the world (1.7% for example between 1985 and 1995) but this situation was accompanied by a stagnation of employment. Over the past decade, the pace of job creation has, on the contrary, intensified, but productivity growth has slowed to around 1.35% per year. The report contains a third sensitivity study on what might be called healthy life expectancy. In the central scenario, the CEV has, in the interests of prudence, postulated that there is no repercussion of the increase in life expectancy on the expectation of life expectancy. healthy life. In other words, in this central scenario, the impact of age on the profile of individual acute care expenditures or on the probability of long-term care use is unchanged throughout the projection period. The alternative scenario assumes that healthy life expectancy increases by half of the gains in life expectancy. In other words, given an increase in life expectancy at birth of 5 years between 2000 and 2030, being 80 years of age in 2030 has an impact on average acute care expenditures or on the likelihood of using long-term care equivalent to being 77.5 years old in 2000. This alternative scenario results in a significant decline in the co-budget of ageing, of the order of 1% of GDP by 2050. Finally, this 2007 report, which is particularly rich, still includes two special studies on the risk of poverty among the elderly and the development of 2nd pillar pensions. Monetary indicators show that the elderly population is more at risk of poverty than the rest of the population: 20.6 per cent of individuals aged 65 and over have an income below the poverty line, while this figure is 12.2 per cent among individuals aged 16 to 64; within the elderly population, women, the elderly and the isolated are the most vulnerable. However, this picture needs to be nuanced. On the one hand, the income of older people at risk of poverty is less far from the poverty line than it is for younger individuals. On the other hand, according to non-monetary indicators relating in particular to the quality of housing or access to care, the elderly population has fewer poverty problems than the rest of the population. Having said that, the fact remains that, despite various measures that have led to an increase in the income guarantee for the elderly and the increase in the minimum pension in the salaried and self-employed scheme, the risk of poverty among the elderly has not disappeared and, in our case, the reduction in pensions, unlike the other measures I have mentioned, should not be considered to reduce the cos of aging. Finally, this annual report focuses on the development of the second pension pillar following the law on supplementary pensions and the law on supplementary pensions for the self-employed. Only a limited number of data could be made available by the CBFA. However, some tentative conclusions could already be drawn. The coverage ratio of wap-compliant sector pensions would increase from 16 % in 2003 to 18 % in 2007. Furthermore, in terms of the number of affiliated employees, the sector pensions are not yet large enough to have a strong influence on the funding ratio of the entire second pillar. The total funding ratio is estimated to be between 51 and 59 % in 2007. The few data currently available show that around 20% of the active self-employed are affiliated to a free-to-do scheme. supplementary pension for the self-employed, of which 43% have a social PSPS contract.

U kent het goede nieuws : we gaan langer leven en het slechte nieuws : maar dat zal duur zijn voor de openbare financi<91>n. Het rapport van de Studiecommissie voor de vergrijzing (SCvV) van 2007 - het zesde verslag van de Commissie - bevestigt de omvang van de uitdagingen waarvoor de vergrijzing van de bevolking de Belgische overheidsfinanci<91>n plaatst in de komende decennia. Onder de door de SCvV in haar basisscenario gehanteerde hypothesen zouden de demografische evoluties ervoor zorgen dat de budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing oplopen tot 4,4 % van het bbp tussen 2006 en 2030 en tot 6,2 % van het bbp tussen 2006 en 2050. De verwachte toename van de overheidsuitgaven voor pensioenen en gezondheidszorg samen bedraagt respectievelijk 5,8 % en 8,0 % van het bbp voor de periodes 2006-2030 en 2006-2050, terwijl de uitgaven voor werkloosheid, kinderbijslag, arbeidsongeschiktheit en brugpensioen zouden dalen. In vergelijking met de raming van de SCvV in 2006, werden de budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing opwaarts herzien, namelijk met 0,6 % van het bbp tegen 2030 en met 0,4 % van het bbp tegen 2050. Die herziening kan worden verklaard door de impact van een aantal nieuwe maatregelen enerzijds en door de herschatting van bepaalde evoluties anderzijds. Daarentegen zijn de hypothesen met betrekking tot de demografie, de arbeidsmarkt en de productiviteit nagenoeg ongewijzigd gebleven. Parmi les mesures nouvelles (en ce compris les modalit<8e>s d'ex<8e>cution de certaines mesures d<8e>cid<8e>es ant<8e>rieurement), il faut citer la possibilit<8e> d'attribuer le bonus pension aux b<8e>n<8e>ficiaires de la pension minimum garantie - modalit<8e> particuli<8f>rement importante dans le cas des pensions des travailleurs ind<8e>pendants -, la reprise par l'Etat du paiement des pensions de la SNCB (toutefois compens<8e>e par des recettes suppl<8e>mentaires en mati<8f>re de cotisations sociales), le rel<8f>vement important de la garantie de revenu aux personnes <89>g<8e>es et un certain assouplissement -n<8e>goci<8e> dans le cadre du dernier Accord Interprofessionnel - des restrictions <88> l'acc<8f>s <88> la pr<8e>pension qui d<8e>coulent du Pacte de solidarit<8e> entre les g<8e>n<8e>rations. La r<8e>estimation de l'<8e>volution de certaines d<8e>penses a <8e>galement contribu<8e> <88> l'accroissement du co budg<8e>taire du vieillissement. Elle concerne les pensions de la fonction publique et celles de La Poste. La nouvelle m<8e>thodologie de projection des d<8e>penses publiques de soins de longue dur<8e>e dispens<8e>s aux personnes <89>g<8e>es d<8e>pendantes n'a quant <88> elle pas occasionn<8e> de modification significative des r<8e>sultats. Compte tenu des incertitudes qui entourent les hypoth<8f>ses de base de tout exercice de projection <88> tr<8f>s long terme, il me semble important d'<8e>valuer la sensibilit<8e> des r<8e>sultats <88> des modifications de ces hypoth<8f>ses. L'<8e>dition 2007 du rapport du CEV comprend des analyses de sensibilit<8e> portant sur les hypoth<8f>ses en mati<8f>re de croissance de la productivit<8e>, d'<8e>volution de l'emploi et d'esp<8e>rance de vie "en bonne sant<8e>". Je remercie le secr<8e>tariat du Comit<8e> de s'<90>tre livr<8e> <88> ces exercices. Wat de arbeidsproductiviteit betreft, die per hypothese 1,75 % bedraagt in het SCvV-scenario, werd de impact van een verlaagde (of verhoogde) gemiddelde groeivoet van 0,25 % per jaar bestudeerd. De stijging (of daling) van de budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing bedraagt 0,5 % van het bbp tegen 2030 en 1 % van het bbp tegen 2050 in de hypothese waarin de parameters van de welvaartsaanpassingen onveranderd blijven ten opzichte van het basisscenario (stijging van 0,5 % per jaar van de niet-forfaitaire uitkeringen, toename van 1 % per jaar van de forfaitaire uitkeringen, verhoging van 1,25 % per jaar van de loongrens). Deze resultaten illustreren de gevoeligheid van de budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing voor de productiviteitshypothesen wanneer de generositeit van de welvaartsaanpassingen niet wordt aangepast aan de schommelingen van de productiviteitsgroei. In een scenario waarin die schommelingen een weerslag hebben op de welvaartsaanpassingen, is de impact op de budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing ongeveer twee derde kleiner. Wat de werkgelegenheid betreft, gaat het basisscenario uit van een toename van de werkgelegenheid waarmee een structurele werkloosheidsgraad van 8 % geleidelijk zou worden bereikt tegen 2030, wat een forse daling inhoudt ten opzichte van de werkloosheidsgraad van 13,9 % die werd opgetekend in 2006. Ik herinner eraan dat het werkloosheidsconcept dat in de verslagen van de SCvV wordt gebruikt is gebaseerd op administratieve gegevens. Het omvat alle personen die zijn ingeschreven als niet-werkende werkzoekenden en de oudere niet-werkzoekende werklozen. Dit concept onderscheidt zich van de geharmoniseerde werkloosheidsgraad, die is gebaseerd op de gegevens van de "arbeidskrachtenenqu<90>te". Hierbij wordt een striktere definitie van werkloosheid gehanteerd waarin de oudere niet-werkzoekende werklozen niet zijn opgenomen. De geharmoniseerde werkloosheidsgraad, die we in de verslagen van de Nationale Bank gebruiken en die in 2006 8,2 % bedroeg, ligt dan ook aanzienlijk lager dan de werkloosheidsgraad die in dit verslag wordt vermeld. In een alternatief scenario werd de impact bestudeerd van een toename van de werkgelegenheid waarbij de werkloosheid zou terugvallen tot 4 % in 2030 en op dat niveau zou blijven tot 2050, terzelfder tijd zou het aantal bruggepensioneerden met de helft verminderen in vergelijking met het basisscenario. In dit alternatieve scenario zou de werkgelegenheidsgraad worden verhoogd met 3,6 procentpunten. Dat stemt overeen met ongeveer 230.000 banen in 2050 en met een economische groeivoet die gemiddeld met 0,12 % per jaar hoger zou liggen tijdens de projectieperiode. In dit scenario zouden de budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing 1,4 % van het bbp lager uitvallen. In een omgekeerd scenario, waarbij de structurele werkloosheid slechts zou dalen tot 12 % tegen 2030 en het aantal bruggepensioneerden 50 % hoger zou liggen in vergelijking met het basisscenario, zouden de budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing bijkomend met 1,5 % bbp toenemen. De budgettaire kosten van de vergrijzing lijken dus bijzonder gevoelig te zijn voor de werkgelegenheidsvooruitzichten. Pour r<8e>duire la facture du vieillissement, ou en faciliter le paiement, il est donc clair que trois actions s'imposent simultan<8e>ment : -acc<8e>l<8e>rer la r<8e>duction de la dette publique et les charges qui y sont li<8e>es par la constititution d'exc<8e>dents budg<8e>taires structurels, afin de lib<8e>rer des ressources pour les d<8e>penses li<8e>es au vieillissement; -stimuler les gains de productivit<8e>; -renforcer le taux d'emploi. Accro<94>tre simultan<8e>ment la productivit<8e> et l'emploi est un <8e>norme d<8e>fi. Il fut une <8e>poque oles gains de productivit<8e> en Belgique <8e>taient parmi les plus <8e>lev<8e>s au monde (1,7 % par exemple entre 1985 et 1995) mais cette situation s'accompagnait d'une stagnation de l'emploi. Depuis une dizaine d'ann<8e>es, le rythme de cr<8e>ation d'emplois s'est, au contraire, intensifi<8e> mais la croissance de la productivit<8e> a ralenti aux alentours de 1,35 % par an. Le rapport contient une troisi<8f>me <8e>tude de sensibilit<8e> consacr<8e> <88> ce que l'on pourrait appeler l'esp<8e>rance de vie en bonne sant<8e>. Dans le sc<8e>nario central, le CEV a, dans un souci de prudence, postul<8e> l'absence de toute r<8e>percussion de l'augmentation de l'esp<8e>rance de vie sur l'esp<8e>rance de vie en bonne sant<8e>. En d'autres termes, dans ce sc<8e>nario central, l'impact de l'<89>ge sur le profil des d<8e>penses individuelles de soins aigus ou sur la probabilit<8e> de recours aux soins de longue dur<8e>e est inchang<8e> tout au long de la p<8e>riode de projection. Le sc<8e>nario alternatif suppose que l'esp<8e>rance de vie en bonne sant<8e> s'accro<94>t <88> concurrence de la moiti<8e> des gains d'esp<8e>rance de vie. Autrement dit, compte tenu d'une hausse de l'esp<8e>rance de vie <88> la naissance de 5 ann<8e>es entre 2000 et 2030, le fait d'<90>tre <89>g<8e> de 80 ans en 2030 a sur les d<8e>penses moyennes de soins aigus ou sur la probabilit<8e> de recours aux soins de longue dur<8e>e un impact <8e>quivalent au fait d'<90>tre <89>g<8e> de 77,5 ans en 2000. Ce sc<8e>nario alternatif a pour r<8e>sultat un recul notable du co budg<8e>taire du vieillissement, de l'ordre de 1 % du PIB <88> l'horizon 2050. Enfin, ce rapport 2007, particuli<8f>rement riche, comporte encore deux <8e>tudes sp<8e>ciales sur le risque de pauvret<8e> chez les personnes <89>g<8e>es et le d<8e>veloppement des pensions du 2<8f>me pilier. Les indicateurs mon<8e>taire montrent que la population <89>g<8e>e est davantage expos<8e>e <88> un risque de pauvret<8e> que le reste de la population : 20,6 % des individus <89>g<8e>s de 65 ans et plus ont un revenu inf<8e>rieur au seuil de pauvret<8e>, alors que ce chiffre est de 12,2 % parmi les individus <89>g<8e>s de 16 <88> 64 ans; au sein de la population <89>g<8e>e, les femmes, les plus <89>g<8e>s et les isol<8e>s sont les plus vuln<8e>rables. Cette image doit toutefois <90>tre nuanc<8e>e. D'une part, le revenu des personnes <89>g<8e>es expos<8e>es <88> un risque de pauvret<8e> est moins <8e>loign<8e> du seuil de pauvret<8e> qu'il ne l'est pour les individus plus jeunes. D'autre part, selon des indicateurs non mon<8e>taires relatifs notamment <88> la qualit<8e> du logement ou <88> l'acc<8f>s aux soins, la population <89>g<8e>e rencontre moins de probl<8f>mes de pauvret<8e> que le reste de la population. Cela dit, il n'en demeure pas moins que, malgr<8e> diff<8e>rentes mesures qui ont entra<94>n<8e> un rel<8f>vement <88> la garantie de revenu aux personnes <89>g<8e>es et l'augmentation de la pension minimum dans le r<8e>gime salari<8e> et ind<8e>pendant, le risque de pauvret<8e> chez les personnes <89>g<8e>es n'a pas disparu et, chez nous, la diminution des pensions, <88> la diff<8e>rence des autres mesures que j'ai mentionn<8e>es, ne doit pas <90>tre envisag<8e>e pour r<8e>duire les cos du vieillissement. In dit jaarverslag wordt ten slotte aandacht besteed aan de ontwikkeling van de tweede pensioenpijler naar aanleiding van de wet betreffende de aanvullende pensioenen en de wet betreffende de aanvullende pensioenen voor zelfstandigen. Er kon nog maar een beperkt aantal gegevens beschikbaar worden gesteld door de CBFA. Enige voorzichtige conclusies konden echter al wel worden getrokken. De dekkingsgraad van de WAP-conforme sectorpensioenen zou van 16 % in 2003 stijgen tot 18 % in 2007. Verder zijn de sectorpensioenen in termen van aantal aangesloten werknemers nog niet groot genoeg om de dekkingsgraad van de volledige tweede pijler sterk te kunnen be<95>nvloeden. De totale dekkingsgraad wordt immers geraamd tussen 51 en 59 % in 2007. Uit de weinige gegevens die momenteel beschikbaar zijn, blijkt dat ongeveer 20 % van de actieve zelfstandigen aangesloten is bij een regeling inzake het vrij aanvullend pensioen zelfstandigen, waarvan 43 % een sociaal VAPZ-contract heeft.

Title: 2007 Report of the Higher Employment Council
text: 2007 REPORT OF THE HIGHER EMPLOYMENT COUNCIL Introduction by Mr J. Smets, Vice-President, on the occasion of the presentation of 29 June 2007 1. RECENT LABOUR MARKET DEVELOPMENTS In recent years, employment has developed favourably in a context of economic improvement. In 2005 and 2006, it increased by 41,000 and 46,000 units respectively, and an increase of 60,000 units is expected for 2007. Given that the working population - that is, the number of people entering the labour market - is expected to increase by only 22,000 units, the number of jobseekers is expected to record a significant decrease, by 39,000 units. As a result, the employment rate - the ratio of the number of workers to the working-age population - is expected to rise this year from 61 to 61.5 per cent, while the chage rate is expected to contract from 8.3 to 7.6 per cent of the labour force; this decline echoes the decline that has also been recorded in the European Union. These encouraging results should not make us lose sight of the fact that the Belgian labour market still faces important structural problems: -the employment rate remains well below the European average: in 2006 (the latest year for which international comparisons are available), it was 61 p.c., 3.3 percentage points below the EU27 average and 5 percentage points below the EU15 average, while the European target for 2010 (70 p.c.) remains largely out of reach; -a delay persists with regard to the other two European objectives, namely an employment rate of 60 p.c. for women (54 p.c. in Belgium and 58.4 p.c. in the EU15) and 50 p.c. for people aged over 55 (32 p.c. in Belgium and 45.3 p.c. in the EU15); -as this presentation will highlight, the employment outcomes of other groups such as people of foreign origin and young people remain problematic; -a significant regional dispersion persists: from a European perspective, the employment rate is particularly low in Wallonia and Brussels and reaches an average level in Flanders; -the recent decline in unemployment has had no impact on the number of long-term unemployed (more than two years). The Council therefore continues to advocate a policy that promotes activation and participation in the labour market: - further strengthening the programme for the activation of jobseekers, organising and deepening support from the moment of registration as jobseekers, particularly for the low-skilled, better characterising the group of compensated workers unavailable for medical or social reasons in order to develop a specific strategy for them, and intensifying collaboration between regional employment services; - by increasing the participation of seniors, in particular by extending the activation programme to people over 50 (between 2006 and 2011, the population of people aged 55 to 64 will continue to grow, by 128,000 units, while the population of people aged 25 to 54 will decrease by 87,000 units!); - by stepping up efforts in education and training, but also in mobility. 2. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES ON THE LABOUR MARKET 2007 is the European Year of Equal Opportunities and, as such, the Council has decided to look further at equal opportunities in our labour market. An examination of the situation of men and women on the labour market, by level of training, age group and nationality, shows that the situation of several groups - in terms of employment, chage and inactivity - is much less favourable than might be expected on the basis of their relative importance in the population. These are women, young people, seniors, as well as foreigners, especially those from countries outside the EU. The first three groups cannot be considered homogeneously as risk groups: a more in-depth analysis highlights that the most qualified people have above-average rates of labour market participation, while the participation of the less qualified is below average. This observation leads the Council to make a first recommendation, namely that an effective equal opportunities policy necessarily requires an improvement in the level of training, including the enhancement of skills, which must enable everyone to benefit from the same opportunities for sustainable integration into the labour market. The Council also recommends a policy that promotes diversity and combats discrimination based on sex, age or nationality. This policy should be based on: -the development of a pedagogy of knowledge and recognition of others, for example by raising awareness of intercultural management among business leaders and heads of human resources departments; -an active diversity policy in education and administration but also in companies (for example by negotiating integration objectives at sectoral level); -the rejection of all forms of discrimination, in application of the legislation guaranteeing equal opportunities for all. These policy guidelines must make it possible to considerably limit the under-representation of several groups in the labour market, not least because all the labour force - not only those already looking for work, but also the far too large group of inactive people - will have to be mobilised in order to maintain a sufficient supply of labour. The Council carried out a more detailed examination of the situation of the above-mentioned groups. - namely young people, women, persons of foreign origin and the elderly, as well as persons with disabilities (see points 3 to 7 below). 3. YOUNG PEOPLE The Council examined the situation of the group of young people aged 15 to 29 in order to better understand the process of integration taking place in this period of life. In the group of young people aged 15 to 19, students occupy a preponderant place, which decreases to one third among young people aged 20 to 24, while almost 80% of young people aged 25 to 29 work. But at the same time, however, a relatively large percentage of jobseekers is observed. Successful integration into the labour market depends above all on the level of qualification. Thanks to the level of educational performance, the Flemish Community achieves excellent results, while the French Community remains below the OECD average. In all communities, there is still progress to be made in order to achieve a better distribution of results for the widest possible group. While the average level of education of young people, and in particular women, in Belgium is higher than the EU25 average, the early school leaving rate - although slightly lower than in the EU - remains high, reaching almost 11 p.c. for women and 15 p.c. for men. Between 2000 and 2005, no progress was made in this area, quite the contrary. Early school leavers are too poorly qualified. They are therefore faced with greater integration problems and, particularly in some cities, then run the risk of getting bogged down in unemployment. In Brussels and Wallonia, only a minority of low-skilled young people work and the unemployment rate of this group reaches 34 p.c. in Wallonia and 44 p.c. in Brussels. In the light of this information, the Council calls not only for special attention by public employment services to less qualified young people, but also for: -the fight against early school leaving, accompanied by regular monitoring and the development of a sufficiently long common curriculum, which teaches young people the skills necessary for their personal development and subsequent orientation between the different streams, taking care to avoid stereotypes relating to each other's social res; -better recognition of skills acquired at school and during the course of a career; - the promotion of diversity, as in the case of initiatives in higher education in Flanders; - internships in companies, benefiting from a real training content and sufficient supervision, and alternance training formulas such as the "socio-professional integration agreements" which exist in the French Community - formulas which can benefit from the support of the public authorities; -a specific approach to public employment services, similar to the action carried out by the VDAB in thirteen urban centres. 4. WOMEN Women's participation in the labour market has risen sharply, in parallel with the improvement of their average level of training. This welcome increase cannot go hand in hand with a decrease in the quality of jobs held by women. Strict equality of treatment between men and women must therefore be ensured throughout one's career. However, the facts show: - whereas women work much more part-time than men, particularly in households with children, which shows that it is mainly women who reduce their professional activity in favour of a better combination of work and family life, which can lead to slower career development, more problems of reintegration, etc.; - that the European childcare objectives - childcare services must have places for at least one third of children under the age of three the 2010 horizon - are almost reached, but that low-skilled people make less use of creches than highly qualified people; -that there is still a wage gap to the detriment of women, although it must be acknowledged that this difference has narrowed in Belgium to one of the lowest levels in the EU; -that this difference is partly (but certainly not exclusively) attributable to the choice of studies which, for women, remains strongly oriented towards certain subjects, in university education for example. To encourage women's participation on an equal basis, the Board of Governors recommends: - a development of childcare places, in favour of a large and well-distributed offer throughout the territory, paying particular attention to affordability for low-income families; - a more equitable sharing of domestic and parental responsibilities (access to parental leave, etc.); -gender-neutral job classifications and scale increases; -specific attention to the situation of women with an immigrant background. 5. PERSONS OF FOREIGN ORIGIN The participation of nationals of non-European countries (which especially in Brussels represent a significant part of the population) in our labour market is particularly low: their employment rate is only 35 p.c., the lowest level in the EU, while the gap with the employment rate of nationals (62 p.c.) is one of the highest at European level. It is above all the employment rate of women from non-European countries that is particularly low: it is only 21 p.c., compared with 55 p.c. for Belgian women. It should be noted that the second and third generations of migrants, although of Belgian nationality, seem to have more difficulty integrating into the labour market than the first generation. It should also be noted that the training of nationals of non-European countries has a rather low yield: the gap in the employment rate with Belgians is even greater for the highly qualified than for the least qualified. According to the Council, an effective policy towards this group (which can currently only be measured on the basis of nationality, which somewhat complicates the assessment of the whole problem) requires: -efforts to promote the learning of national languages and directed towards families as a whole; - the promotion of affordable childcare facilities; - recognition of skills acquired in the country of origin; -specific efforts on the part of public employment services; -the development of diversity plans, which have already been mentioned. 6. SENIORS Participation in the labour market decreases considerably among the elderly: the share of workers rises from 69 p.c. among those aged 50-54, to 44 per cent among those aged 55-59 and only to 16 per cent among those aged over 60. Although the employment rate of the latter two groups has increased, thanks in particular to the lengthening of women's careers and a package of measures limiting the possibilities of early departure, further progress is needed in all regions, and more particularly for women, less qualified workers and nationals of non-European countries. In 2006, almost one third of people aged 50 to 64 had left the labour market by using the status of senior unemployed, full-time early retirement, full career break, full-time credit, pension or disability. Recommendations made earlier by the Council have been echoed in the Pact of Solidarity between Generations, the provisions of which must be fully implemented. In addition to the policy of activating older jobseekers already mentioned, the Council calls for particular attention to be paid to: - the opportunity offered to the social partners by the prohibition of age-based scale wage increases to re-examine the wage training process from a new angle, taking into account, for example, training, experience and productivity; - the need to promote training and mobility, including of older workers, in an appropriate human resources policy; - the need to continue to strictly restrict access to early retirement (by providing for exceptions based, for example, on the arduousness of the profession). 7. PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES According to data from an ad hoc module of the Labour Force Survey, 17 per cent of the working-age population, or about 1.1 million people, suffered from a disability or chronic health problem in 2002. The employment rate of this group is much lower than that of the able-bodied: 42.5 against 64.3 p.c. Several factors hinder the participation of the less able-bodied: their state of health or disability, the inadequacy of job offers or working conditions, but also their low average level of training: some 58 per cent of the group concerned is poorly qualified, which is much more than among the able-bodied. In this context, the Council recommends various actions including: -reasonable accommodation (possibly supported by the public authorities) with infrastructure, timetables and technology, which may increase the integration opportunities for people with disabilities; -specific attention from the public employment services, to help these people find suitable employment.

Ces r<8e>sultats encourageants ne doivent pas nous faire perdre de vue que le march<8e> du travail belge doit encore faire face <88> d'importants probl<8f>mes structurels: -le taux d'emploi reste nettement inf<8e>rieur <88> la moyenne europ<8e>enne: en 2006 (la derni<8f>re ann<8e>e pour laquelle des comparaisons internationales sont disponibles), il s'<8e>levait <88> 61 p.c., soit 3,3 points de pourcentage de moins que la moyenne de l'UE27 et 5 points de pourcentage en de<8d><88> de celle de l'UE15, alors que l'objectif europ<8e>en <88> l'horizon 2010 (70 p.c.) reste largement hors d'atteinte; -un retard persiste en ce qui concerne les deux autres objectifs europ<8e>ens, <88> savoir un taux d'emploi de 60 p.c. pour les femmes (54 p.c. en Belgique et 58,4 p.c. dans l'UE15) et de 50 p.c. pour les personnes <89>g<8e>es de plus de 55 ans (32 p.c. en Belgique et 45,3 p.c. dans l'UE15); -comme le soulignera cet expos<8e>, les r<8e>sultats en mati<8f>re d'emploi d'autres groupes tels que les personnes d'origine <8e>trang<8f>re et les jeunes restent probl<8e>matiques; -une dispersion r<8e>gionale notable persiste: dans une perspective europ<8e>enne, le taux d'emploi est particuli<8f>rement faible en Wallonie et <88> Bruxelles et il atteint un niveau moyen en Flandre; -le r<8e>cent recul du chmage n'a eu aucune incidence sur le nombre de chmeurs de longue dur<8e>e (plus de deux ans). Aussi le Conseil continue-t-il de plaider en faveur d'une politique qui favorise l'activation et la participation au march<8e> du travail: - en renfor<8d>ant davantage le programme d'activation des demandeurs d'emploi, en organisant et en approfondissant l'accompagnement d<8f>s l'inscription en tant que demandeur d'emploi, particuli<8f>rement pour les peu qualifi<8e>s, en caract<8e>risant mieux le groupe des cheurs indemnis<8e>s indisponibles pour raisons m<8e>dicales ou sociales afin de d<8e>velopper une strat<8e>gie sp<8e>cifique en leur faveur, et en intensifiant la collaboration entre les services r<8e>gionaux de l'emploi; - en accroissant la participation des seniors, notamment en <8e>tendant le programme d'activation aux personnes <89>g<8e>es de plus de 50 ans (entre 2006 et 2011, la population des personnes <89>g<8e>es de 55 <88> 64 ans continuera de s'accro<94>tre, de 128.000 unit<8e>s, tandis que la population des personnes <89>g<8e>es de 25 <88> 54 ans baissera de 87.000 unit<8e>s!); - en intensifiant les efforts en mati<8f>re d'<8e>ducation et de formation, mais aussi de mobilit<8e>. 2. <83>GALIT<83> DES CHANCES SUR LE MARCH<83> DU TRAVAIL 2007 est l'ann<8e>e europ<8e>enne de l'<8e>galit<8e> des chances et, <88> ce titre, le Conseil a d<8e>cid<8e> d'examiner plus avant l'<8e>galit<8e> des chances sur notre march<8e> du travail. L'examen de la situation des hommes et des femmes sur le march<8e> du travail, par niveau de formation, par tranche d'<89>ge et par nationalit<8e>, fait appara<94>tre que la situation de plusieurs groupes - en mati<8f>re d'emploi, de chage et d'inactivit<8e> - est nettement moins favorable que ce <88> quoi l'on pourrait s'attendre sur la base de leur importance relative dans la population. Il s'agit des femmes, des jeunes, des seniors, de m<90>me que des <8e>trangers, en particulier ceux issus de pays hors de l'UE. Les trois premiers groupes ne peuvent <90>tre consid<8e>r<8e>s de mani<8f>re homog<8f>ne comme des groupes <88> risque: une analyse plus approfondie souligne en effet que les personnes les plus qualifi<8e>es pr<8e>sentent des taux de participation au march<8e> du travail, sup<8e>rieurs <88> la moyenne, tandis que la participation, des personnes moins qualifi<8e>es est inf<8e>rieure <88> la moyenne. Cette constatation am<8f>ne le Conseil <88> formuler une premi<8f>re recommandation, <88> savoir qu'une politique d'<8e>galit<8e> des chances efficace passe n<8e>cessairement par une am<8e>lioration du niveau de formation, en ce compris la valorisation des comp<8e>tences, qui doit permettre <88> tous de b<8e>n<8e>ficier des m<90>mes chances d'insertion durable sur le march<8e> du travail. Le Conseil recommande <8e>galement de mener une politique favorisant la diversit<8e> et luttant contre la discrimination fond<8e>e sur le sexe, l'<89>ge ou la nationalit<8e>. Cette politique devrait reposer sur: -le d<8e>veloppement d'une p<8e>dagogie de la connaissance et de la reconnaissance de l'autre, par exemple par la sensibilisation des chefs d'entreprise et des chefs de services des ressources humaines au management interculturel; -une politique active de diversit<8e> dans l'enseignement et dans l'administration mais <8e>galement dans les entreprises (par exemple en n<8e>gociant des objectifs d'insertion au niveau sectoriel); -le rejet de toute forme de discrimination, en application de la l<8e>gislation garantissant l'<8e>galit<8e> des chances pour tous. Ces orientations politiques doivent permettre de limiter consid<8e>rablement la sous-repr<8e>sentation de plusieurs groupes sur le march<8e> du travail, notamment parce que toutes les forces de travail - pas uniquement les personnes qui recherchent d<8e>j<88> un emploi, mais <8e>galement le groupe bien trop important des personnes inactives - devront <90>tre mobilis<8e>es afin de maintenir une offre de main-d'<cf>uvre suffisante. Le Conseil a proc<8e>d<8e> <88> un examen plus d<8e>taill<8e> de la situation des groupes susmentionn<8e>s - <88> savoir les jeunes, les femmes, les personnes d'origine <8e>trang<8f>re et les seniors -, de m<90>me que des personnes moins valides (voir points 3 <88> 7 ci-apr<8f>s). 3. LES JEUNES Le Conseil a examin<8e> la situation du groupe des jeunes de 15 <88> 29 ans afin de mieux cerner le processus d'insertion qui s'op<8f>re dans cette p<8e>riode de la vie. Dans le groupe des jeunes <89>g<8e>s de 15 <88> 19 ans, les <8e>tudiants occupent une place pr<8e>pond<8e>rante, qui diminue pour atteindre un tiers parmi les jeunes <89>g<8e>s de 20 <88> 24 ans, tandis que pr<8f>s de 80 p.c. des jeunes <89>g<8e>s de 25 <88> 29 ans travaillent. Une insertion r<8e>ussie sur le march<8e> du travail d<8e>pend avant tout du niveau de qualification. Gr<89>ce au niveau de performance obtenu en mati<8f>re d'enseignement, la Communaut<8e> flamande obtient d'excellents r<8e>sultats, tandis que la Communaut<8e> fran<8d>aise demeure sous la moyenne de l'OCDE. Dans toutes les communaut<8e>s, il y encore des progr<8f>s <88> r<8e>aliser afin de parvenir <88> une meilleure r<8e>partition des r<8e>sultats pour le groupe le plus large possible. Si le niveau de formation moyen des jeunes, et en particulier des femmes, est en Belgique sup<8e>rieur <88> la moyenne de l'UE25, le taux de d<8e>crochage scolaire - m<90>me s'il est l<8e>g<8f>rement inf<8e>rieur <88> celui de l'UE - reste <8e>lev<8e>, atteignant pr<8f>s de 11 p.c. pour les femmes et 15 p.c. pour les hommes. Entre 2000 et 2005, aucun progr<8f>s n'a par ailleurs <8e>t<8e> enregistr<8e> dans ce domaine, bien au contraire. Les jeunes en d<8e>crochage scolaire sont trop peu qualifi<8e>s. Ils sont d<8f>s lors confront<8e>s <88> des probl<8f>mes d'insertion plus importants et, particuli<8f>rement dans certaines villes, encourent ensuite le risque de s'enliser dans le chmage. <cb> Bruxelles et en Wallonie, seule une minorit<8e> de jeunes peu qualifi<8e>s travaillent et le taux de chmage de ce groupe atteint 34 p.c. en Wallonie et 44 p.c. <88> Bruxelles. <cb> la lumi<8f>re de ces informations, le Conseil plaide, non seulement en faveur d'une attention particuli<8f>re des services publics de l'emploi pour les jeunes moins qualifi<8e>s, mais aussi en faveur: -de la lutte contre le d<8e>crochage scolaire, accompagn<8e>e d'un suivi r<8e>gulier et de la mise au point d'un cursus commun suffisamment long, qui enseigne aux jeunes les comp<8e>tences n<8e>cessaires <88> leur d<8e>veloppement personnel et <88> leur orientation ult<8e>rieure entre les diff<8e>rentes fili<8f>res, en veillant <88> <8e>viter les st<8e>r<8e>otypes relatifs au re social des uns et des autres; -d'une meilleure reconnaissance des comp<8e>tences acquises <88> l'<8e>cole et au cours de la carri<8f>re; - de l'encouragement de la diversit<8e>, <88> l'instar des initiatives prises dans l'enseignement sup<8e>rieur en Flandre; - de stages en entreprises, b<8e>n<8e>ficiant d'un r<8e>el contenu formatif et d'un encadrement suffisant, et de formules de formation en alternance telles que les "conventions d'insertion socioprofessionnelle" qui existent en Communaut<8e> fran<8d>aise - formules qui peuvent b<8e>n<8e>ficier du soutien des pouvoirs publics; -d'une approche sp<8e>cifique des services publics de l'emploi, <88> l'image de l'action men<8e>e par le VDAB dans treize centres urbains. 4. LES FEMMES La participation des femmes au march<8e> du travail a fortement progress<8e>, parall<8f>lement <88> l<d5>am<8e>lioration de leur niveau moyen de formation. Cette progression, bienvenue, ne peut aller de pair avec une diminution de la qualit<8e> des emplois occup<8e>s par les femmes. Il faut donc veiller <88> une stricte <8e>galit<8e> de traitement entre hommes et femmes, et ce tout au long de la carri<8f>re. Les faits montrent toutefois: - que les femmes travaillent beaucoup plus <88> temps partiel que les hommes, particuli<8f>rement dans les m<8e>nages avec enfants, ce qui d<8e>montre que ce sont surtout elles qui r<8e>duisent leur activit<8e> professionnelle au profit d<d5>une meilleure combinaison entre vie professionnelle et familiale, ce qui peut entra<94>ner une <8e>volution plus lente de leur carri<8f>re, davantage de probl<8f>mes de r<8e>insertion, etc.; - que les objectifs europ<8e>ens en mati<8f>re d'accueil des enfants -les services d'accueil doivent disposer de places pour le tiers au moins des enfants de moins de trois ans <88> l'horizon 2010 - sont presque atteints, mais que les personnes peu qualifi<8e>es font moins appel aux cr<8f>ches que les personnes hautement qualifi<8e>es; -qu<d5>il subsiste une diff<8e>rence salariale au d<8e>triment des femmes, bien qu<d5>il faille reconna<94>tre que cette diff<8e>rence s<d5>est r<8e>duite en Belgique pour atteindre l<d5>un des niveaux les plus bas de l<d5>UE; -que cette diff<8e>rence est en partie (mais certainement pas exclusivement) imputable au choix des <8e>tudes qui, chez les femmes, demeure fortement orient<8e> vers certaines mati<8f>res, dans l<d5>enseignement universitaire par exemple. Pour encourager la participation des femmes sur une base <8e>galitaire, le Conseil sup<8e>rieur recommande: - un d<8e>veloppement des places d<d5>accueil pour les enfants, au profit d<d5>une offre nombreuse et bien r<8e>partie sur le territoire, en accordant une attention toute particuli<8f>re <88> l<d5>accessibilit<8e> financi<8f>re pour les familles <88> bas revenus; - un partage plus <8e>quitable des responsabilit<8e>s domestiques et parentales (acc<8f>s au cong<8e> parental, etc.); -des classifications de fonctions et des augmentations bar<8e>miques neutres du point de vue du genre; -une attention sp<8e>cifique <88> la situation des femmes issues de l<d5>immigration. 5. LES PERSONNES D<d5>ORIGINE ETRANGERE La participation des ressortissants de pays non europ<8e>ens (qui surtout <88> Bruxelles repr<8e>sentent une part importante de la population) <88> notre march<8e> du travail est particuli<8f>rement faible: leur taux d'emploi ne s'<8e>l<8f>ve qu'<88> 35 p.c., soit le niveau le plus faible dans l'UE, tandis que lcart avec le taux d'emploi des nationaux (62 p.c.) est l<d5>un des plus <8e>lev<8e>s au niveau europ<8e>en. C<d5>est surtout le taux d<d5>emploi des femmes originaires de pays non europ<8e>ens qui est particuli<8f>rement bas: il n<d5>est que de 21 p.c., contre 55 p.c. pour les femmes belges. Remarquons que les deuxi<8f>me et troisi<8f>me g<8e>n<8e>rations de migrants, bien que de nationalit<8e> belge, semblent conna<94>tre davantage de difficult<8e>s <88> s<d5>ins<8e>rer sur le march<8e> du travail que la premi<8f>re g<8e>n<8e>ration. Il convient <8e>galement de noter que la formation des ressortissants de pays non europ<8e>ens a un rendement assez faible: lcart du taux d'emploi avec les Belges est m<90>me plus important pour les personnes hautement qualifi<8e>es que pour les moins qualifi<8e>es. Selon le Conseil, une politique efficace <88> lgard de ce groupe (qui ne peut pour l<d5>heure <90>tre mesur<8e> que sur la base de la nationalit<8e>, ce qui complique quelque peu l'appr<8e>ciation de l'ensemble de la probl<8e>matique) passe par: -des efforts visant <88> favoriser l'apprentissage des langues nationales et dirig<8e>s vers les familles dans leur ensemble; - la promotion de structures d<d5>accueil pour les enfants financi<8f>rement accessibles; - la reconnaissance des comp<8e>tences acquises dans le pays d<d5>origine; -des efforts sp<8e>cifiques de la part des services publics de l<d5>emploi; -le d<8e>veloppement de plans de diversit<8e> dont il a d<8e>j<88> <8e>t<8e> question. 6. LES SENIORS La participation au march<8e> du travail diminue consid<8e>rablement chez les seniors: la part des travailleurs passe de 69 p.c. chez les 50-54 ans, <88> 44 p.c. chez les 55-59 ans et <88> 16 p.c. seulement chez les personnes <89>g<8e>es de plus de 60 ans. Bien que le taux d<d5>emploi des deux derniers groupes ait progress<8e>, gr<89>ce notamment <88> l<d5>allongement de la carri<8f>re des femmes et <88> un train de mesures limitant les possibilit<8e>s de d<8e>part anticip<8e>, de nouveaux progr<8f>s sont indispensables dans toutes les r<8e>gions, et plus particuli<8f>rement pour les femmes, les travailleurs moins qualifi<8e>s et les ressortissants de pays non europ<8e>ens. En 2006, pr<8f>s d<d5>un tiers des personnes <89>g<8e>es de 50 <88> 64 ans avaient quitt<8e> le march<8e> du travail en recourant au statut de chmeur <89>g<8e>, <88> la pr<8e>pension <88> temps plein, <88> l<d5>interruption de carri<8f>re compl<8f>te, au cr<8e>dit-temps <88> temps plein, <88> la pension ou <88> l<d5>invalidit<8e>. Des recommandations formul<8e>es pr<8e>c<8e>demment par le Conseil ont trouv<8e> un <8e>cho dans le pacte de solidarit<8e> entre les g<8e>n<8e>rations, dont les dispositions doivent <90>tre mises en <cf>uvre int<8e>gralement. Outre la politique d<d5>activation des demandeurs d<d5>emploi <89>g<8e>s dont il a d<8e>j<88> <8e>t<8e> question, le Conseil demande qu<d5>une attention particuli<8f>re soit accord<8e>e: - <88> l<d5>opportunit<8e> offerte aux partenaires sociaux par l'interdiction des augmentations salariales bar<8e>miques sur la base de lge de r<8e>examiner le processus de formation salariale sous un angle nouveau, en tenant compte par exemple de la formation, de l<d5>exp<8e>rience et de la productivit<8e>; - <88> la n<8e>cessit<8e> de promouvoir la formation et la mobilit<8e>, y compris des travailleurs <89>g<8e>s, dans une politique des ressources humaines adapt<8e>e; - <88> la n<8e>cessit<8e> de continuer <88> restreindre strictement l<d5>acc<8f>s <88> la pr<8e>pension (en pr<8e>voyant des exceptions bas<8e>es par exemple sur la p<8e>nibilit<8e> du m<8e>tier). 7. LES PERSONNES HANDICAPEES Selon les donn<8e>es d<d5>un module ad hoc de l<d5>enqu<90>te sur les forces de travail, 17 p.c. de la population en <89>ge de travailler, soit environ 1,1 million de personnes, souffraient en 2002 d'un handicap ou d'un probl<8f>me de sant<8e> chronique. Le taux d'emploi de ce groupe est tr<8f>s inf<8e>rieur <88> celui des personnes valides: 42,5 contre 64,3 p.c. Plusieurs facteurs freinent la participation des moins valides: leur <8e>tat de sant<8e> ou leur handicap, l<d5>inadaptation des offres d'emploi ou des conditions de travail, mais <8e>galement leur faible niveau moyen de formation: quelque 58 p.c. du groupe concern<8e> est faiblement qualifi<8e>, ce qui est nettement plus que chez les valides. Dans ce contexte, le Conseil pr<8e>conise diverses actions dont: -des am<8e>nagements raisonnables (<8e>ventuellement soutenus par les pouvoirs publics) aux infrastructures, aux horaires et <88> la technologie, susceptibles d'augmenter les possibilit<8e>s d'insertion des personnes handicap<8e>es; -une attention sp<8e>cifique des services publics de l<d5>emploi, pour aider ces personnes <88> trouver un emploi adapt<8e>.

Title: Central banks and financial stability
text: Opening session of the Conference of the International Cooperative and Mutual Insurance Federation Brussels, 26 September 2007 "Central banks and financial stability" Presentation by Guy QUADEN, Governor of the National Bank of Belgium If there is one concept that is directly associated with the central banking function, it is that of stability. This objective of stability applies first and foremost to prices. By curbing inflation, central banks can preserve the value and purchasing power of the means of payment they create. More broadly, monetary stability helps to maintain a more steady rate of growth in economic activity. The price system can then fully fulfil its anchor to guide the multiple decisions of economic agents. Price stability also eliminates a major source of disruption in financial markets by reducing the uncertainties created by unanticipated fluctuations in inflation. Financial stability thus appears to be very directly linked to monetary stability. The internationalization of financial activities, the globalization of markets and, above all, the increasing diversification and sophistication of risk management products and techniques have profoundly changed the functioning of financial markets, leading central banks to reconsider and rethink their contribution to financial stability. The central banks directly responsible for the individual supervision of credit institutions have adjusted the way in which their micro-prudential supervision is carried out and those which, like the National Bank of Belgium, do not carry out this task, have also had to adapt, both by reconsidering their relationship with the supervisory bodies and by redefining their specific financial stability. The concept of macro-prudential supervision has thus emerged as an important new focus of central bank activity. The term macro clearly implies that what is intended is, beyond the situation of individual institutions, the overall stability of the financial system. Indeed, the two do not necessarily go hand in hand. One of the main implications of the globalization of the financial system is that market operators are reacting much faster than in the past to common sources of information. This increases the risk of widespread behaviours which, even if justified at an individual level, can generate systemic problems if adopted simultaneously by a large number of institutions. In this new context, there is a growing need to complement micro-prudential supervision with macro-prudential analysis. Stability, it must be stressed, is obviously not synonymous with immobility. Financial institutions are evolving and must constantly adapt to both competitive pressures and abrupt changes in the macroeconomic environment. The challenge is precisely to let market mechanisms operate while preventing malfunctions in the financial system that would have repercussions on the economy as a whole. The pursuit of this objective requires a threefold action: prevention, surveillance and crisis management, which I would like to briefly explain. 1. PREVENTION In the field of prevention, enormous resources have been invested by national and international authorities in recent years. These efforts have focused on defining and developing rules or standards to improve the functioning of institutions, markets and infrastructure essential for the proper functioning of the financial system. I would just like to highlight the main principles that have prevailed in this area. The first is the move towards a more multinational approach. The opening up of financial markets and systems goes hand in hand with an increased need for harmonisation. This is particularly felt at European Union level. The Commission has thus implemented its Financial Services Action Plan, which brings together no less than 42 major measures to complete the integration of financial markets. At the level of the Group of 10 countries, the Basel Committee on Counterbanking has developed, in close consultation with the financial sector, its revised framework for international convergence on capital requirements. This major text serves as an inspiration for the development of solvency requirements for insurance companies, the famous Solvency II Directive, which is certainly well known to the participants in this conference. A second characteristic is that preventive measures are becoming more flexible, more protean. It is becoming increasingly clear that, in the face of ever-changing markets, a body of binding legal texts is not enough. To use Anglo-Saxon terminology, "hard laws" must be supplemented both by "soft laws" in the form of recommendations and general principles but also by the use of market discipline. Market discipline is not a recent concept. What is more new is the highlighting of this essential facet for safeguarding financial stability in certain regulations. For example, the Basel Committee structured the New Capital Adequacy Agreement around three pillars. A ce of quantitative capital requirements  the first pillar  and the consideration of the individual risk profile of each bank through prudential supervision  the second pillar  the Committee has provided for a third pillar concerning the nature of the information to be published by the institutions to ensure the proper functioning of this market discipline. The Solvency II Insurance Directive explicitly incorporates this three-pillar architecture. Finally, a final factor must be highlighted is that of the variety of areas taken into account by prevention. Good prevention obviously requires the application of accounting standards and ratios aimed at preserving the solvency of financial institutions. However, it must also be based on an appropriate corporate governance structure and the use of appropriate procedures and techniques for risk management. This arsenal, designed to ensure stability, must be combined with measures to increase the efficiency of the financial system, preserving a good competitive environment and ensuring consumer protection. 2. SURVEILLANCE The second main line of action is that of surveillance. The best rules and prevention measures will never be an absolute guarantee. Preventive measures must be complemented by a good monitoring structure to detect warning signs of vulnerability. At this level, supervisory authorities and central banks each have their own specific role to play. The former seek above all to avoid the failures of individual institutions, with the ultimate aim of ensuring consumer protection. Central banks aim to supplement this counter with a system-wide surveillance to prevent a global crisis of a systemic nature from disrupting economic activity. These systemic problems may be related to the weakening of a large customer segment, which requires attention to major macroeconomic developments. They can also result from the breakdown of infrastructures that provide essential connections between financial institutions or be the consequence of failures in certain financial markets when a large number of participants simultaneously seek to liquidate their positions. These few examples testify to the need for a broad approach covering the entire financial sector. While the situation of banks requires special monitoring, supervision must also cover securities markets, payment and settlement infrastructures and also other financial institutions, in particular insurance companies. They are indeed major players in the financial markets. Because of the structure of their activities and their investment portfolio, insurance companies favour a long-term approach that generally exerts a stabilizing re-engagement on the financial markets. However, if the sector were to face systemic problems, this would have a direct impact on the operating conditions and liquidity of these markets, with inevitable repercussions on other operators, in particular banks. 3. CRISIS MANAGEMENT The combination of good preventive measures and an effective surveillance system will never prevent any crisis. If the soundness of the financial system must remain very strong at all times, it must be associated with good efficiency. For this objective to be achieved, financial markets must remain largely open to competition, which is an essential factor in innovation. In this context, the occurrence of an accident therefore remains possible and is not to be considered, in itself, as a sign of failure in the exercise of prudential supervision. In the event of tensions in the financial markets, the priority of central banks is to ensure that the stability of the whole system is maintained and to minimise the negative impact that these tensions could have on economic activity. This includes ensuring a good flow of liquidity within the system, a very topical problem in a context of uncertainty and the loss of confidence have resulted in the functioning of the entire money market. The undervaluation of various risks for some time called for correction. "Repricing", as is often the case, has occurred in a rather brutal and chaotic manner with possible negative consequences for all financial institutions, non-financial companies and the economy. It is not to rescue reckless operators but to limit this collateral damage as much as possible that the European Central Bank and other central banks have intervened in the way we know. I would add that it is always essential to maintain the distinction between liquidity problem and solvency problem. In the latter case, it is imperative to focus on solutions from the private sector. This requires the responsibility of management and the assumption of losses by shareholders. The use of public funds to solve a financial crisis can only be considered as one as the ultimate solution, to be implemented exclusively to avoid a major dysfunction within the economy. Finally, I would like to stress that possible financial crises should increasingly comply with the classic scenario for a country's authorities to deal with the failure of one of their resident institutions. The financial system has become integrated so that problems quickly acquire a cross-border dimension. This may take the form of a breakdown of key infrastructures for the proper functioning of the payment or securities settlement system, the emergence of serious difficulties within a financial group present in many different countries or, as today, the malfunctioning of major financial market segments. In such situations, coordination problems and operational issues quickly come to the fore. Central banks and supervisors are aware of this and are preparing for it by organising internationally coordinated simulation and stress test exercises. CONCLUSION As I quickly tried to show, safeguarding financial stability must combine a long-term vision in the design of preventive measures, rigour in supervision and cold blood in crisis management. This safeguard is a common objective of the authorities and market operators that can only be achieved by combining the efforts and experiences of each other. That is why I thank you for your invitation and wish you fruitful work.

Le concept de surveillance macro prudentielle a ainsi <8e>merg<8e> comme un nouvel axe important de l'activit<8e> des banques centrales. Dans ce nouveau contexte, un besoin croissant se fait jour de compl<8e>ter la surveillance micro prudentielle par une analyse macro prudentielle. Stabilit<8e>, il faut le souligner, n'est <8e>videmment pas synonyme d'immobilit<8e>.
