Le d<8e>fi est pr<8e>cis<8e>ment de laisser jouer les m<8e>canismes de march<8e> tout en emp<90>chant des dysfonctionnements du syst<8f>me financier qui se r<8e>percuteraient sur l'ensemble de l'<8e>conomie. La poursuite de cet objectif requiert une triple action: pr<8e>vention, surveillance et gestion des crises que je voudrais bri<8f>vement expliciter. 1. PR<83>VENTION Dans le domaine de la pr<8e>vention, d'<8e>normes ressources ont <8e>t<8e> investies par les autorit<8e>s nationales et internationales au cours de ces derniers ann<8e>es. Ces efforts ont port<8e> sur la d<8e>finition et l'<8e>laboration de r<8f>gles ou de standards visant <88> am<8e>liorer le fonctionnement des institutions, march<8e>s et infrastructures essentielles pour le bon fonctionnement du syst<8f>me financier. Je voudrais juste mettre en exergue les grands principes qui ont pr<8e>sid<8e> en cette mati<8f>re. Le premier est le mouvement vers une approche davantage multinationale. L'ouverture des march<8e>s et syst<8f>mes financiers va de pair avec un besoin accru d'harmonisation. Celui-ci se fait particuli<8f>rement sentir au niveau de l'Union europ<8e>enne. La Commission a ainsi mis en <cf>uvre son Plan d'action pour les services financiers, regroupant pas moins de 42 grandes mesures destin<8e>es <88> parachever l'int<8e>gration des march<8e>s financiers. Au niveau des pays du groupe des 10, le Comit<8e> de B<89>le sur le contre bancaire a con<8d>u, en <8e>troite concertation avec le secteur financier, son cadre r<8e>vis<8e> de convergence internationale en mati<8f>re de normes de fonds propres. Ce texte majeur sert d'inspiration pour la mise au point des exigences de solvabilit<8e> pour les compagnies d'assurances, la fameuse directive Solvency II, certainement bien connue des participants <88> cette conf<8e>rence. Une deuxi<8f>me caract<8e>ristique est que les mesures de pr<8e>vention deviennent plus souples, davantage prot<8e>iformes. Il appara<94>t de plus en plus <8e>vident que, face <88> des march<8e>s en perp<8e>tuel changement, un corpus de textes l<8e>gaux contraignants ne suffit pas. Pour reprendre la terminologie anglo-saxonne, les "hard laws" doivent <90>tre compl<8e>t<8e>es <88> la fois par des "soft laws" sous la forme de recommandations et de principes g<8e>n<8e>raux mais aussi par le recours <88> la discipline de march<8e>. La discipline de march<8e> n'est pas une notion r<8e>cente. Ce qui est plus nouveau est la mise en <8e>vidence de cette facette essentielle pour la sauvegarde de la stabilit<8e> financi<8f>re dans certaines r<8f>glementations. Ainsi, le Comit<8e> de B<89>le a structur<8e> le Nouvel Accord sur les fonds propres autour de trois piliers. A c<8e> de normes de fonds propres quantitatives <d0> le premier pilier <d0> et de la prise en compte du profil de risque individuel de chaque banque via la surveillance prudentielle <d0> le deuxi<8f>me pilier <d0> le Comit<8e> a pr<8e>vu un troisi<8f>me pilier concernant la nature des informations <88> publier par les institutions pour assurer le bon fonctionnement de cette discipline de march<8e>. La directive Solvency II pour les assurances reprend explicitement cette architecture en trois piliers. Un dernier facteur doit enfin <90>tre mis en exergue, c'est celui de la vari<8e>t<8e> des domaines pris en compte par la pr<8e>vention. Une bonne pr<8e>vention passe <8e>videmment par l'application de normes et de ratios comptables visant <88> pr<8e>server la solvabilit<8e> des institutions financi<8f>res. Elle doit cependant aussi s'appuyer sur une structure adapt<8e>e en mati<8f>re de gouvernance d'entreprise ainsi que sur l'utilisation de proc<8e>dures et techniques ad<8e>quates pour la gestion des risques. Cet arsenal, destin<8e> <88> assurer la stabilit<8e>, doit se combiner <88> des mesures visant <88> accro<94>tre l'efficacit<8e> du syst<8f>me financier, en pr<8e>servant de bonnes conditions de concurrence et en assurant la protection du consommateur. 2. SURVEILLANCE Le second grand axe d'action est celui de la surveillance. Les meilleures r<8f>gles et dispositifs de pr<8e>vention ne constitueront jamais une garantie absolue. Les mesures de pr<8e>vention doivent <90>tre compl<8e>t<8e>es par une bonne structure de surveillance visant <88> d<8e>tecter les signes avant-coureurs de vuln<8e>rabilit<8e>. A ce niveau les autorit<8e>s de supervision et les banques centrales ont chacunes leur re sp<8e>cifique <88> jouer. Les premi<8f>res cherchent avant tout <88> <8e>viter les d<8e>faillances d'institutions individuelles, dans l'objectif ultime d'assurer la protection des consommateurs. Les banques centrales visent <88> compl<8e>ter ce contre par une surveillance <8e>tendue <88> l'ensemble du syst<8f>me afin d'<8e>viter qu'une crise globale, de nature syst<8e>mique, ne perturbe l'activit<8e> <8e>conomique. Ces probl<8f>mes de nature syst<8e>mique peuvent <90>tre li<8e>s <88> la fragilisation d'un large segment de la client<8f>le, ce qui exige d'<90>tre attentif aux grandes <8e>volutions macro <8e>conomiques. Ils peuvent aussi r<8e>sulter de la rupture d'infrastructures qui assurent des connections essentielles entre institutions financi<8f>res ou encore <90>tre la cons<8e>quence de d<8e>faillances de certains march<8e>s financiers lorsque un grand nombre d'intervenants cherchent simultan<8e>ment <88> liquider leurs positions. Ces quelques exemples t<8e>moignent de la n<8e>cessit<8e> d'une approche large couvrant l'ensemble du secteur financier. Si la situation des banques requiert un suivi tout particulier, la surveillance doit aussi porter sur les march<8e>s de titres, les infrastructures de paiement et de r<8f>glement et, <8e>galement, les autres institutions financi<8f>res, en particulier les compagnies d'assurances. Celles-ci sont en effet des acteurs majeurs sur les march<8e>s financiers. De par la structure de leurs activit<8e>s et de leur portefeuille de placement, les compagnies d'assurances privil<8e>gient une approche <88> long terme qui exerce un re g<8e>n<8e>ralement stabilisateur sur les march<8e>s financiers. Mais, si le secteur devait faire face <88> des probl<8f>mes d'ordre syst<8e>mique, ceci se r<8e>percuterait directement sur les conditions de fonctionnement et la liquidit<8e> de ces march<8e>s avec des r<8e>percussions in<8e>vitables sur les autres op<8e>rateurs et notamment les banques. 3. GESTION DE CRISE La combinaison de bonnes mesures de pr<8e>vention et d'un syst<8f>me efficace de surveillance ne permettra jamais d'<8e>viter toute crise. Si la solidit<8e> du syst<8f>me financier doit rester, en tout temps, tr<8f>s forte, celle-ci doit <90>tre associ<8e>e <88> une bonne efficacit<8e>. Pour que cet objectif soit atteint, il faut que les march<8e>s financiers restent largement ouverts <88> la concurrence, facteur essentiel d'innovation. Dans ce contexte, la survenance d'un accident reste donc possible et n'est pas <88> consid<8e>rer, en soi, comme une marque d'<8e>chec dans l'exercice de la surveillance prudentielle. En cas de tensions sur les march<8e>s financiers la priorit<8e> des banques centrales est d'assurer le maintien de la stabilit<8e> de l'ensemble du syst<8f>me et de minimiser l'impact n<8e>gatif que ces tensions pourraient exercer sur l'activit<8e> <8e>conomique. Il s'agit notamment d'assurer une bonne circulation de la liquidit<8e> au sein du syst<8f>me, un probl<8f>me de grande actualit<8e> dans un contexte ol'incertitude et la perte de confiance ont eu pour r<8e>sultat de gripper le fonctionnement de l'ensemble du march<8e> mon<8e>taire. La sous-<8e>valuation depuis un certain temps de divers risques appelait une correction. Le "repricing", comme c'est souvent le cas, s'est produit de mani<8f>re assez brutale et chaotique avec de possibles cons<8e>quences n<8e>gatives pour l'ensemble des institutions financi<8f>res, des entreprises non financi<8f>res et de l'<8e>conomie. Ce n'est pas pour voler au secours d'op<8e>rateurs imprudents mais pour limiter au maximum ces dommages collat<8e>raux que la Banque centrale europ<8e>enne et d'autres banques centrales sont intervenues de la fa<8d>on que l'on sait. J'ajoute qu'il est toujours essentiel de maintenir la distinction entre probl<8f>me de liquidit<8e> et probl<8f>me de solvabilit<8e>. Dans ce dernier cas il est imp<8e>ratif de privil<8e>gier les solutions venant du secteur priv<8e>. Ceci passe par la responsabilisation du management et la prise en charge des pertes par les actionnaires. L'utilisation des fonds publics pour r<8e>soudre une crise financi<8f>re ne peut <90>tre envisag<8e>e que une comme solution ultime, <88> mettre exclusivement en <cf>uvre pour <8e>viter un disfonctionnement majeur au sein de l'<8e>conomie. Je voudrais enfin insister sur le point que d'<8e>ventuelles crises financi<8f>res devraient de moins en moins se conformer au sc<8e>nario classique oles autorit<8e>s d'un pays doivent faire face <88> la d<8e>faillance d'un de leurs <8e>tablissements r<8e>sidents. Le syst<8f>me financier est devenu int<8e>gr<8e> de sorte que les probl<8f>mes acqui<8f>rent rapidement une dimension transfrontali<8f>re. Ceci pourra se mat<8e>rialiser par une rupture d'infrastructures cl<8e>s pour le bon fonctionnement du syst<8f>me de paiement ou de r<8f>glement titre, par l'<8e>mergence de graves difficult<8e>s au sein d'un groupe financier pr<8e>sent dans de nombreux pays diff<8e>rents ou encore, comme aujourd'hui, par le disfonctionnement de compartiments majeurs des march<8e>s financiers. Dans de telles situations, les probl<8f>mes de coordination et les questions op<8e>rationnelles viennent rapidement <88> l'avant-plan. Les banques centrales et les autorit<8e>s prudentielles en sont conscientes et s'y pr<8e>parent, par l'organisation d'exercices de simulation et de stress tests coordonn<8e>s au niveau international. CONCLUSION Comme j'ai rapidement cherch<8e> <88> le montrer, la sauvegarde de la stabilit<8e> financi<8f>re doit associer vision <88> long terme dans la conception des mesures de pr<8e>vention, rigueur dans la surveillance et sang froid dans la gestion de crise. Cette sauvegarde est un objectif commun aux autorit<8e>s et aux op<8e>rateurs de march<8e> qui ne peut <90>tre atteint qu'en combinant les efforts et exp<8e>riences des uns et des autres. C'est pourquoi je vous remercie de votre invitation et vous souhaite de fructueux travaux.

Title: Annual Meetings of the World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund
text: Annual Meetings of the World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund Guy Quaden, Governor of the Fund for Belgium Washington, October 23 First of all, I wish to thank Rodrigo de Rato for his inspired leadership. I would also like to welcome Robert Zoellick as President of the World Bank and Dominique Strauss-Kahn as Managing Director of the Fund. The IMF faces a number of important challenges. I will talk about three of those challenges: The first challenge is no doubt the most delicate one. The Fund has to find a way to connect with the new realities of a changed global environment. All members have a right to a fair and adequate representation in the IMF. I recognise that the current distribution of quotas and voting rights does not reflect the shifts in the global economy which have taken place over the last decades; therefore the calls for change are justified. Discussions over the past 13 months have shown that it is not easy to find a comprehensive solution. The often complicated technical details of the issue should not obscure the ultimate objective: a shift of actual quota shares to dynamic economies, while preserving and preferably enhancing the voting power of low income countries. For those who might have doubts : my country and I are fully committed to this objective. Although a compromise has not yet been reached, I feel a lot of progress has been made and a solution is within reach. Developing a new income and expenditure model is the second major challenge the IMF is facing. The Fund cannot continue to rely solely on the revenue generated by its lending activities. The report of the Committee of eminent persons represents an excellent basis for developing a new income model, broadening the Fundd4s income base in correspondence with the multiple tasks of the Fund. We should however not limit this exercise to the income side, but also look at the Fundd4s expenditures, based on an analysis of what we view as the Fundd4s strategic priorities. The Fund must establish a costing framework, enabling it to calculate precisely the cost of the different elements of its mission. This will allow us, shareholders, to clearly indicate in what areas expenditures should be reduced. The third challenge I want to mention here, is the need for the Fund to enhance the effectiveness of its surveillance. A candid but even-handed exercise of surveillance is crucial for the relevance and legitimacy of the Fund. With its recent decisions, the Executive Board has created the framework for a more focused and effective bilateral surveillance. The Fund should also design a similar framework to govern its multilateral surveillance. Like the IMF, the World Bank Group is facing important challenges, particularly in defining the strategic directions for the coming years. In my view fair governance and anti-corruption principles must maintain a central place in the work of the World Bank Group. I share President Zoellickd4s Vision on the Bankd4s objectives to work towards an inclusive and sustainable globalisation. Tackling poverty remains the major strategic objective. Sub-Saharan Africa remains the region with the biggest needs and the most challenging environment to reduce poverty. In this context I would like to emphasize the important role of IDA as the premier development agency. Belgium supports a substantial IDA15 replenishment, which is crucial for our effort to reach the MDGs, re.emphasizing IDAd4s prominent role within the complex aid architecture. The World Bank Group will also need to redefine its role in middle income countries, taking into account their specific needs. The World Bank Groupd4s institutions need to formulate and implement joint strategies to assist this group of countries in realizing inclusive and sustainable growth with a particular emphasis on the poorest segments of society. The Bankd4s active role regarding further integrating the regional and global public goods should be reinforced with the objective of demonstrating to individual countries that investments in these areas are in their own interest. The triple objective of the Bankd4s energy policy remains more then ever important: providing low income countries with sufficient energy for growth, the transition to a low carbon environment and adapting to climate change. The Bankd4s current business model is well adapted to face all those challenges. I can assure you, Mr. President, of my full cooperation in your important mission. Thank you for your attention.

Title: Hearing of the Governor before the Finance and Budget Committee - Presentation
text: Hearing of the Governor before the Finance and Budget Committee - 19 March 2008 Presentation Before turning to the specific subject of this hearing, the application of the notional interest regime by the Bank, I think it is useful to briefly remind you of the tasks that the Bank fulfils, what is its special status and the way in which it generates and distributes its income. The National Bank of Belgium is the central bank of our country. Historically, central banks have exercised crucial control over monetary policy and financial stability. Even after joining the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem, the Bank continues to play an important role. Above all, it should be stressed that the Governor of the Bank sits on the Governing Council of the ECB, where the principle of "one person, one vote" is required, and therefore actively participates in the definition of monetary policy. The Bank's staff assists him in this task. Moreover, the Eurosystem is characterised by a high degree of operational decentralisation: almost all of its tasks are carried out by the national central banks. This is particularly the case with the introduction of banknotes, the implementation of monetary policy (in particular through the operational management of offers introduced by Belgian banks in the ECB's tendering procedures), the holding of monetary reserves constituted by credit institutions and the management of foreign exchange reserves (in gold and foreign currencies, including foreign exchange reserves that have been transferred to the ECB). In addition to those entrusted to it within the framework of the Eurosystem, the National Bank carries out various other tasks of general interest. First, it contributes to the stability of the financial system (macroprudential supervision, crisis prevention and management). The Governor of the Bank chairs the Financial Stability Committee, which brings together the members of the Bank's Management Committees and the Banking, Finance and Insurance Commission. The Financial Stability Committee is responsible for all matters of common interest to both institutions, including the stability of the financial system as a whole and the coordination of crisis management. The Bank also manages belgium's main interbank payment systems and a securities settlement system. It also manages the Central Balance Sheets, the Central Corporate Credit And the Personal Credit Central and collects and processes a significant amount of economic and financial statistics. The Bank has a high-quality printing plant, acts as a State Cashier and manages the Annuity Fund. Moreover, it is a centre of first-rate knowledge in the fields of economic research and analysis and its publications are authoritative. It is undeniable that the Bank's essential resources in all these areas contribute to strengthening the financial and economic image of Brussels and Belgium, which also benefits employment - for example at the level of the various international financial operators established in Belgium (such as Euroclear). Having briefly reviewed the Bank's missions and activities, I would now like to draw your attention to its legal structure. The Bank was established by a law of 1850 in the form of a public limited company. Its shares have also been listed on the stock exchange. However, it became clear from the outset that, in view of the importance of its tasks as a central bank, it could not be regarded as an ordinary commercial company. The legislator therefore provided the Bank with a special legal framework and its own bodies, entrusting only limited liability to the general meeting of shareholders. The organs of the Bank, namely - in addition to the Governor - the Management Committee, the Regency Council and the College of Censors, have their own composition, defined by law, and exercise the specific powers entrusted to them by the legislator. 2. The Regency Council shall exchange views on general questions relating to the Bank, monetary policy and the national and international economic situation. In addition, it plays a key role in the appointment of directors, remuneration and supervision. It is also responsible for approving the amount of the dividend and approving the annual accounts, which is equivalent to discharge for the members of the Management Committee. The composition of the Regency Council, which exercises some of the reserved powers in ordinary companies, both on the board of directors and at the general meeting of shareholders, is designed in such a way as to establish a fair representation of the various Belgian socio-economic interests. While, in the post-World War II period, many central banks were nationalized in Europe, the Belgian legislature opted for an intermediate solution, in which the Belgian state became the owner of half of the shares and the other half remained in the hands of the private sector. As a result, the Bank has a different structure from that of most other central banks in neighbouring countries. Nevertheless, it has always ensured respect for the rights of the sovereign State, which has a privileged relationship with its central bank, as well as with its shareholders, whether private shareholders or the State as the majority shareholder. In order to comment in more detail on these aspects, it is useful to briefly explain how the Bank generates and distributes its revenues. You will note that the sovereign state occupies a preponderant place in this context and that equality between shareholders is always respected. The issuance of banknotes (formerly in Belgian francs, now in euros) is one of the main tasks of the National Bank of Belgium. This privilege was conferred on him by the State. From an accounting point of view, the notes are recorded as debts on the Liabilities side of the Bank's balance sheet. These debts are not remunerated. In return for the notes it has issued, the Bank holds assets that are largely contributed by commercial banks in exchange for the notes they withdraw. The assets and receivables thus acquired by the Bank shall be shown as assets on its balance sheet and shall be interest-bearing. As the Bank issues notes, it generates revenue, which is referred to as "seigniorage." This seigniorage is in fact the responsibility of the community since it is a direct result of the broadcasting privilege. In all the countries of the world, there are therefore rules for sharing seigniorage between the State, which has the right to mint money, and the central bank, which ensures the issuance of money: part of the seigniorage is left to the central bank to cover its operating costs and guarantee its financial soundness. The rest is allocated to the state. At the National Bank of Belgium, this distribution mechanism is essentially defined in Articles 29 and 32 of the Organic Law. Article 29 lays down the so-called 3 p.c. rule. In accordance with that directive, the National Bank of Belgium retains, to cover its operating costs and the remuneration of its capital, the first 3 p.c. of the proceeds of the net profitable assets it generates in the context of its issuing activity. The surplus goes to the state. Thus, for the financial year 2007, an amount of EUR 152.7 million was paid to the State. As with all companies, an imp is levied on the result. For the financial year 2007, the tax amounted to EUR 103 million. The deduction of notional interest was taken into account when calculating the corporation tax. Then, the profits are distributed, in accordance with the provisions of Article 32 of the Organic Law of the Bank. Under this article, the sovereign State is given priority to one fifth of the profit after the allocation of a first dividend to the shareholders and amounts, fixed by law, to the reserves and the staff. For the 2007 financial year, the State's priority share of the Bank's profits amounted to db46 million. In addition, all shareholders receive an annual dividend. The dividend paid to shareholders is db72 gross for 2007, which represents a revenue of db14.4 million (i.e. 200,000 shares multiplied by db72) for the State shareholder. 3. You will notice that the National Bank of Belgium is a special institution that pursues objectives of general interest and takes into account all stakeholders. Unfortunately, some of its minority shareholders have been trying for five years to question these principles. They ignore its specificity and argue, wrongly, that it would not properly distribute its profits. Several legal actions have even been filed. For the time being, the courts have always ruled in favour of the Bank. In various judgments already rendered, the court insists on the special character of the Bank because of its status as a central bank, and on the fact that it has always respected the rules to which it is subject and properly distributed its profits. By way of example, I would like to quote an extract from the judgment delivered on 9 March 2007 by the Commercial Court, in which the judge confirms that the Bank correctly applied the law when transferring to the State the capital gains realized on gold, "[ ]the Court observes that there can be no fault, let alone liability, to comply with the law and comply with its requirements; that, by respecting the will of the legislator, the BNB behaved as a normally diligent banking organization". I believe that this also applies to the Bank's application of the rules on the deduction of notional interest. It is true that the National Bank of Belgium has been using the notional interest deduction regime since 2006. For the 2007 financial year, it estimates the resulting tax savings at EUR 17 million. The SNB falls within the scope of the Act of 22 June 2005 introducing a tax deduction for risk capital. As you know, the deduction of notional interest applies to all companies, with the exception of those that already benefit from an exorbitant tax regime under ordinary law. text: GENERAL ASSEMBLY 2008 INTRODUCTORY STATEMENT BY THE GOVERNOR Ladies and Gentlemen, I welcome you, on my own behalf and on behalf of the other members of the Management Committee, to this ordinary general meeting of shareholders of the National Bank of Belgium. As is tradition, I would like to briefly mention the most significant events of the year under review, before giving the floor to the Deputy Governor who will present and comment on the annual accounts for the financial year 2007. This afternoon, we will answer your questions. Several major projects marked the year 2007. They were highlighted in the Corporate Report, which has been profoundly revised. You will no doubt have noticed that. Its first part, which was traditionally devoted to describing all of the Bank's activities, has given way to a more selective and concise presentation of the main achievements of the past year. These are, for the most part, the advances made in the field of payment and securities liquidation systems, the internationalization of some of our IT applications and the modernization of the Central Balance Sheet. Several of these projects are part of the process of establishing a new organisation of work between the Eurosystem central banks, characterised by increased collaboration between the institutions. The Bank, in the person of its Governor, actively participates in the definition of the Eurosystem's monetary policy. It is also responsible for implementing it on the national territory in its relations with other financial institutions The functioning of the Eurosystem, which today involves the ECB and the 15 national central banks, is, as we know, highly decentralised. However, there is an increasing number of central banks partnering to provide services to other members or to the system. This evolution saves money by working together on important projects. The Bank is playing a very active role in this movement: it is in particular the instigator of several large-scale IT projects. I will cite two examples among others, which demonstrate its know-how and the recognition of the Bank's competences by its Eurosystem partners. The first example concerns the management of fiat money. Responsible for the introduction of coins and banknotes in Belgium, the Bank has developed, on the occasion of the introduction of the euro, a computer application that makes it possible to manage banknote flows more effectively and efficiently. Thanks to this application called "Cash", the deliveries and withdrawals of banknotes by banks and cash carriers, which are carried out in the form of secure parcels, are announced in advance electronically and, at the end of the operations, the communication of data, the recording of payments and invoicing are carried out automatically. The success of this application has led the Nederlandsche Bank, the Banque centrale du Luxembourg and the Bank of Finland to enter into a partnership with the Bank to jointly manage this application and consequently achieve economies of scale that benefit all users. The second example relates to the implementation of European monetary policy. In order to manage the guarantees linked to the granting of loans to banks more effectively, the SNB has developed a new IT application in partnership with the Nederlandsche Bank. This platform, called "Euro Collateral management system", makes it possible to manage these guarantees in a largely automated way and thus improve the efficiency of this 2. management and services provided to credit institutions. The advantages offered by this platform have aroused the interest of other central banks. Other projects concern the collection and exchange of data. All this demonstrates the Bank's willingness to participate actively in all forms of collaboration and to become an important service provider for the Eurosystem. * * * Legal and financial information obviously remains at the heart of the corporate report. The main facts relating to the Governance of the Bank as well as all the information relating to its financial situation are the subject of important chapters whose presentation has also been improved. For greater clarity, the various accounting rules have been grouped according to their origin: those imposed by the European System of Central Banks, those resulting from the Organic Law and the Statute of the Bank or the conventions to which it is a party, and those enacted by the Regency Council. The financial information is preceded by the annual report, which includes the most important changes in the result and describes the main risks facing the Bank and how it manages them. As the 2007 report demonstrates, we strive to provide the best possible information. The presentation of the corporate report will continue to evolve to give all the information they are entitled to expect on the Bank's activities and results. It is also on the basis of this report that we will answer your questions concerning the 2007 accounting year. I now give the floor to the Deputy Governor, who will present to you in detail the annual accounts for the financial year 2007. As usual, a question-and-answer session will take place after lunch. I would like to thank the shareholders who sent us their questions in advance, thus facilitating the preparation and smooth running of this meeting. Thank you for your attention.

Pour g<8e>rer plus efficacement les garanties qui sont li<8e>es <88> l'octroi des cr<8e>dits accord<8e>s aux banques, la Banque nationale a d<8e>velopp<8e> une nouvelle application informatique en partenariat avec la Nederlandsche Bank. Tout cela t<8e>moigne de la volont<8e> de la Banque de participer activement <88> toutes les formes de collaboration qui se mettent en place et de devenir un prestataire de services important pour l'Eurosyst<8f>me. * * * Les informations juridiques et financi<8f>res restent bien <8e>videmment au c<cf>ur du rapport d'entreprise. Les principaux faits touchant <88> la gouvernance de la Banque ainsi que l'ensemble des informations relatives <88> sa situation financi<8f>re font l'objet de chapitres importants dont la pr<8e>sentation a <8e>galement <8e>t<8e> am<8e>lior<8e>e. Pour plus de clart<8e>, on a regroup<8e> les diff<8e>rentes r<8f>gles comptables selon leur origine: celles qui sont impos<8e>es par le Syst<8f>me europ<8e>en de banques centrales, celles qui d<8e>coulent de la loi organique et des statuts de la Banque ou des conventions auxquelles elle est partie, et celles qui ont <8e>t<8e> <8e>dict<8e>es par le Conseil de r<8e>gence. L'information financi<8f>re est pr<8e>c<8e>d<8e>e du rapport de gestion, qui reprend notamment les <8e>volutions les plus importantes du r<8e>sultat et qui d<8e>crit les principaux risques auxquels la Banque est confront<8e>e et la mani<8f>re dont elle les g<8f>re. Comme le rapport 2007 en t<8e>moigne, nous nous effor<8d>ons d'offrir la meilleure information possible. La pr<8e>sentation du rapport d'entreprise continuera <88> <8e>voluer pour donner <88> tous les informations qu'ils sont en droit d'attendre sur les activit<8e>s et les r<8e>sultats de la Banque. C'est <8e>galement sur la base de ce rapport que nous r<8e>pondrons <88> vos questions concernant l'exercice comptable 2007. Je c<8f>de maintenant la parole au vice-gouverneur, qui va vous pr<8e>senter en d<8e>tail les comptes annuels de l'exercice 2007. Je vous remercie de votre attention.

Title: BUILDING FORUM
text: CONSTRUCTION FORUM (26 February 2009) Speech by Jan Smets I have been following the economy for a long time, but never have I seen the economic outlook deteriorate as quickly as in recent months. You know: the financial crisis has infected the real economy internationally, and that has happened and is happening even further through 3 channels: - banks' capital bases have been affected by losses and value adjustments, and this may make banks more cautious in lending, a move that is counterbalanced by the recapitalisations in which the government plays its full role but which may make investing more difficult; - the fall in share prices affects the wealth of households, who may wish to restore that wealth by saving more and thus spending less; -consumer and business confidence has fallen to record lows, weighing on consumption and investment. Moreover, unlike many previous crises, this one is indisputably global. The US mortgage problems have spread all over the world through their packaging and resale, and their economic problems have also affected the whole world: for 2009 we expect only 0.5 % world growth, compared to 3.4 % last year and even around 5 % in previous years, and many countries are in recession. It goes without saying that the Belgian economy does not escape this. First of all because we our international banking system, which is also quite developed internationally, we have been heavily influenced by the financial crisis, but also because, as a small open economy, we are also severely affected by the international drop in demand. According to our latest forecasts, on which the government has also supported, our economy is expected to decline by 1.9 % this year, and the construction sector will certainly also be affected - although his situation is certainly much less unfavourable than, for example, in Spain and Ireland, where he and with him the economy suffers from the bursting of a real bubble in the real estate market. The job of forecaster is very difficult today because, when it comes to the current crisis, the references of the past are lacking. We are not in depression as in the early thirties, thanks in particular to the actions of central banks and governments, but we also have no clear view of the timing of the recovery - which, t or later, will happen. Business confidence has fallen to a very low level, and you've probably learned that it has fallen again this month. And the current crisis is above all a crisis of confidence, the restoration of which is an indispensable condition for recovery. It is true that this decline in confidence has been less significant in civil engineering, but the latest figure also indicates a deterioration. Fortunately, central banks, governments and the social partners are currently making every effort to stabilise the economy. First, by stabilizing the financial system: central banks through liquidity injections, governments by granting guarantees or intervening in banks' capital. Subsequently, in order to counter the economic slowdown, central banks cut interest rates, governments set up stimulus packages, which should ideally respond to the three "T's": timely - which means that the measures must be likely to fuel spending now -, targeted - that is to say oriented towards the most promising segments - and temporary - that is to say, by avoiding a structural burden on our public finances. In this context, the authorities have taken measures to reduce charges and make payment facilities available to businesses, but they have rightly paid particular attention to construction, for example by temporarily reducing VAT and encouraging infrastructure works, both at federal and regional level. 2. I believe that this kind of effort is very much in line with what I would recommend. Why? Because it seems very important to me - and with me, the NBB and many international institutions - to place government action in a double perspective. One: it must help stabilise the economy, and that means that the government, especially now, must partly take over the spending from the private sector and families, and thus, as it were, lay a floor under the demand. Our social security system contributes very well to this, but it is good that the government is making an extra effort. But two: the government must also contribute to ensuring that our economy is well prepared for the exit from the crisis. This means, for example, that we take good care of the first victims of the crisis - the unemployed - but also that we do not let them go too early, but that we retain, train and guide them, so that they can be put back into a labour market that is becoming tendentiously tighter after the crisis. This also means that we are now helping the economy and businesses to survive the crisis, but at the same time ensuring that, once the international revival is in place, they are well equipped to respond to it. The trick, then, is to do what needs to be done in the short term, and at the same time to try to strengthen ourselves structurally in order to prepare for the long term. In that respect, investments in infrastructure are very welcome. Because, at least if they are implemented early or at least in time so that their effect is felt immediately, they help to stabilize the economy, but at the same time they increase our capital stock and thus support our structural growth potential in the future, all the more so because we can play important assets in that area in our country: our central location, the presence of many international institutions and multinationals, the already quite decent score we achieve for the quality of our infrastructure in international rankings, the relatively greater weight of the transport sector than in other countries. These are all assets that underline the logistical growth potential of our economy. While these elements illustrate that the maintenance of good public infrastructure is necessary to consolidate or even strengthen our competitive position, it is clear that our investment in this area has been structurally reduced for twenty years now. In the 1970s, public investment of all kinds still amounted to more than 4% of GDP in gross terms, 2% of GDP when depreciation is deducted. Since then, the consolidation of public finances has weighed heavily on these investments, which have returned, since the early 1990s, to some 2% of GDP in gross terms, and to about zero in net terms, which means that, overall, the authorities have done nothing more than keep the stock of public capital stable. without increase. As a result, we also see that our public investment remains well below the European average. In fact, apart from Austria and Germany, public investment fell sharply after the enormous efforts of the early 1990s, following reunification, Belgium has the lowest rate of public investment in Europe. Once again, this weakness is explained by the fact that we have made more efforts than other European countries, starting from a higher state debt, to consolidate our public finances and be able to enter the European monetary union - and I think everyone will agree that participation in this extraordinary European project that is the single currency has already brought us a lot, and that the financial crisis would have hit us much harder - through exchange rate instability, and higher interest rates - if we had not had the euro. One only has to look at what some states outside the eurozone are experiencing at the moment to realize this. But let us not forget that, while the euro has brought us a lot of stability, it cannot guarantee us high economic growth on its own. This requires structural efforts: after the crisis, more people will have to be mobilised on the labour market because the labour supply is likely to shrink due to the ageing of the population, and this requires continued efforts in terms of training and activation. And it will also be necessary to strengthen the structural potential of our economy through innovation, research and development, but also by acting on our strengths, including our infrastructure. And it is obviously necessary to accompany this growth strategy with a budgetary perspective that remains sustainable and that does not pass on all the burdens on future generations. Bouwforum-JS-26-02-2009 (2).doc 3. And that is why my conclusion is rather simple. One: investing in infrastructure is useful to contribute to the recovery. In general, investment has a multiplier effect on the economy that is more interesting than that of consumer spending. A euro spent on consumption generates, through its indirect effects, a total of one and a half euros in additional added value. One euro spent on investments almost two. Also in terms of employment, an investment, apart from the direct jobs, usually creates the same number of jobs in other, derived activities. Secondly, investment in infrastructure is necessary, because we have fallen rather worryingly behind other countries in this respect and can only maintain our good reputation in this area if we improve our sustainable investment efforts. Again: especially our location in the heart of Europe makes this particularly opportune. Thirdly, we must do this effectively, because the resources of the public authorities - which, by the way, are over-demanded in this period of crisis - are scarce. The public budget is undergoing the full shock of the crisis and is going into the red, and that is perfectly normal, it cannot and should not even be otherwise if we want the State to play its normal stabilising role. But in the long term, we must try to get back to balance, and still find the space to structurally strengthen growth and employment. It is a combination and a task that I believe can only succeed if the authorities' action places greater emphasis on investing in what best helps to prepare for the future. There are good practices abroad that can serve as inspiration, such as, for example, Finland, which also went through a serious financial crisis in the early 1990s, with an economic recession of almost 10%, but which has managed, in 15 years of time, to transform itself into one of the most competitive economies, by focusing on the policies of the future: education, training, research, people's activation, but also investment in technology and infrastructure. Better and sustainable investment in our infrastructure, building the future, building tomorrow is therefore the message. And who better to build than the professional builders that you all are? I wish you every success and thank you for your attention. Bouwforum-JS-26-02-2009 (2).doc
text_original: BOUWFORUM (26 februari 2009) Toespraak van Jan Smets Ik volg al lang de economie, maar nooit heb ik de economische vooruitzichten zo snel zien achteruitgaan als in de jongste maanden. U weet het: de financi<91>le crisis heeft de re<91>le economie internationaal besmet, en dat is gebeurd en gebeurt nog verder via 3 kanalen: - de kapitaalbasis van de banken is aangetast door verliezen en waardecorrecties, en dat doet de banken mogelijk voorzichtiger worden bij de kredietverlening, een beweging die wel wordt gecounterd door de herkapitalisaties waarin de overheid helemaal haar rol speelt maar waardoor investeren moeilijker kan worden; - de daling van de aandelenkoersen tast het vermogen van de gezinnen aan, die dat vermogen mogelijk willen herstellen door meer te sparen en dus minder uit te geven; -het vertrouwen van consumenten en ondernemingen is naar laagterecords gezakt, wat weegt op consumptie en investeringen. In tegenstelling tot veel voorgaande crises, is deze bovendien onbetwistbaar globaal. De Amerikaanse hypotheekproblemen zijn via de verpakking en doorverkoop ervan over de hele wereld terechtgekomen, en ook hun economische problemen hebben de hele wereld getroffen: voor 2009 verwachten we nog maar een wereldgroei van 0,5 %, te vergelijken met 3,4 % vorig jaar en zelfs om en bij de 5 % in de jaren voordien, en veel landen bevinden zich in recessie. Het spreekt vanzelf dat de Belgische economie daaraan niet ontsnapt. Vooreerst omdat we met ons internationaal toch ook vrij ontwikkeld banksysteem zelf hard be<95>nvloed zijn door de financi<91>le crisis, maar ook omdat we als kleine open economie eveneens zwaar getroffen worden door de internationale vraaguitval. Volgens onze jongste vooruitzichten, waarop ook de regering heeft gesteund, zou onze economie dit jaar met 1,9 % achteruitgaan, en ook de bouwsector zal daar zeker de invloed van ondervinden - al is zijn situatie zeker veel minder ongunstig dan bv. in Spanje en Ierland, waar hij en met hem de economie lijdt onder de uiteenspatting van een echte zeepbel op de vastgoedmarkt. Le m<8e>tier de pr<8e>visionniste est des plus difficiles aujourd'hui car, s'agissant de la crise actuelle, les r<8e>f<8e>rences du pass<8e> manquent. On n'est pas en d<8e>pression comme au d<8e>but des ann<8e>es trente, notamment gr<89>ce aux actions des banques centrales et des gouvernements, mais on n'a pas non plus de vue claire sur le timing de la reprise - qui, t ou tard, arrivera. La confiance des entrepreneurs est tomb<8e>e <88> un niveau tr<8f>s bas, et vous avez sans doute appris qu'elle a encore chut<8e> ce mois-ci. Et la crise actuelle est avant tout une crise de confiance, dont la restauration est une condition indispensable <88> la reprise. Il est vrai que ce recul de la confiance a <8e>t<8e> moins important dans le g<8e>nie civil, mais le tout dernier chiffre indique l<88> aussi une d<8e>t<8e>rioration. Heureusement, les banques centrales, les gouvernements et les partenaires sociaux d<8e>ploient pour le moment tous les efforts pour parvenir <88> stabiliser l'<8e>conomie. D'abord en stabilisant le syst<8f>me financier: les banques centrales par des injections de liquidit<8e>s, les gouvernements en accordant des garanties ou en intervenant dans le capital des banques. Par la suite, afin de contrer le ralentissement <8e>conomique, les banques centrales ont r<8e>duit les taux d'int<8e>r<90>t, les gouvernements ont mis sur pied des plans de relance, qui devraient id<8e>alement r<8e>pondre aux trois "T": timely - ce qui veut dire que les mesures doivent <90>tre de nature <88> alimenter les d<8e>penses maintenant -, targeted - c'est-<88>-dire orient<8e>s vers les segments les plus prometteurs - et temporary - c'est-<88>-dire, en <8e>vitant de grever nos finances publiques de fa<8d>on structurelle. Dans ce cadre, les autorit<8e>s ont pris des mesures d'all<8e>gement des charges et de facilit<8e>s de paiement en faveur des entreprises, mais elles ont port<8e>, avec raison, une attention particuli<8f>re <88> la construction, par exemple en r<8e>duisant temporairement la TVA et en encourageant les travaux d'infrastructure, tant au niveau du pouvoir f<8e>d<8e>ral qu'au niveau des r<8e>gions. 2. Ik meen dat dat soort van inspanningen zeer goed beantwoordt aan wat ik zou aanbevelen. Waarom? Omdat het mij - en met mij, de NBB en veel internationale instellingen - heel belangrijk lijkt om de overheidsactie in een dubbel perspectief te plaatsen. E<8e>n: zij moet de economie helpen stabiliseren, en dat betekent dat de overheid, zeker nu, voor een stuk de bestedingen moet overnemen van de priv<8e>-sector en de gezinnen, en dus als het ware een bodem moet leggen onder de vraag. Ons systeem van sociale zekerheid draagt daaraan heel goed bij, maar het is goed dat de overheid nog een extra relance-inspanning levert. Maar twee: de overheid moet er ook toe bijdragen dat onze economie goed voorbereid is op de exit uit de crisis. Dat betekent bijvoorbeeld dat we de eerste slachtoffers van de crisis - werklozen - goed opvangen, maar ook dat we ze niet te vroeg laten gaan maar vasthouden, opleiden en begeleiden, zodat ze na de crisis terug goed kunnen ingezet worden in een arbeidsmarkt die tendentieel krapper aan het worden is. Dat betekent ook dat we nu economie en bedrijven helpen om de crisis te overleven, maar tegelijk ervoor moeten zorgen dat zij, eenmaal de internationale herleving er is, goed gewapend zijn om daarop in te spelen. De kunst bestaat er dus in om op korte termijn te doen wat men moet doen, en tegelijk te trachten ons structureel te versterken om de lange termijn voor te bereiden. In dat opzicht zijn investeringen in infrastructuur precies heel welkom. Want, tenminste als men ze vervroegd of in ieder geval tijdig uitvoert zodat hun effect zich onmiddellijk laat voelen, helpen ze de economie te stabiliseren, maar tegelijk vergroten ze onze kapitaalvoorraad en ondersteunen ze zo ons structureel groeipotentieel in de toekomst, temeer omdat we op dat stuk in ons land voorname troeven kunnen uitspelen: onze centrale ligging, de aanwezigheid van veel internationale instellingen en multinationals, de al vrij behoorlijke score die we halen voor de kwaliteit van onze infrastructuur in internationale rangschikkingen, het relatief groter gewicht ook van de vervoersector dan in andere landen. Allemaal troeven die het logistieke groeipotentieel van onze economie onderstrepen. Si ces <8e>l<8e>ments illustrent que le maintien d'une bonne infrastructure publique s'impose pour consolider, voire renforcer notre position concurrentielle, force est de constater que notre investissement en la mati<8f>re a <8e>t<8e> structurellement r<8e>duit depuis d<8e>j<88> une vingtaine d'ann<8e>es. Dans les ann<8e>es 1970, les investissements publics de toute nature atteignaient encore plus de 4 pc du PIB en termes bruts, 2 pc du PIB lorsqu'on en d<8e>duit les amortissements. Depuis lors, l'assainissement des finances publiques a fortement pes<8e> sur ces investissements, qui sont revenus, depuis le d<8e>but des ann<8e>es 1990, <88> quelque 2 pc du PIB en termes bruts, et <88> environ z<8e>ro en termes nets, ce qui veut dire que, globalement, les autorit<8e>s n'ont rien fait de plus que de maintenir le stock de capital public stable, sans accroissement. Et, de ce fait, on observe <8e>galement que nos investissements publics restent tr<8f>s en de<8d><88> de la moyenne europ<8e>enne. En fait, mis <88> part l'Autriche et l'Allemagne, oles investissements publics ont fortement chut<8e> apr<8f>s les <8e>normes efforts du d<8e>but des ann<8e>es 1990, <88> la suite de la r<8e>unification, la Belgique affiche le taux d'investissement public le plus faible de l'Europe. Encore une fois, cette faiblesse s'explique par ce qu'on a dfaire plus d'efforts que d'autres pays europ<8e>ens, en partant d'un endettement de l'<83>tat plus <8e>lev<8e>, pour assainir nos finances publiques et pouvoir rentrer dans l'union mon<8e>taire europ<8e>enne - et je pense que tout le monde sera d'accord pour reconna<94>tre que la participation <88> cet extraordinaire projet europ<8e>en qu'est la monnaie unique nous a d<8e>j<88> beaucoup apport<8e>, et que la crise financi<8f>re nous aurait frapp<8e> beaucoup plus durement - par une instabilit<8e> des cours de change, et par des taux d'int<8e>r<90>t plus <8e>lev<8e>s - si nous n'avions pas eu l'euro. Il suffit de voir ce que certains <83>tats hors la zone euro vivent pour le moment pour s'en rendre compte. Mais n'oublions pas que, si l'euro nous a apport<8e> beaucoup de stabilit<8e>, il ne peut pas tout seul nous garantir une croissance <8e>conomique <8e>lev<8e>e. Pour cela, il faut des efforts structurels: apr<8f>s la crise, il faudra mobiliser davantage de gens sur le march<8e> du travail car la r<8e>serve de main d'<cf>uvre risque de se r<8e>duire <88> cause du vieillissement de la population, et cela demande la poursuite des efforts en termes de formation et d'activation. Et il faudra aussi renforcer le potentiel structurel de notre <8e>conomie via l'innovation, la recherche et le d<8e>veloppement, mais aussi en agissant sur nos points forts parmi lesquels nos infrastructures. Et il faut <8e>videmment assortir cette strat<8e>gie de croissance d'une perspective budg<8e>taire qui reste soutenable et qui ne reporte pas toutes les charges sur les g<8e>n<8e>rations futures. Bouwforum-JS-26-02-2009 (2).doc 3. En vandaar dat mijn conclusie nogal simpel is. E<8e>n: investeren in infrastructuur is nuttig om bij te dragen aan de relance. Investeren heeft in het algemeen trouwens een multiplicatoreffect op de economie dat interessanter is dan dat van consumptieve uitgaven. Een euro besteed voor verbruik genereert, via zijn indirecte effecten, in totaal anderhalve euro extra toegevoegde waarde. Een euro besteed voor investeringen bijna twee. Ook in termen van werkgelegenheid cre<91>ert een investering, buiten de directe jobs, meestal nog eens evenveel jobs in andere, afgeleide activiteiten. Twee: investeren in infrastructuur is noodzakelijk, want we hebben op dat stuk een vrij zorgwekkende achterstand opgelopen t.o.v. andere landen en kunnen onze op zich goede reputatie op dat gebied maar vasthouden als we onze duurzame investeringsinspanningen verbeteren. Nogmaals: vooral onze ligging in het hart van Europa maakt dat bijzonder opportuun. Drie: we moeten dit doelmatig doen, omdat de middelen van de overheid - die in deze crisisperiode trouwens overbevraagd wordt - schaars zijn. De overheidsbegroting ondergaat de volledige schok van de crisis en gaat in het rood, en dat is perfect normaal, het kan en mag zelfs niet anders als we willen dat de Staat zijn normale stabiliserende rol speelt. Maar op termijn moeten we trachten terug naar het evenwicht te gaan, en toch de ruimte vinden om groei en werkgelegenheid structureel te versterken. C'est une combinaison et une mission qui ne pourront r<8e>ussir, je pense, que si l'action des autorit<8e>s met davantage l'accent sur l'investissement dans ce qui contribue le mieux <88> pr<8e>parer l'avenir. Il y a de bonnes pratiques <88> l'<8e>tranger qui peuvent servir d'inspiration, telles que par exemple la Finlande, qui a travers<8e> elle aussi une grave crise financi<8f>re au d<8e>but des ann<8e>es 1990, avec une r<8e>cession <8e>conomique de pr<8f>s de 10 pc, mais qui a r<8e>ussi, en 15 ans de temps, <88> se transformer en une des <8e>conomies les plus comp<8e>titives, en se concentrant sur les politiques d'avenir: l'enseignement, la formation, la recherche, l'activation des gens, mais aussi l'investissement en technologies et en infrastructures. Beter en duurzaam investeren in onze infrastructuur, bouwen aan de toekomst, bouwen aan morgen is dus de boodschap. En wie kan er beter bouwen dan de professionele bouwers die u allen is? Ik wens u heel veel succes toe en dank u voor uw aandacht. Bouwforum-JS-26-02-2009 (2).doc

Title: 2009 General Assembly: Introductory statement by the Governor
text: GENERAL ASSEMBLY 2009 INTRODUCTORY STATEMENT BY GOVERNOR Brussels, 2009-03-30 Ladies and Gentlemen, I welcome you, on my own behalf and on behalf of the other members of the Management Committee, to this ordinary general meeting of shareholders of the National Bank of Belgium. As is traditional, I would like to briefly mention the most significant events of the year under review, before giving the floor to the Deputy Governor who will present and comment on the annual accounts for the financial year 2008. This afternoon, we will answer your questions. The year 2008 will continue to be marked by one of the most important financial crises that Europe and the world have ever experienced. Economic history is made up of cycles, periods of growth and recession. This time, however, the crisis is more brutal, deeper and more widespread than most previous ones and has called on the political and monetary authorities to respond quickly, often urgently, to deal with situations unprecedented in nature and magnitude. The Bank found itself at the forefront and had to - in particular in the last months of the year - face a liquidity crisis that threatened the entire Belgian and European financial system. Faced with the worsening crisis of confidence and the almost complete drying up of the interbank market, some Belgian banks have faced serious liquidity problems. These institutions no longer had the guarantees accepted to obtain additional liquidity by using loans granted by the Eurosystem. Faced with a risk that had become systemic and a general crisis of confidence, the SNB set up an unprecedented procedure to provide them with liquidity in an emergency. These very exceptional interventions are intended to solve liquidity problems limited in time and only after the possibilities of recourse to the credits granted in the context of monetary policy have been exhausted. These interventions have reached considerable amounts and have not remained without impact on the Bank's annual accounts, which the Deputy Governor will present to you in a moment. The risk of loss arising from the granting of loans in the context of the execution of monetary policy shall be borne by the Eurosystem as a whole, in proportion to the share of each national central bank in the capital of the European Central Bank. However, the risk is not shared when it comes to the provision of emergency liquidity. For this reason, an amendment has been made to the Bank's Organic Law: the risks associated with the operations necessary to ensure the stability of the financial system are now automatically covered by the State guarantee. The Bank's Organic Law has also been amended to provide the Bank with an Audit Committee. This amendment transposes, in the case of the Bank, a European directive that requires listed companies to set up an Audit Committee. If, in ordinary companies, the Audit Committee is set up within the Board of Directors, a specific solution is established 2. was to be applied to the Bank, in the absence of a body comparable to a board of directors. Given the composition and powers of the College of Censors, the legislator has entrusted it with this new responsibility. Finally, a third amendment to the Organic Law modifies the rules for the distribution of the Bank's revenues and profits. The aim is to abolish the so-called 3% rule under which the Bank disposes of the net financial income generated by its activities up to 3% of the annual average of its net profitable assets to cover its operating costs, pay a dividend to its shareholders and replenish its reserves, with the surplus going to the State. The new rule also removes the complex mechanism of devolution of profits, with in particular a priority share for the State. From now on, the distribution of revenues will have to be made on the basis of the net result for the year. The Regency Council will determine the share of the net profits of the year that will be used to replenish the reserves and remunerate the capital, the balance being allocated to the State. This method, which is simpler and more in line with the practices followed by other central banks, should make it possible to further increase transparency in the allocation of the institution's income, while taking into account the specificity of its public tasks. The text also provides for the allocation of a minimum dividend to shareholders to the fullest extent that profits allow. The dividend distributed can be expected to grow faster in the future, compared to the current policy of a constant dividend in real terms. As already announced, the SNB will adapt its reserve and dividend policy to the new financial provisions of its organic statute once the law has been published in the Moniteur belge. As soon as it has been defined, the future reserve and dividend policy will be made public in accordance with the rules on inside information. It will also be presented to shareholders who wish to do so during information sessions to be held after the summer months. That being said, there is one element of the reserve policy that the Regency Council has already been able to anticipate: the fate of the provision for miscellaneous risks and the provision for future exchange rate losses. The amount of these two provisions will be transferred in full to the available reserves, which will have a significant positive impact on the amount of the minimum dividend. The year 2008 was also characterized by the development of several important projects. The Bank continued and intensified its efforts to reduce the administrative burden on enterprises of transmitting data for macroeconomic statistics. This relief has not come at the expense of quality. On the contrary, collection and counter techniques have been improved, which has made it possible to maintain or even strengthen the reliability of the data. Like other IT systems developed by the Bank, the new application developed for this purpose has attracted interest from other central banks in the euro area. They tend to pool their resources more in order to increase collaboration and the sharing of know-how within the Eurosystem. This concern to improve 3. the effectiveness of the procedures is present in the development of all the services that the legislator has entrusted to the Bank. It results in the development of internet applications (in particular for the deposit of companies' annual accounts), the rationalization of ticket processing or the continuous improvement of logistics services. In this way, the Bank was able to further reduce its staff while continuing to take on its various missions of general interest. I now give the floor to the Deputy Governor, who will present to you in detail the annual accounts for the financial year 2008. As usual, a question-and-answer session will take place after lunch. I would like to thank the shareholders who sent us their questions in advance, thus facilitating the preparation and smooth running of this meeting. Thank you for your attention.
