Title: The issue of pensions in the context of ageing and the crisis
text: 31/03/2010 Cl.: IV.E.2. THE PROBLEM OF PENSIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF AGEING AND THE CRISIS by Guy Quaden, Governor of the National Bank of Belgium Chairman of the Study Committee on Ageing of the Higher Council of Finance Presentation at the Seminar of the Belgian Association of Pension Institutions Brussels, 1 April 2010 PP2 1. INTRODUCTION In addition to the particularly difficult economic and budgetary situation at the time, Belgium and other European countries are now faced with the challenge of reaching retirement age for the generation born between the end of the Second World War and the mid-1960s. PP 3 The old-age dependency ratio, i.e. the share of people aged over 65 expressed as a proportion of the working-age population (15 to 64), would rise in Belgium from 25.8 to 45.8 per cent between 2008 and 2060. This increase would occur in all EU15 countries, but the proportions of this increase in pressure on the working-age population would vary from country to country, ranging from an increase of 34.9 percentage points in Spain to an increase of 17.9 percentage points in the United Kingdom, with an average of 24.6 points in the EU15. At the level of the pension problem, the ageing of the population has two main inseparable aspects that must be taken into account by political decision-makers. The first element relates to the increase in the budgetary burden that will weigh on public finances, namely the "fiscal sustainability" component. The first part of this presentation will return to the projections made by the Study Committee on Aging in its last Annual Report, dated June 2009. The second essential element in the problem of pensions is the 'social sustainability' aspect, in the sense that pensions have a protective net to play. On the one hand, they must limit the specific risk of poverty that affects the elderly. On the other hand and more generally, "social sustainability" aims to maintain the standard of living after admission to retirement. This aspect was also addressed in the context of the CEV Annual Report and will be part of the second part of this presentation. The economic and financial crisis from which we are emerging very gradually is also having a considerable impact on the long-term sustainability of public finances. The third part of the presentation will focus on presenting the risks associated with a situation that would be considered unsustainable by economic actors. As a result, certain economic policies should be put in place, particularly with regard to pension reforms, which will be the subject of the last part of this presentation. 2. TRENDS IN SOCIAL EXPENDITURE BY 2060 PP 4 The Aging Review Committee's projections are based on a set of assumptions that need to be briefly recalled: . demographic assumptions assume in the long term a fertility rate stabilizing at the average level observed in recent years, lower than in the past, life expectancies at birth continuously increasing (from 77 years in 2007 to 85 years in 2060 for men and from 83 years to 91 years for women) and a positive migratory balance but depending in particular on the relative economic attractiveness of Belgium; . the social policy assumptions are in line with the legislation currently in force, i.e. an increase of 1.25 p.c. in the salary ceilings and the minimum entitlement per year of career, by 1 p.c. of lump sums and minima and by 0.5 p.c. of other allowances; . macroeconomic assumptions, such as employment or productivity, are potentially the most consequential, but are more than ever surrounded by broad uncertainties. PP 5 Already, in the medium term, the macroeconomic scenario used was marked by a high degree of uncertainty, mainly as to the duration and intensity of the financial crisis and its impact on the real economy. This scenario assumed a loss of output as a result of the crisis, which was not compensated for over the next five years. On the other hand, economic growth was expected to return, from 2011, to a growth rate comparable to that observed on average before the outbreak of the crisis. In the long run, recurring uncertainty is mainly based on assumptions about productivity growth. This uncertainty is also amplified by the crisis. In its latest report, the CEV made an important change from this point of view, since the reference scenario now has an annual productivity growth rate of 1.5 p.c., which is an average between two alternative scenarios: the hitherto usual growth scenario of 1.75 p.c. and a lower growth scenario (1.25 p.c.). To the extent that, in the long term, employment growth would be virtually zero, as a result of the decline in the working-age population from the mid-2020s, GDP growth would be progressively more limited, with just over 1.5 p.c. of growth from the end of the 2030s. Lower growth means, all other things being equal, that the costs of aging are heavier to bear. PP 6 In the CEV reference scenario, the budgetary contribution for ageing amounts to 8.2 p.c. of GDP between 2008 and 2060. It already stands at 2.6 p.c. between 2008 and 2010, because the economic crisis has been reflected not only in a decline in GDP  and therefore an increase in this ratio, but also in a sharp increase in the number of farmers. In the longer term, the budgetary contribution of ageing reaches 4.9 per cent of GDP between 2014 and 2060. PP 7 PP 8 PP 9 Expenditure on pensions and health care is crucial to the budgetary contribution of ageing: celles.ci increased by 5.3 and 4.2 per cent of GDP respectively between 2008 and 2060. On the contrary, the other categories of social expenditure  chage, family allowances, etc. should contribute slightly to tempering the increase in cos linked to demographic changes. The remainder of this presentation will focus on the pension-related contribution. The increase in pension expenditures is mainly due to the large increase in the number of pensioners occurring in each plan. However, pension expenditure in the employed and self-employed schemes is growing proportionately less rapidly than the corresponding number of beneficiaries, due to a long-term deterioration in their rate of benefit (average pension in relation to the macroeconomic average salary). In these two regimes, the rate of profit first increases until around 2020, mainly due to the various measures of adaptation to well-being taken in the medium term. Subsequently, it is constantly reduced as a result of different factors. In the self-employed scheme, more than 3/4 of pensioners receive a minimum pension which is only partially adapted to welfare. In the salaried scheme, several factors explain this development: the application of a salary ceiling when calculating the pension (blocked in real terms during the period 1982.1998 and partially adapted to the evolution of wages in the long term); only partial adaptation to well-being; the splitting of the pension at the household rate into two pensions at the single rate, which increases the number of beneficiaries but does not increase the amount of their income proportionally. On the other hand, the rate of profit in the public sector is projected not to be reduced, as a result of equalization or the adjustment of pensions to wage developments. 3. SOCIAL SUSTAINABILITY OF PENSIONS In order to determine the social sustainability or, in other words, the adequacy of pensions, it is examined whether they are able, now and in the future, to protect the elderly against the risk of poverty. In addition, they should enable people retiring to maintain their standard of living at a reasonable level. The results of the EU survey. SILC 2007 relate to the situation in 2006. The effects of the most recent measures and measures that will only produce their effects in the longer term are therefore not reflected in these indicators. This survey shows that in Belgium 15% of the total population is at risk of poverty1, compared with 23% of people aged 65 and over. In this group, the people most at risk are women, the very elderly and the isolated. The percentage rises to 20 p.c. for pensioners. 1 This means that the equivalent disposable income of the persons concerned is below the poverty line, which in 2006 amounted to 878 per month or 10,540 per year. PP 10 PP 11 PP 12 In comparison with neighbouring countries2, pensioners and persons over 65 living in Belgium are at increased risk of poverty. In these countries too, the risk of poverty is higher for women than for men. The social sustainability of pensions is still measured by replacement rates3, which give an indication of the decline in the available means of subsistence between working life and pension. Traditionally, second and third pillar pensions are intended to avoid or limit a significant drop in income at that time. In many European countries, the reforms that have been carried out in recent years have resulted or will result in a reduction in pension benefits, to the detriment of social sustainability. Thus, in countries with the highest net replacement rates, the reforms implemented have the effect of reducing it (Portugal, Italy, Austria and, to a lesser extent, Sweden, France and Finland). In Germany, the replacement rate of low-income workers was somewhat improved, while for middle incomes the replacement rate was revised downwards. This trend towards a smaller reduction for the lowest incomes is also widespread. The countries where replacement rates were the lowest (Belgium, United Kingdom) will, on the contrary, retain replacement rates at least as high as before the reforms. They will even be significantly improved in the United Kingdom, as far as the lowest incomes are concerned. As a result, replacement rates in the EU15 countries tend to refocus, for both middle and modest incomes, slightly less for higher incomes. The second pillar of pensions was the subject of more particular attention in the 2007 and 2008 annual reports of the CEV, which showed in particular the effect of this pillar on the average amounts received by pensioners. One of the objectives was to see to what extent a second pension pillar can provide a solution to the problem of poverty. Focusing on persons who have had a pure career as an employee, it is possible to differentiate the average monthly pension amounts for pensioners who have only a statutory pension and for those who also receive a supplementary pension. It shows that, so far, the second pillar of pensions is mainly a supplement for pensioners who already have a relatively high statutory pension than for those with low pensions. In particular, few women receive a second-pillar supplementary pension and, when they participate, this supplement is significantly lower than that of men. Yet it is precisely retired women who are at increased risk of poverty. 2 As already mentioned, the risk of income-related poverty is based on the income or poverty line set here at 60 per cent of median equivalised net income. Starting from the EU investigation. SILC 2007 (2006 revenues), this corresponds to an annual income of 10,624 in Germany, 9,938 in France and 10,924 in the Netherlands. The average risk of poverty in the EU.25 is calculated by Eurostat on the basis of a weighting of population categories. 3 That is the amount of the average pension expressed as a percentage of the last salary. These figures show that  at least until 2004  the supplementary pension was not an effective means of combating poverty. It was more of a way for people with more comfortable incomes to avoid an excessive drop in their income when they retire. The supplementary pension therefore seemed to be an effective means of increasing the replacement rate of people with relatively high incomes. However, the Green Paper, published within the framework of the National Pensions Conference, gives some more recent indications, particularly with regard to second-pillar pensions, which are particularly interesting since they were subsequent to the law on supplementary pensions, one of the objectives of which was a democratisation of this pillar. Thus, it appears that many sectoral plans cover largely or exclusively manual workers, mostly male. In 2008, 60 per cent of workers were covered by this pillar. Nevertheless, the resources for this socio-professional category remain much lower than those devoted to management plans, with employees halfway there. The same Green Paper states that pension commitment would increasingly be regarded as one of the aspects of remuneration policy. 4. BUDGETARY SUSTAINABILITY AND THE EFFECT OF THE ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL CRISIS PP 13 The crisis-related deterioration in public finances and the projected increase in expenditure linked to the ageing of the population raise the question of the sustainability of public finances. In almost all advanced economies, the effect of automatic stabilisers and stimulus packages, following the economic recession, has been to seriously alter the health of public finances. Public deficit and debt levels are rising rapidly, and deficits now have such a structural component that fiscal problems will not go away once the economy recovers from the recession. In addition, the fiscal impact of an ageing population is expected to generate even higher deficits and a sharp rise in public debt. On the one hand, economic growth will slow down, as a result of the decline in the working-age population, which will not be offset by the limited improvement in the employment rate. Productivity growth will thus be the only contributing factor to GDP growth. According to pre-financial crisis projections, the potential growth rate would fall from 2.2 p.c. in 2010 to 1.4 p.c. in 2060 in the euro area. On the other hand, there will be increasing pressure on public spending on pensions, health and long-term care for the elderly. PP 14 In the euro area, annual age-related public expenditure is expected to increase by 5.1 percentage points of GDP between 2010 and 2060. The fiscal situation is unsustainable in virtually all euro area countries, requiring substantial adjustments. The effort required to meet the intertemporal budgetary constraint  the "sustainability gap"  amounts to no less than 5.8 p.c. of GDP. This euro area average, however, masks considerable divergences between countries, with some having to produce a double-digit effort. The main elements that make up the sustainability gap are the current structural budgetary position and the projected change in age-related cos. A few countries are facing both large initial imbalances and a projected large increase in age-related spending. This is particularly the case for Greece, which faces a very high deficit and debt and a huge ageing stock by 2060. It is therefore not surprising that the financial markets have become nervous about this country. In most of the top 15 EU Member States, deficit increases and debt resulting from deteriorating economic conditions, combined with the projected impact of ageing populations on public finances, make fiscal sustainability an acute problem. In this context, it is important to announce clear and reliable strategies for returning to sustainable and sound public finances. In many of these countries, major fiscal consolidation is inevitable. 5. IMPLICATIONS IN TERMS OF BUDGETARY POLICY PP15 . Rebuilding confidence in the sustainability of public finances is crucial PP 16 In the current context, even more than usual, the risks to lack of trust are numerous. First, uncertainty tends to generate precautionary savings from households. Such a Ricardian effect would be detrimental to the recovery of the economy. Second, doubts about the sustainability of public finances lead to adverse effects on financial markets, which has the effect of driving up interest rates. So far, governments have financed higher budget deficits at a relatively limited cost. The sharp rise in interest rates that usually accompanies that of public debt has not materialized or not yet materialized, but cannot be ruled out in the future. Preserving and, in some countries, rebuilding confidence in public finances is thus of the utmost importance. Therefore, the economic policies decided must offer the prospect of significantly reduced budget deficits and guarantee the long-term sustainability of public finances. The ongoing economic recovery is still fragile and could remain modest in the near future. Therefore, a strong and rapid consolidation effort, coupled with the gradual disappearance of stimulus measures, could also weigh on economic recovery. In addition, a postponement of consolidation efforts raises the risk of a rise in long-term interest rates. The development of ambitious and credible fiscal consolidation programmes to improve sustainability is urgent in most countries. However, a distinction can be made between the announcement of consolidation plans and their effective implementation. To avoid doubts about the solvency of countries, it can therefore be recommended that credible consolidation plans and concrete measures should not be delayed, even if they will, for the most part, only be implemented once a certain recovery has been confirmed. . The strategy to pre-finance the cost of ageing has failed, so important reforms are inevitable Fiscal policy has long been seen as a crucial part of the strategy to prepare for the economic implications of demographic change. The reduction in the level of public debt and a sound fiscal position should create the necessary margins to finance the increase in ageing expenditure. For example, the Belgian targets for general government financing capacity, contained in successive stability programmes presented between 1999 and 2008, were systematically positive and improving over two- to three-year horizons, but rarely in the coming budget year. However, as it is politically difficult to produce budget surpluses, these targets have been postponed year after year, with the result that only the years 2001 and 2006 can be credited with a positive budgetary balance, indicating that this pre-financing strategy has not materialized, even in relatively favourable years. The deterioration of public finances linked to the economic and financial crisis and the fact that the costs of ageing have already begun to be felt make pre-financing now practically impossible, so the strategy needs to be adapted. Although deficit and debt reduction must remain an essential part of the strategy, the other two components of this strategy, namely higher employment rates and reforms of social protection systems, have become much more important. In addition, the urgency is now at the rendezvous. The second component of the strategy is to increase potential growth. L<d5>effort n<8e>cessaire afin de satisfaire <88> la contrainte budg<8e>taire intertemporelle <d0> le <c7> sustainability gap <c8><ca>.sl<8f>ve <88> pas moins de 5,8 p.c. du PIB. Les principaux <8e>l<8e>ments qui composent le <c7> sustainability gap <c8> sont la position budg<8e>taire structurelle actuelle et le changement projet<8e> des cos li<8e>s au vieillissement. Quelques pays sont confront<8e>s <88> la fois <88> de grands d<8e>s<8e>quilibres initiaux et <88> une importante augmentation projet<8e>e des d<8e>penses relatives <88> l'<89>ge. C'est en particulier le cas pour la Gr<8f>ce, qui fait face <88> un d<8e>ficit et <88> une dette tr<8f>s <8e>lev<8e>s et <88> un <8e>norme cot du vieillissement <88> l<d5>horizon 2060. Il n<d5>est donc pas surprenant que les march<8e>s financiers soient devenus nerveux par rapport <88> ce pays. Dans la plupart des 15 premiers pays membres de l<d5>UE, les augmentations du d<8e>ficit et la dette cons<8e>cutives <88> la d<8e>t<8e>rioration de la situation <8e>conomique, combin<8e>es <88> l'impact projet<8e> du vieillissement des populations sur les finances publiques, font de la soutenabilit<8e> budg<8e>taire un probl<8f>me aigu. Il importe, dans ce contexte, d<d5>annoncer des strat<8e>gies claires et fiables de retour <88> des finances publiques soutenables et saines. Dans nombre de ces pays, une consolidation fiscale majeure est in<8e>vitable. 5. IMPLICATIONS EN TERMES DE POLITIQUE BUDGETAIRE PP15 . La reconstitution de la confiance vis.<88>.vis de la soutenabilit<8e> des finances publiques est cruciale PP 16 Dans le contexte actuel, plus encore que d<d5>habitude, les risques encourus par le manque de confiance sont nombreux. Premi<8f>rement, l'incertitude tend <88> g<8e>n<8e>rer une <8e>pargne de pr<8e>caution de la part des m<8e>nages. Un tel effet Ricardien serait nocif au r<8e>tablissement de lconomie. Deuxi<8f>mement, le doute quant <88> la soutenabilit<8e> des finances publiques conduit <88> des effets n<8e>fastes sur les march<8e>s financiers, ce qui a pour effet de faire monter les taux d'int<8e>r<90>t. Jusqu'ici, les gouvernements ont financ<8e> des d<8e>ficits budg<8e>taires plus <8e>lev<8e>s <88> un cot relativement limit<8e>. La forte hausse des taux d'int<8e>r<90>t qui accompagne g<8e>n<8e>ralement celle de la dette publique ne s<d5>est pas ou pas encore mat<8e>rialis<8e>e, mais ne peut <90>tre exclue <88> l'avenir. La pr<8e>servation et, dans certains pays, la reconstitution de la confiance vis.<88>.vis des finances publiques est ainsi de la plus grande importance. Par cons<8e>quent, les politiques <8e>conomiques d<8e>cid<8e>es doivent offrir la perspective de d<8e>ficits budg<8e>taires r<8e>duits significativement et garantir la soutenabilit<8e> <88> long terme des finances publiques. Le r<8e>tablissement <8e>conomique en cours est encore fragile et pourrait rester modeste dans un avenir proche. Par cons<8e>quent, un effort de consolidation fort et rapide, s<d5>ajoutant <88> la disparition progressive des mesures de stimulus, pourrait <8e>galement peser sur le r<8e>tablissement <8e>conomique. Par ailleurs, un ajournement des efforts de consolidation fait planer le risque d<d5>une hausse des taux d'int<8e>r<90>ts <88> long terme. L'<8e>laboration de programmes de consolidation budg<8e>taires ambitieux et cr<8e>dibles, visant <88> am<8e>liorer la soutenabilit<8e>, est urgente dans la plupart des pays. Toutefois, une distinction peut <90>tre faite entre l'annonce des plans de consolidation et leur mise en <cf>uvre effective. Pour <8e>viter que la solvabilit<8e> des pays soit mise en doute, on peut ainsi recommander de ne pas retarder l'annonce de plans de consolidation cr<8e>dibles et de mesures concr<8f>tes, m<90>me s<d5>ils ne seront, la plupart du temps, mis en application qu'une fois une certaine reprise confirm<8e>e. . La strat<8e>gie pour pr<8e>financer le cot du vieillissement a <8e>chou<8e>, de sorte que des r<8e>formes importantes sont in<8e>vitables La politique budg<8e>taire a <8e>t<8e> longtemps consid<8e>r<8e>e comme une partie cruciale de la strat<8e>gie pour se pr<8e>parer aux implications <8e>conomiques du changement d<8e>mographique. La r<8e>duction du niveau de la dette publique et une situation budg<8e>taire saine devaient cr<8e>er les marges n<8e>cessaires au financement de la hausse des d<8e>penses de vieillissement. C<d5>est ainsi, par exemple, que les objectifs belges en mati<8f>re de capacit<8e> de financement des administrations publiques, contenus dans les programmes de stabilit<8e> successifs pr<8e>sent<8e>s entre 1999 et 2008, <8e>taient syst<8e>matiquement positifs et en am<8e>lioration <88> des horizons de deux <88> trois ans, mais rarement pendant l'ann<8e>e budg<8e>taire <88> venir. Cependant, comme il est politiquement difficile de produire des exc<8e>dents budg<8e>taires, ces cibles ont <8e>t<8e> postpos<8e>es ann<8e>e apr<8f>s ann<8e>e, avec pour cons<8e>quence que seules les ann<8e>es 2001 et 2006 peuvent <90>tre cr<8e>dit<8e>es d<d5>un solde budg<8e>taire positif, ce qui indique que cette strat<8e>gie de pr<8e>financement ne s'est pas mat<8e>rialis<8e>e, m<90>me durant les ann<8e>es relativement favorables. La d<8e>t<8e>rioration des finances publiques li<8e>e <88> la crise <8e>conomique et financi<8f>re et le fait que les cots du vieillissement ont d<8e>j<88> commenc<8e> <88> se faire sentir rendent le pr<8e>financement d<8e>sormais pratiquement impossible, de sorte que la strat<8e>gie doit <90>tre adapt<8e>e. Bien que la r<8e>duction du d<8e>ficit et de la dette doivent demeurer une partie essentielle de la strat<8e>gie, les deux autres composants de cette strat<8e>gie<ca>.<88> savoir des taux d'emploi plus <8e>lev<8e>s et des r<8e>formes des syst<8f>mes de protection sociale<ca>.sont devenues bien plus importantes. En outre, l'urgence est d<8e>sormais au rendez.vous. La deuxi<8f>me composante de la strat<8e>gie consiste <88> augmenter la croissance potentielle. Toutefois, dans le contexte de la diminution de la population en <89>ge de travailler, le taux de croissance potentiel diminuera <8e>galement. En outre, on s<d5>attend <88> ce que la crise financi<8f>re et <8e>conomique en cours ait une influence n<8e>gative sur l<d5>output potentiel, voire sur la croissance potentielle. Les choix budg<8e>taires peuvent aider <88> am<8e>liorer l'innovation, l'emploi et la comp<8e>titivit<8e> en r<8e>orientant des recettes et des d<8e>penses afin de favoriser l'investissement et l<d5>emploi. Ainsi, il est souhaitable de mieux accompagner et pr<8e>parer les (futurs) travailleurs, d<d5>am<8e>liorer l'infrastructure requise pour le d<8e>ploiement <8e>conomique, ou encore d<d5>amplifier l'investissement dans l'<8e>ducation, la formation et la recherche. Cependant, les effets d'une telle strat<8e>gie ne sont ni directs et ss, ni suffisants pour faire face aux cos croissants du vieillissement. La troisi<8f>me partie de la strat<8e>gie, soit la d<8e>cision d<d5>entreprendre des r<8e>formes importantes, est donc devenue in<8e>vitable. . Les mesures visant <88> limiter l'impact budg<8e>taire du vieillissement doivent <90>tre une part essentielle des plans de consolidation fiscale Dans nombre de pays, les r<8e>formes ayant pour but de relever lge effectif du d<8e>part <88> la retraite et de limiter la hausse des d<8e>penses li<8e>es au vieillissement, devraient constituer une partie essentielle de la consolidation fiscale instamment n<8e>cessaire. Ces r<8e>formes doivent notamment permettre de restaurer la confiance en la soutenabilit<8e> <88> long terme des finances publiques. Et, si une politique budg<8e>taire fortement restrictive peut avoir un impact n<8e>gatif sur la relance, ce n<d5>est pas le cas de r<8e>formes mises en application graduellement. PP 17 Certaines r<8e>formes peuvent en effet mener <88> une forte r<8e>duction des cos du vieillissement. L'Italie, la Su<8f>de et le Danemark, par exemple, ont entrepris des r<8e>formes des syst<8f>mes de pension qui devraient laisser la part des d<8e>penses de pension presque inchang<8e>e <88> long terme. Toutefois, certaines de ces r<8e>formes sont difficiles <88> mettre en application. En effet, il n'y a pas beaucoup de marge pour r<8e>duire les droits individuels, vu la faiblesse du taux de remplacement dans de nombreux pays, dont la Belgique. La principale alternative est de relever l'<89>ge effectif de d<8e>part <88> la retraite, ce qui permet <88> la fois d<d5>am<8e>liorer le taux d'emploi et de limiter les cos du vieillissement. Ceci peut <90>tre fait soit en relevant l'<89>ge l<8e>gal de la retraite au.dessus de 65 ans (cf. Allemagne, Danemark, Finlande, Su<8f>de et Royaume.Uni), en relevant l'<89>ge de la retraite anticip<8e>e ou en la rendant d<d5>acc<8f>s difficile, en augmentant les incitants pour rester au travail plus longtemps ou en p<8e>nalisant les retraites anticip<8e>es (cf. Royaume.Uni, Portugal, Allemagne et Finlande, par exemple, voire la Belgique qui a opt<8e> pour une bonification annuelle comportant un forfait de 2 euros par jour ouvr<8e> au del<88> de l'<89>ge de 62 ou apr<8f>s 44 ans de contributions). La prolongation de la carri<8f>re de r<8e>f<8e>rence est <8e>galement une incitation financi<8f>re <88> rester au travail, mais cette solution ne concerne pas la Belgique <d0> sauf les fonctionnaires<ca>., puisque toute la carri<8f>re y est d<8e>j<88> prise en consid<8e>ration. En outre, la dur<8e>e de la carri<8f>re de r<8e>f<8e>rence peut <8e>galement <90>tre allong<8e>e (cf. France, Italie ou m<90>me Belgique pour les femmes). Un <8e>talement dans le temps de telles mesures devrait permettre d<d5>am<8e>liorer l'acceptation politique de telles r<8e>formes, de m<90>me que le rappel du caract<8f>re in<8e>quitable par rapport aux g<8e>n<8e>rations futures du syst<8f>me s<d5>il demeurait inchang<8e>. 6. CONCLUSION Dans la plupart des pays europ<8e>ens, le vieillissement de la population <d0> une <8e>volution globalement positive <d0> s<d5>accompagne de d<8e>fis importants en mati<8f>re de finances publiques. Le cot des d<8e>penses li<8e>es au vieillissement de la population devrait en effet s<d5>accro<94>tre largement d<8f>s les prochaines ann<8e>es et pour plusieurs d<8e>cennies. Ce d<8e>fi budg<8e>taire s<d5>accompagne d<d5>une probl<8e>matique de soutenabilit<8e> sociale, en ce sens que les pensions doivent servir <88> <8e>viter que les plus <89>g<8e>s ne vivent dans la pr<8e>carit<8e> ou ne voient leurs moyens d<d5>existence se d<8e>t<8e>riorer soudainement. En Belgique, le cot du vieillissement, estim<8e> par le CEV, devrait augmenter de 5,6 points de PIB entre 2010 et 2060. Le poids des pensions dans cette <8e>volution est le plus important, suivi par les d<8e>penses de soins de sant<8e>. Les effets de la crise <8e>conomique et financi<8f>re sont venus renforcer la menace que le vieillissement de la population implique exer<8d>ait d<8e>j<88> sur la soutenabilit<8e> des finances publiques. Le risque d<d5>une crise de confiance, qui serait p<8e>nalisante <88> la fois pour la reprise <8e>conomique et pour les finances publiques, est <8e>lev<8e>, particuli<8f>rement dans certains pays. Il importe donc de restaurer la confiance dans la soutenabilit<8e> budg<8e>taire <88> long terme. Dans ce contexte, des r<8e>formes importantes des syst<8f>mes de pension dans les pays qui, comme la Belgique, n<d5>ont r<8e>form<8e> que mod<8e>r<8e>ment, sont plus que jamais n<8e>cessaire. Leur concr<8e>tisation pourrait, par contre, <90>tre programm<8e>e et <8e>tal<8e>e dans le temps. Un <8e>l<8e>ment important, <88> cet <8e>gard, est de relever lge effectif de d<8e>part <88> la retraite, que ce soit par voie r<8e>glementaire ou incitative. Favoriser le deuxi<8f>me pilier des pensions peut faire partie de cette grande r<8e>forme. Le deuxi<8f>me pilier peut contribuer <88> un taux de remplacement tel que le niveau de vie ne diminue pas trop lors du d<8e>part <88> la retraite. Toutefois, il ne r<8e>sout pas le probl<8f>me de soutenabilit<8e> budg<8e>taire et ne r<8e>duit pas le risque de pauvret<8e> si les b<8e>n<8e>ficiaires de ce pilier demeurent les pensionn<8e>s ayant d<8e>j<88> une pension du premier pilier plus importante que la moyenne. Il faudra continuer <88> analyser les effets de la loi sur les pensions compl<8e>mentaires, puisque les premi<8f>res informations en la mati<8f>re indiquent une certaine d<8e>mocratisation. Jusqu'ici, celle.ci semble s'<90>tre surtout traduite par une hausse du taux de couverture des travailleurs <88> faibles revenus tandis que les montants des contributions devant permettre d'am<8e>liorer leurs moyens d'existence une fois <88> la retraite sont encore limit<8e>s. De larges marges d'am<8e>lioration existent donc encore, tant en termes de couverture que de montants octroy<8e>s dans le cadre du deuxi<8f>me pilier des pensions aux personnes dont les revenus sont les plus faibles. Title: Belgium and world trade: Why the decline? How can this be remedied?
text: BELGIUM AND WORLD TRADE: WHY THE SETBACK? HOW CAN THIS BE REMEDIED? ___________________________________ Speech by Mr Guy Quaden, Governor of the National Bank of Belgium, on the occasion of the General Assembly of ICC Belgium1 1 International Chamber of Commerce BNB EU Bil Quadri Pos_100pct of 3 May 2010 Ladies and Gentlemen, PP1 First of all, I would like to thank you for inviting me to this General Assembly and for giving me the opportunity to exchange with representatives of the business world some thoughts on recent trends in foreign trade. The institution I represent follows with great interest the developments in Belgium's trade, not only because we compile many statistics in this area but also and above all because of their importance for our economy. As you know, trade has contributed greatly to our country's current prosperity. As one of the first nations to have developed its industry, Belgium has been able to take full advantage of its favourable geographical location and the many free trade agreements concluded with our European partners since the second half of the nineteenth century. In this way, Belgium has secured both a supply of resources and access to large markets of opportunity. Thus, its importance in international trade has far exceeded that of its population or production. Even today, according to United Nations statistics, Belgium ranks 8th in merchandise trade, ahead of large countries such as Brazil and India. Of course, while it has helped to establish Belgium's economic prosperity, the very wide international openness of our economy makes it very sensitive to developments in the world economy. The "Great Recession" of 2008 and 2009 has just demonstrated it again: the decline of about 20 p.c. in exports and imports that we have experienced. in Belgium, following the collapse of international trade, between mid-2008 and mid-2009 resulted in a contraction of a similar magnitude in industrial production, and thus largely explains the 3 p.c. decrease in the level of our GDP over the past year. However, one of the reasons why this Great Recession did not turn into a Great Depression, as in the 1930s, was that the authorities learned the lessons of history, not only in terms of monetary or fiscal policies, but also by largely resisting the temptations of protectionism. Belgium will hopefully benefit from the recovery of the global economy and demand, which should gradually take shape, driven in particular by the economies of Asia. However, in order to take full advantage of it, it is important that our companies, mainly in industry, are able to maintain their place in external markets. In fact, the ability of Belgian companies to maintain their level of competitiveness has been a source of concern for some time now. In particular, they have crystallized around the evolution of market share indicators. The latter highlight a growth in Belgium's exports, which is, year after year, less sustained than that of imports from our main trading partners. PP2 Admittedly, some countries show results that are still lower than the annual export growth of 5.4 p.c. recorded in Belgium between 1995 and 2008. But other countries, yet facing the same external environment as us, and sharing the same currency, are performing better. Opting for a proactive and ambitious perspective, I consider, with others, that Belgium must aim for a place among the most dynamic European economies. On the other hand, at the same time, I am convinced that it has the means to achieve this ambition, building on its strengths in terms of human and technological skills. However, the results of the last fifteen years tend to show that the overall competitiveness of the economy, seen as its ability to adapt in order to take advantage of the upheavals in the outside world, needs to be strengthened. It is on this aspect, crucial for a small and very open country like Belgium, that I wish to take stock today. Belgium's position in a rapidly changing environment PP3 This requires a global context that has been marked by major changes over the past two decades, particularly as a result of falling transport costs, the technological revolution in the field of information and communication and a wave of liberalization of trade and capital movements in several parts of the world, especially the countries of the former Eastern bloc and China. In a short period of time, these countries, whose productive apparatus has also been strengthened by foreign investment, have become essential trading partners for advanced economies. On the one hand, because of their size and strong growth, they are opportunities that need to be exploited. On the other hand, these countries are able to supply developed countries with large quantities of consumer and intermediate goods at a lower cost. As such, they therefore represent competitors for domestic producers. PP4 These developments were particularly marked in the case of China, whose share of world exports tripled in the space of fifteen years. The emergence of these new economic poles has been accompanied by an in-depth reorganization of production methods. Under the influence of multinational enterprises in particular, the different stages of production - from initial development to production and then final distribution - are increasingly distributed among different locations, depending on the efficiency advantages that each of them offers. PP5 Supported by the growing importance of intra-industry and intra-firm trade, this dual movement of emergence of new economic poles and fragmentation of the production chain has led to a considerable acceleration of world trade. Over the past two decades, it has grown by an average of 5.8 p.c. per year, twice as fast as output growth. The rapid development of emerging economies, which relies heavily on their increasing participation in international trade, is fundamentally positive. It is a potential factor in raising income and reducing poverty for a considerable proportion of the world's population. However, in addition to the challenges it poses to natural resources and the environment, it requires companies in developed economies to make adaptation efforts. First of all, adapt to the opportunities offered by new outlets, by directing their international activities more towards the countries in which the demand for imported goods is growing most strongly. Then adapt to the arrival of new competitors who not only benefit from an abundant and cheaper workforce, but who also increasingly use advanced technologies. The strategy that needs to be implemented to deal with this is well known: companies must orient their activities towards the production of goods that are less standardised and incorporate to a greater extent scientific or technical innovations, with the aim of exploiting market niches that are more isolated from competition. PP6 However, the statistics available to us tend to indicate that the Belgian economy is struggling to keep up with these developments. This is evidenced by the continued decline in its share of world trade from 3 per cent in 1995 to 2.4 per cent in 2009. Admittedly, most advanced economies have also suffered losses in market share. All in all, this reflects the rise of emerging economies and the growth of their share in world trade. However, it is clear that some countries are better than others, and better than Belgium, at preserving their place in world trade. What competitiveness for the Belgian economy? The question that arises is therefore to identify the handicaps that could explain Belgium's greater loss of market share. In this respect, it is now established that the competitiveness of an economy covers a wide range of elements. Alongside the price and cost aspects, which remain very important for the positioning of the economy in relation to partners with comparable structural characteristics, more intangible factors also determine the economy's ability to offer goods and services that stand out for their quality, innovativeness, or attractive image in the eyes of consumers. PP7 Recent analyses show that Belgian exporters have relatively little control over pricing. These are largely determined by market conditions, especially for relatively standardized products. In a context where sales prices are given, the control of wage costs must not be neglected, otherwise the profitability of export activities will be weighed on and, in the long term, their sustainability threatened. In addition, wage costs are a determinant of the level of employment and attractiveness to foreign investors. While it is obviously illusory to try to compete with emerging economies in this respect, it is important to ensure that deviations from labour costs in our main neighbours are limited. In this respect, calculated using 1996 as a starting point, the handicap in the evolution of hourly wage costs in the private sector would amount to 3.5 p.c. in 2009, according to the estimate of the CCE secretariat. This difference is essentially the result of the widening gap with Germany, which, as is well known, has pursued a policy of major wage moderation in recent years. Beyond cost competitiveness, the explanation for Belgium's loss of market share also lies largely in so-called structural factors, relating to geographical orientation and product-specific specialisation of exports. PP8 It appears from the comparison with other European countries that Belgium's exports suffer from concentration on nearby markets  and therefore from an insufficient presence on those further away and with strong growth. In 2008 the countries which, together with Belgium, formed the European Union of Fifteen, before its enlargement to include the countries of Central and Eastern Europe, still accounted for a share of 71.7 p.c. in Belgium's exports, compared with 1.2 for China and 4.9 p.c. for the emerging countries of Europe. However, with the exception of Japan, it was in the EU15 that the growth in import demand was the weakest among the various economic zones of the world. While there has been a shift in reorientation over the past 15 years, it has remained more timid than in other countries. PP9 On the other hand, the goods presented for export by Belgian producers comprise a significant proportion of products whose demand is not very dynamic. These include, for example, road vehicles, glass products or textile products. On the contrary, capital goods or high-tech equipment are generally under-represented in exports. Beyond the presence on relatively less dynamic markets, the specialization of goods from relatively intensive production in capital factor or labour factor exposes Belgian exporters to the pressure of new producers. Indeed, it is on this type of products that competition from emerging countries is increasingly important, since they are endowed with considerable reserves of labor and, increasingly, equipment comparable to those available here. Not surprisingly, it is for this type of product that Belgian exporters suffer significant losses in market share, as can be seen in particular by examining the evolution of exports to our two main outlet markets, namely Germany and France. Growth in the volume of road vehicle exports, for example, was extremely low, averaging 1 per cent per year between 1995 and 2007 to Germany and 1.6 per cent to France. This weakness is largely the result of a reorientation of the demand of our traditional partners for this type of goods towards new vehicle producers from outside the Europe of the Fifteen. On the other hand, the demand addressed to their European partners for more knowledge-intensive products, such as medicines, has been very vigorous. PP10 The development of the pharmaceutical sector has therefore made it possible to support Belgium's export performance. However, the base of products incorporating research and innovation is expected to widen further in Belgium's export basket. Indeed, while R&D-intensive goods now account for a larger share of exports than they did fifteen years ago, we are still lagging behind in products incorporating cutting-edge innovations, such as electrical and electronic equipment. Innovation surveys show that while a relatively high proportion of Belgian companies market products and services incorporating existing innovations, only a very small proportion of them manage to put completely new products on the market on sale. Some examples of success, however, show us the way forward. Conclusion PP11 The main lesson to be learned from all this is that a company's success in foreign markets is no coincidence. It depends above all on its ability to meet existing demand and sufficiently stand out from the supply of its competitors, especially those who benefit from lower production costs. In addition, in addition to trade in goods, globalization offers opportunities for our companies to showcase their know-how in the fields of infrastructure, energy, or other areas of services for which the needs are important and their competence widely recognized. Naturally, factors of geographical proximity or specialization will continue to play an important role. The long-standing links forged by current exporters with their trading partners and the experience accumulated in the various production chains must serve as a basis for establishing a presence on foreign markets. In this context, a controlled evolution of costs  whether wages or other production costs  is a necessary condition. But this base must also be broadened, on the one hand by encouraging these companies to explore new markets and offer new products, and on the other hand by encouraging new vocations as exporters. In this respect, studies carried out at firm level show that export activities, as well as innovation activities, are largely concentrated in large enterprises. The largest and most productive companies are, in fact, better able to bear the sunk fixed costs inherent in them. However, once this threshold is exceeded, strategies based on research and development of new products and on commercialization across borders increase opportunities for business growth. Therefore, initiatives - public or private or mixed - allowing a wider dissemination of innovation throughout the fabric of enterprises must be encouraged. More broadly, the foundations on which the external competitiveness of the economy is based are largely the same as those necessary to ensure the overall development of the economy in a structural and sustainable manner and to guarantee the prosperity of the population. It is therefore a shared responsibility of public authorities, education and research, entrepreneurs and workers to take action in this direction. Thank you for your attention.

COMMENT Y REM<83>DIER? ___________________________________ Discours prononc<8e> par Monsieur Guy Quaden, Gouverneur de la Banque nationale de Belgique, <88> l'occasion de l'assembl<8e>e g<8e>n<8e>rale de l'ICC Belgium1 1 International Chamber of Commerce BNB EU Bil Quadri Pos_100pct du 3 mai 2010 Mesdames, Messieurs, PP1 Je voudrais tout d'abord vous remercier de m'avoir convi<8e> <88> cette assembl<8e>e g<8e>n<8e>rale et de me donner ainsi l'occasion d'<8e>changer avec des repr<8e>sentants du monde de l'entreprise quelques r<8e>flexions sur les tendances r<8e>centes du commerce ext<8e>rieur. L'institution que je repr<8e>sente suit avec beaucoup d'int<8e>r<90>t les d<8e>veloppements des <8e>changes commerciaux de la Belgique, non seulement parce que nous <8e>tablissons de nombreuses statistiques en la mati<8f>re mais <8e>galement et surtout en raison de leur importance pour notre <8e>conomie. Comme vous le savez, les <8e>changes commerciaux ont grandement contribu<8e> <88> la prosp<8e>rit<8e> actuelle de notre pays. <83>tant l'une des premi<8f>res nations <88> avoir d<8e>velopp<8e> son industrie, la Belgique a su largement tirer parti de sa situation g<8e>ographique favorable et des nombreux trait<8e>s de libre <8e>change conclus avec nos partenaires europ<8e>ens, et ce depuis la seconde moiti<8e> du XIX<8f>me si<8f>cle. De cette mani<8f>re, la Belgique s<d5>est assur<8e> <88> la fois un approvisionnement en ressources et un acc<8f>s <88> de vastes march<8e>s de d<8e>bouch<8e>s. Ainsi, son importance dans les <8e>changes commerciaux internationaux a largement d<8e>pass<8e> celle de sa population ou de sa production. Aujourd<d5>hui encore, la Belgique occupe selon les statistiques des Nations Unies le 8<8f>me rang dans le commerce de marchandises, devan<8d>ant des pays de grande taille, comme le Br<8e>sil ou l<d5>Inde. Bien entendu, si elle a permis d<d5>asseoir la prosp<8e>rit<8e> <8e>conomique de la Belgique, la tr<8f>s large ouverture internationale de notre <8e>conomie rend celle-ci tr<8f>s sensible aux d<8e>veloppements de l'<8e>conomie mondiale. La <c7> Grande R<8e>cession <c8> de 2008 et 2009 vient encore de le d<8e>montrer: le repli d'environ 20 p.c. des exportations et des importations que nous avons connu en Belgique, suite <88> l'effondrement du commerce international, entre la mi-2008 et la mi-2009 s'est traduit par une contraction d'une ampleur similaire de la production industrielle, et explique donc en grande partie la diminution de 3 p.c. du niveau de notre PIB au cours de l'ann<8e>e derni<8f>re. La Belgique va esp<8e>rons-le, b<8e>n<8e>ficier de la reprise de lconomie et de la demande mondiales qui devrait se profiler progressivement, sous l'impulsion notamment des <8e>conomies d'Asie. Toutefois, afin d'en profiter pleinement, il importe que nos entreprises, principalement dans l'industrie, soient en mesure de conserver la place qu<d5>elles occupent sur les march<8e>s ext<8e>rieurs. De fait, la capacit<8e> des entreprises belges <88> pr<8e>server leur niveau de comp<8e>titivit<8e> suscite, depuis quelques temps d<8e>j<88>, de nombreuses inqui<8e>tudes. Ces derniers mettent en <8e>vidence une croissance des exportations de la Belgique qui est, ann<8e>e apr<8f>s ann<8e>e, moins soutenue que celle des importations de nos principaux partenaires commerciaux. PP2 Certes, certains pays pr<8e>sentent des r<8e>sultats encore inf<8e>rieurs <88> la croissance annuelle des exportations de 5,4 p.c. enregistr<8e>e en Belgique entre 1995 et 2008. Mais d<d5>autres pays, pourtant confront<8e>s au m<90>me environnement ext<8e>rieur que nous, et partageant la m<90>me monnaie, obtiennent des performances meilleures. Optant pour une perspective volontariste et ambitieuse, , je consid<8f>re, avec d'autres, que la Belgique doit viser une place parmi les <8e>conomies europ<8e>ennes les plus dynamiques. D<d5>autre part, dans le m<90>me temps, je suis persuad<8e> qu<d5>elle a les moyens de r<8e>aliser cette ambition, en s<d5>appuyant sur ses atouts en mati<8f>re de comp<8e>tences humaines et technologiques. Toutefois, les r<8e>sultats des quinze derni<8f>res ann<8e>es tendent <88> montrer que la comp<8e>titivit<8e> globale de lconomie, consid<8e>r<8e>e comme <8e>tant son aptitude <88> s<d5>adapter pour tirer profit des bouleversements du monde ext<8e>rieur, doit <90>tre renforc<8e>e. C'est sur cet aspect, crucial pour un petit pays tr<8f>s ouvert comme la Belgique, que je souhaite faire le point aujourd'hui. Position de la Belgique dans un environnement en mutation rapide PP3 Il faut pour cela se situer dans un contexte mondial qui a <8e>t<8e> marqu<8e> par d'importantes mutations au cours des deux derni<8f>res d<8e>cennies, notamment <88> la suite de la diminution des co<9e>ts de transport, de la r<8e>volution technologique dans le domaine de l<d5>information et de la communication et d'une vague de la lib<8e>ralisation des <8e>changes commerciaux et des mouvements de capitaux dans plusieurs parties du monde, en particulier les pays de l'ancien bloc de l'Est et la Chine. En peu de temps, ces pays, dont l'appareil productif a par ailleurs <8e>t<8e> renforc<8e> par des investissements <8e>trangers, sont devenus des partenaires commerciaux incontournables pour les <8e>conomies avanc<8e>es. D'une part, du fait de leur taille et de leur croissance vigoureuse, ils constituent des d<8e>bouch<8e>s qu'il convient d'exploiter. D'autre part, ces pays sont en mesure de fournir aux pays d<8e>velopp<8e>s des grandes quantit<8e>s de biens de consommation et de biens interm<8e>diaires, et ce <88> moindre co<9e>t. <cb> ce titre, ils repr<8e>sentent donc des concurrents pour les producteurs nationaux. PP4 Ces <8e>volutions ont <8e>t<8e> particuli<8f>rement marqu<8e>es dans le cas de la Chine, dont la part dans les exportations mondiales a tripl<8e> en l<d5>espace d<d5>une petite quinzaine d<d5>ann<8e>e. L'<8e>mergence de ces nouveaux p<99>les <8e>conomiques s'est accompagn<8e>e d'une r<8e>organisation en profondeur des modes de production. Sous l'influence notamment des entreprises multinationales, les diff<8e>rentes <8e>tapes de la production - du d<8e>veloppement initial <88> la production puis la distribution finale - sont de plus en plus largement r<8e>parties entre diff<8e>rentes localisations, en fonction des avantages que chacune d'elles offrent en mati<8f>re d'efficience. PP5 Soutenu par l'importance grandissante du commerce intra-branche et intra-firme, ce double mouvement d'<8e>mergence de nouveaux p<99>les <8e>conomiques et de fragmentation de la cha<94>ne de production a donn<8e> lieu <88> une acc<8e>l<8e>ration consid<8e>rable du commerce mondial. Au cours des vingt derni<8f>res ann<8e>es, il a progress<8e> de 5,8 p.c. par an en moyenne, soit un rythme deux fois plus rapide que la croissance de la production. Le d<8e>veloppement rapide des <8e>conomies <8e>mergentes, qui s<d5>appuie largement sur leur participation croissante aux <8e>changes internationaux, est fondamentalement positif. Il constitue un facteur potentiel de rel<8f>vement du revenu, et de recul de la pauvret<8e>, pour une proportion consid<8e>rable de la population mondiale. Toutefois, outre les d<8e>fis qu<d5>il pose en mati<8f>re de ressources naturelles et d<d5>environnement, il impose aux entreprises des <8e>conomies d<8e>velopp<8e>es des efforts d'adaptation. S'adapter tout d'abord aux opportunit<8e>s offertes par de nouveaux d<8e>bouch<8e>s, en orientant davantage leurs activit<8e>s internationales vers les pays dans lesquels la demande pour des biens import<8e>s cro<94>t le plus fortement. S'adapter ensuite <88> l'arriv<8e>e de nouveaux concurrents qui b<8e>n<8e>ficient non seulement d'une main-d<d5><cf>uvre abondante et meilleur march<8e>, mais qui recourent aussi de plus en plus <88> des technologies avanc<8e>es. La strat<8e>gie qui doit <90>tre mise en <cf>uvre pour y faire face est bien connue: les entreprises doivent orienter leurs activit<8e>s vers la production de biens moins standardis<8e>s et incorporant dans une plus large mesure des innovations scientifiques ou techniques, dans le but d'exploiter des niches de march<8e> plus isol<8e>es de la concurrence. PP6 Pourtant, les statistiques dont nous disposons tendent <88> indiquer que l'<8e>conomie belge peine <88> s'inscrire dans ces <8e>volutions. En t<8e>moigne la r<8e>duction continue de sa part dans le commerce mondial, qui est pass<8e>e de 3 p.c. en 1995 <88> 2,4 p.c. en 2009. Certes, la plupart des <8e>conomies avanc<8e>es ont aussi subi des pertes de parts de march<8e>. Cela est somme toute le reflet de la mont<8e>e en puissance des <8e>conomies <8e>mergentes et de la croissance de leur part dans le commerce mondial. Force est toutefois de constater que certains pays parviennent mieux que d<d5>autres, et mieux que la Belgique, <88> pr<8e>server leur place dans le commerce mondial. Quelle comp<8e>titivit<8e> pour lconomie belge ? La question qui se pose est d<8f>s lors d'identifier les handicaps qui pourraient expliquer les pertes de parts de march<8e> plus importantes de la Belgique. <cb> cet <8e>gard, il est d<8e>sormais <8e>tabli que la comp<8e>titivit<8e> d'une <8e>conomie couvre un large faisceau d'<8e>l<8e>ments. Parall<8f>lement aux aspects de prix et de co<9e>ts, qui demeurent tr<8f>s importants pour le positionnement de l'<8e>conomie par rapport aux partenaires disposant de caract<8e>ristiques structurelles comparables, des facteurs plus intangibles d<8e>terminent <8e>galement la capacit<8e> de l'<8e>conomie <88> offrir des biens et services qui se d<8e>marquent par leur qualit<8e>, leur caract<8f>re innovant, ou par leur image attrayante aux yeux des consommateurs. PP7 Les analyses r<8e>centes montrent que les exportateurs belges ont relativement peu de prise en mati<8f>re de fixation des prix. Ceux-ci sont largement d<8e>termin<8e>s par les conditions du march<8e>, en particulier pour les produits relativement standardis<8e>s. Dans un contexte o<9d> les prix de vente sont donn<8e>s, la ma<94>trise des co<9e>ts salariaux ne doit pas <90>tre n<8e>glig<8e>e, sous peine de peser sur la rentabilit<8e> des activit<8e>s d'exportation et, <88> terme, de menacer leur p<8e>rennit<8e>. Par ailleurs, les co<9e>ts salariaux sont un d<8e>terminant du niveau d<d5>emploi et de l<d5>attractivit<8e> vis-<88>-vis des investisseurs <8e>trangers. S'il est <8e>videmment illusoire de tenter de concurrencer les <8e>conomies <8e>mergentes sur ce plan, il importe de faire en sorte de limiter les <8e>carts par rapport aux co<9e>ts du travail en vigueur chez nos principaux voisins. <cb> cet <8e>gard, calcul<8e> en prenant 1996 comme point de d<8e>part, le handicap dans l'<8e>volution des co<9e>ts salariaux horaires dans le secteur priv<8e> s'<8e>l<8f>verait <88> 3,5 p.c. en 2009, selon l'estimation du secr<8e>tariat du CCE. Cette diff<8e>rence r<8e>sulte essentiellement de l'<8e>cart qui s'est creus<8e> par rapport <88> l'Allemagne, qui, comme l'on sait, a poursuivi ces derni<8f>res ann<8e>es une politique de grande mod<8e>ration salariale. Au-del<88> de la comp<8e>titivit<8e>-co<9e>t, l'explication des pertes de parts de march<8e> de la Belgique r<8e>side aussi largement dans des facteurs dits structurels, portant sur l'orientation g<8e>ographique et la sp<8e>cialisation par produit des exportations. PP8 Il ressort en effet de la comparaison avec les autres pays europ<8e>ens que les exportations de la Belgique souffrent d'une concentration sur les march<8e>s proches <d0> et donc d'une pr<8e>sence insuffisante sur ceux plus <8e>loign<8e>s et <88> forte croissance. En 2008 les pays qui, avec la Belgique, formaient l'Union europ<8e>enne des Quinze, avant l'<8e>largissement de celle-ci aux pays d'Europe centrale et orientale, repr<8e>sentaient encore une part de 71,7 p.c. dans les exportations de la Belgique, contre 1,2 pour la Chine et 4,9 p.c. pour les pays <8e>mergents d'Europe. Or, <88> l'exception du Japon, c'est dans l'UE15 que la croissance de la demande d'importation a <8e>t<8e> la plus faible parmi les diff<8e>rentes zones <8e>conomiques du monde. Un mouvement de r<8e>orientation est certes survenu au cours des 15 derni<8f>res ann<8e>es, mais il est rest<8e> plus timide que dans d'autres pays. PP9 D'autre part, les biens pr<8e>sent<8e>s <88> l'exportation par les producteurs belges comprennent pour une part importante des produits dont la demande est peu dynamique. Il s'agit par exemple des v<8e>hicules routiers, des produits du verre ou des produits textiles. Au contraire, les biens d'<8e>quipement ou les appareillages de haute technologie sont de mani<8f>re g<8e>n<8e>rale sous-repr<8e>sent<8e>s dans les exportations. Au del<88> de la pr<8e>sence sur des march<8e>s relativement moins dynamique, la sp<8e>cialisation des biens issus de productions relativement intensives en facteur capital ou en facteur travail exposent les exportateurs belges <88> la pression des nouveaux producteurs. En effet, c'est sur ce type de produits que la concurrence des pays <8e>mergents est de plus en plus en importante, puisqu'ils sont dot<8e>s de r<8e>serves de main-d'<cf>uvre consid<8e>rables et, de mani<8f>re croissante, d'<8e>quipements comparables <88> ceux disponibles chez nous. Sans surprise, c'est pour ce type de produits que les exportateurs belges subissent des pertes de parts de march<8e> importantes, comme on peut notamment le constater en examinant l'<8e>volution des exportations vers nos deux principaux march<8e>s de d<8e>bouch<8e>, <88> savoir l'Allemagne et la France. La croissance du volume des exportations de v<8e>hicules routiers, par exemple, y a <8e>t<8e> extr<90>mement faible, s'<8e>levant <88> 1 p.c. par an en moyenne entre 1995 et 2007 vers l'Allemagne et <88> 1,6 p.c. vers la France. Cette faiblesse r<8e>sulte largement d'une r<8e>orientation de la demande de nos partenaires traditionnels pour ce type de biens vers de nouveaux producteurs de v<8e>hicules, originaires de l'ext<8e>rieur de l'Europe des Quinze. A contrario, la demande adress<8e>e <88> leurs partenaires europ<8e>ens pour des produits plus intensifs en connaissance, comme les m<8e>dicaments, a <8e>t<8e> quant <88> elle tr<8f>s vigoureuse. PP10 Le d<8e>veloppement du secteur pharmaceutique a donc permis de soutenir les performances <88> l'exportation de la Belgique. Toutefois, la base des produits incorporant de la recherche et des innovations devrait encore s'<8e>largir dans le panier des exportations de la Belgique. En effet, si les biens intensifs en recherche et en d<8e>veloppement repr<8e>sentent maintenant une proportion plus importante dans les exportations que ce n'<8e>tait le cas il y a une quinzaine d'ann<8e>es, nous accusons encore un retard en ce qui concerne les produits incorporant des innovations de pointe, comme les <8e>quipements <8e>lectriques et <8e>lectroniques. Il ressort des enqu<90>tes sur l'innovation que si une fraction relativement <8e>lev<8e>e des entreprises belges commercialise des produits et des services incorporant des innovations existantes, seule une tr<8f>s faible proportion d'entre elles parvient <88> mettre en vente des produits totalement nouveaux sur le march<8e>. Certains exemples de succ<8f>s, nous montrent cependant la voie <88> suivre. Conclusion PP11 Le principal enseignement qu'il faut retirer de tout ceci est que le succ<8f>s d'une entreprise sur les march<8e>s ext<8e>rieurs n'est pas le fruit du hasard. Il d<8e>pend avant tout de sa capacit<8e> <88> r<8e>pondre <88> une demande existante et se d<8e>marquer suffisamment de l'offre de ses concurrents, en particulier ceux qui sont avantag<8e>s par des co<9e>ts de production moins <8e>lev<8e>s. Par ailleurs, outre les <8e>changes de marchandises, la mondialisation offre des opportunit<8e>s pour nos entreprises de faire valoir leur savoir-faire dans les domaines des infrastructures, de l'<8e>nergie, ou dans d'autres domaines des services pour lesquels les besoins sont importants et leur comp<8e>tence largement reconnue. Naturellement, les facteurs de proximit<8e> g<8e>ographique ou de sp<8e>cialisation continueront de jouer un r<99>le important. Les liens tiss<8e>s de longue date par les exportateurs actuels avec leurs partenaires commerciaux et l'exp<8e>rience accumul<8e>e dans les diff<8e>rentes fili<8f>res de production doivent servir de base pour asseoir la pr<8e>sence sur les march<8e>s ext<8e>rieurs. Dans ce cadre, une <8e>volution ma<94>tris<8e>e des co<9e>ts <d0> qu<d5>il s<d5>agisse des salaires ou des autres co<9e>ts de production <d0> constitue une condition n<8e>cessaire. Mais il convient aussi d'<8e>largir cette base, d'une part en incitant ces entreprises <88> explorer de nouveaux march<8e>s et <88> proposer de nouveaux produits, et d'autre part en suscitant des nouvelles vocations d'exportateurs. <cb> cet <8e>gard, les <8e>tudes r<8e>alis<8e>es au niveau des firmes montrent que les activit<8e>s d'exportation, de m<90>me d'ailleurs que les activit<8e>s d'innovation, sont largement concentr<8e>es dans les grandes entreprises. Les entreprises les plus grandes et les plus productives sont, en effet, mieux <88> m<90>me de supporter les co<9e>ts fixes irr<8e>cup<8e>rables qui leur sont inh<8e>rents. Toutefois, une fois ce seuil d<8e>pass<8e>, les strat<8e>gies bas<8e>es sur la recherche et le d<8e>veloppement de nouveaux produits et sur la commercialisation <88> l'ext<8e>rieur des fronti<8f>res, accroissent les possibilit<8e>s de croissance des entreprises. D<8f>s lors, les initiatives - publiques ou priv<8e>es ou mixtes - permettant une plus large diffusion de l'innovation dans l'ensemble du tissu des entreprises doivent <90>tre encourag<8e>es. Plus largement, les assises sur lesquelles se fonde la comp<8e>titivit<8e> externe de l'<8e>conomie sont en grande partie les m<90>mes que celles n<8e>cessaires pour assurer de mani<8f>re structurelle et soutenable le d<8e>veloppement g<8e>n<8e>ral de l'<8e>conomie et pour garantir la prosp<8e>rit<8e> de la population. Il s'agit d<8f>s lors d'une responsabilit<8e> partag<8e>e des autorit<8e>s publiques, de l'enseignement et de la recherche, des entrepreneurs et des travailleurs, d'inscrire leur action dans ce sens. Je vous remercie pour votre attention.

Title: Governor's Introductory Statement
text: GENERAL ASSEMBLY 2010 INTRODUCTORY STATEMENT BY THE GOVERNOR Brussels, 2010-05-31 Ladies and Gentlemen, On my own behalf and on behalf of the other members of the Management Committee, I welcome you to this ordinary general meeting of shareholders of the National Bank of Belgium. As is tradition, I would like to begin this assembly by briefly mentioning some important changes that occurred or were announced in 2009, in particular the new reserve and dividend policy defined by the Regency Council in application of the law of 3 April 2009, as well as the will of the authorities of our country to modify the organization of the counter of the financial sector in Belgium. These two changes are important for the Bank and are intimately linked to two basic tasks of central banks, namely the issuance of banknotes and the safeguarding of financial stability. * * * It is the monopoly on the issue of banknotes entrusted by States to central banks that allows them to have the resources necessary for the implementation of monetary policy and other tasks of general interest entrusted to them. The counterpart of banknotes, which are recorded on the liabilities side of the central bank's balance sheet, consists of foreign exchange reserves and loans granted to commercial banks in the context of monetary policy, as assets on the balance sheet. The return on these assets, financed by unpaid liabilities in the form of bank notes, constitutes what is known as "seigniorage income". Thanks to the monopoly of the issue of notes that the State grants it, the central bank therefore receives the income from seigniorage, which entails significant profits in relation to its needs. That is why, everywhere, the regime of central banks ensures that the surplus of their income goes to the national state. In Belgium, the rule of revenue sharing between the Bank and the State was recently amended by Parliament, which led the Regency Council of the Bank to define a new reserve and dividend policy. As explicitly required by the explanatory memorandum to the Act of 3 April 2009, the Regency Council has defined a reserve and dividend policy to ensure that the distinct interests of the Bank (in particular its financial independence), shareholders and the sovereign State are all taken into account in a balanced manner. Shareholders now receive a second dividend equal to half of the net proceeds of the assets forming the counterpart of the previously reserved profits. The undistributed part of this product is itself set aside, together with other products for a much higher amount, so that in total a quarter of the profit to be distributed is paid into the available reserve. Shareholders thus have the prospect of a growing yield base for the setting of the dividend, this growth being largely financed by monetary income. As in the past, the dividend is largely protected against the volatility of the Bank's profit, which depends on the Eurosystem's monetary policy and exogenous factors such as demand for banknotes or exchange rate developments. The dividend is also guaranteed by the reserves. The State, as the sovereign State which has granted the issuing privilege, receives only the balance of the annual revenues in the last place. It is specified that this balance may in no case include a drawdown on the reserves or any part of the net proceeds of the portfolio which forms the counterpart of the reserves. Finally, the Regency Council decided to transfer an amount of 954 million from the provisions to the available reserve. The basis for calculating the dividend was significantly increased from the outset. * * * The financial crisis has led the authorities to re-examine the architecture of financial sector supervision in Belgium. It is known that the supervision of individual financial institutions and markets is the responsibility of the CBFA while the Bank is already in charge of macroprudential supervision, i.e. that of the overall stability of the national financial system. The crisis has shown that these missions are closely linked and has highlighted the need for clarification. For this reason, proposals were made last year to adapt the organization of the counter-attack of financial institutions and markets. Although no surveillance model can completely exclude the occurrence of financial crises, more and more countries are favouring the so-called "twin peaks" model. It provides that the central bank, already in charge of macroprudential supervision, is also responsible for counter-microprudentials, a separate body to ensure the proper functioning of markets, compliance with the conduct of business rules applicable to the supply of financial services and products, and the correct information and protection of the consumer of financial services. Such a two-pillar structure has many advantages. First, it facilitates the independent exercise of two important tasks, namely the maintenance of the soundness of financial institutions on the one hand, and the preservation of market integrity and consumer protection on the other. In addition, the centralisation of the microprudential and macroprudential components of supervision within a single institution allows a coherent view of all the risks facing financial institutions and facilitates the coordinated implementation of supervisory policy instruments. This structure also makes it possible to make the most of the assets available to central banks for the counter-risks. I am thinking in particular of their day-to-day relations with the money market, their participation in payment and settlement systems, their macroeconomic analyses, or their participation in the European Union in an integrated network of central banks. The Belgian authorities have opted for this dual structure and a law recently passed by Parliament provides for the transfer to the Bank, by 1 January 2011 at the latest, of the CBFA's powers in the field of counter-prudential supervision of credit institutions, insurance companies, stock exchange companies and various other types of financial institutions.
