Title: Farewell speech for Guy Quaden
text: Brussels, 30 March 2011. Farewell speech for Guy Quaden during the Bank's Board Luncheon Mr. Deputy Prime Minister, Dear Members and Honorary Members of the Bank's Administrative Bodies, Mr. Governor, Dear Guy This week, the Bank is taking leave of a Governor who, for nearly 23 years, has put his many talents at the service of our Institution. With these 23 years and 12 years as governor, Guy is, in terms of duration, in the leading position of the twenty governors that the Bank has known since its inception. He ranks 5th for the total duration and 6th for the duration of his term as governor. A long and fruitful career as a central banker. Yet there was nothing to predict this path at the beginning of his professional career. After his studies in economics in his hometown of Liege, Guy left in 1969 for Paris - he narrowly missed the barricades of May '68 but was able to sniff the revolutionary atmosphere - oil obtained a diple at the ecole pratique des hautes etudes de la Sorbonne. In 1973, he became a doctor of economics at the University of Liege. Guy clearly bet on an academic career and his exceptional qualities are already manifested through the very rapid course of academic scales: at the age of 23 in 1968, assistant; at the age of 29 in 1974 first assistant; three years later lecturer and in 1978, at the age of 33, full professor. As a professor, Guy is particularly interested in socio-economic issues and public finances. In 1984, his career took a new turn. Apart from economic theory he became increasingly interested in the real economy and especially economic policy: he was appointed President of the Central Council of the Economy. Its Liege origin is no stranger to this development: indeed since the early sixties (the period of Andre Renard) the tradition was that the presidency of this council was entrusted to an independent personality with very close links with the Liege principality. It is, without a doubt, especially his scientific training and his knowledge of the files that led Guy to this high responsibility in our socio-economic system, but I do not doubt it, also his sense of diplomacy. His election as Dean of the Faculty of Economics, Management and Social Sciences in 1987 was the provisional culmination of the career of a man whose remarkable intellectual and didactic qualities made him particularly fit to remain a full-time professor. Guy Quaden will continue in the professorship, but from from 1988 as extraordinary teacher. For many generations of students, he will remain above all the enthusiastic Professor Quaden. From the beginning of August 1988, his professional career continued the turn begun by the Central Council of the Economy, with increased attention to the real economy, as Guy found his way to the National Bank of Belgium. I imagine that his great friendship with Roger Ramaekers, who was at the time Regent at the Bank as a representative of the cooperative world of consumption, has something to do with it, but it was Guy Spitaels, president of the PS at the time who appointed him to succeed Roland Beauvois in the direction of the Bank. By Royal Decree of 20 July 1988 Guy was appointed Director of the Bank, not an obvious succession because Mr Beauvois had a notorious reputation on the Bank. Among other things, he was the mastermind behind the resistance against the devaluation of the Belgian Franc that put the Bank in a bad light for years. As a member of the Executive Committee, Guy Quaden was responsible for the Departments of Accounting and Budget Control and Printing and the Main Treasury and Security departments. Guy Quaden becomes a pragmatic central banker in addition to being a professor. As an intellectual, however, he has always wanted to base his actions on an in-depth analysis that could stand the test of scientific criticism. In the nineties of the last century, Belgium was preparing for its entry into the Eurozone. From 1996 to 1999, Director Quaden became known to the general public, as Commissioner-General for the Euro. In this capacity, he was not only the coordinator of the many initiatives that the Bank itself had to undertake for this purpose, but also the strategist who had to convince many bodies to prepare for the arrival of the Euro in a joint approach. After our country became a member of the Eurozone on 1 January 1999, the Bank said goodbye to its then Governor, Mr Alfons Verplaetse, and Mr Guy Quaden was appointed Governor of our institution, with effect from 1 March 1999. Governor Quaden was able to start his task with a largely new and expanded Executive Committee. On the eve of the twenty-first century, the challenges were great and numerous. Both the Governing Bodies of the Bank and the departments and departments concerned had to adapt to the new division of tasks and working methods within the European System of Central Banks. These major structural adjustments were thoroughly prepared and went smoothly. The introduction of the euro cash in 2002 was also a success, not only because of the efforts of all parts of the Bank but also thanks, once again, to the excellent cooperation with all the social actors involved. More than ever, Mr Quaden's governorship adopted a diplomatic approach, in which there was room for mutual discussion. Governor Quaden wished that the Bank would not undergo the numerous and far-reaching changes in the environment in which it has to carry out its tasks reactively but would take a proactive approach. That is why ten years ago a start was made with the strategic exercises and the drawing up of the resulting master plans. With this method, which was completely new to the Bank at the time, the Management Board, its management and staff draw up an action plan which, in each medium term, defines the objectives to be achieved and the efforts to be made. This strategic approach led to major productivity gains. This also made it possible for the Bank to reduce its workforce by about a fifth during governor Quaden's term of office, while by no means reducing its tasks. In the 1990s, there was sometimes a fear that the Bank's activities would be reduced with the creation of the ECB. On the other hand, all activities, whether or not they fall within the scope of the ESCB, evolve. Never before has the Bank's expertise in monetary analysis and macroeconomic research been used so much. The tasks entrusted to the SNB by the public authorities are increasing. Our Institution also continues to advise the government: think of the recent study missions carried out as part of the formation of the federal government. Guy Quaden's mandates in Belgium are too numerous to mention. However, a few presidencies are particularly worth mentioning. He was Chairman of the Financial Stability Committee, the Supervisory Board of the Financial Services Authority, the CREFS, the Board of the Belgian-Luxembourg Foreign Exchange Institute, the Professional Association of Public Credit Institutions... It is also worth highlighting one federal institution, namely the Higher Council of Finance. Governor Quaden has always valued the important mission of the Supreme Council of Finance. In 1990, he became an active member. In 2006, he was appointed Vice-Chair of the Council, which was then renewed, and became Chair of the Study Committee on Aging. Not only could the economic and financial world appeal to Guy Quaden's commitment. Guy has also held senior positions in institutions pursuing broader social goals, such as the Carnegie Hero Fund and the King Baudouin Foundation. From the latter foundation he was the Chairman of the Board of Directors. As governor, he also assumed a growing number of international obligations. He is a member of the Governing Council and the General Council of the European Central Bank, and his thoughtful words are particularly listened to and taken into consideration. The international financial press very much appreciates the comments he gives at the end of each meeting of the Governing Council on the stance of monetary policy. He is also a Director of the Bank for International Settlements. At the global level, he serves as Governor of the International Monetary Fund and Alternate Governor of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Finance Corporation and the International Development Association. As in Brussels, the Governor served the interests of the Bank and our country, as well as those of the European and international community, in Frankfurt, Basel and Washington. Despite his many busy professional activities, Guy has also been committed to the well-being of the Bank's staff. Governor Quaden has always been an advocate of a personnel policy in which all employees are encouraged to develop their talents to the maximum. Like no other, he has encouraged the continuous efforts to train and restrain staff in view of the new tasks that are constantly emerging. Confidence in social dialogue, and thus in the ability of responsible people to solve problems through dialogue, has remained a constant in his social views. That is why Governor Quaden has always attached great importance to the representation of the social partners in the first advisory body of the Bank that the Council of Regency has always been. Governor Quaden was not only a skilled diplomat in many domestic and foreign cases. He also led the Bank as a "patron" in his own way. Governor Quaden's style was that of the captain of a team. Not only as a loyal supporter of Standard, he knew how important teamwork is. Thanks in part to the team spirit that has become an essential feature of our institution's corporate culture, the Bank has been able to adapt to its new missions in a quasi-effortless manner over the past twelve years. He also ensured the same team spirit and spirit of cooperation in the Executive Committee. In his letter of 24 February 2011 to the Minister of Finance, with which he made his mandate available from 1 April 2011, Governor Quaden refers to the great new challenge that awaits our Institution from next month, the integration of prudential control according to the Twin Peaks model. This extensive operation was also thoroughly prepared, in close cooperation with the Management and staff of both institutions involved. Governor Quaden can also look back on this preparatory file as a satisfied man. The highest authorities of our country have repeatedly expressed their admiration for the eminent re-eminent that the governor has played in the monetary and financial history of Belgium over the last decade. As a token of recognition, he received the title of Baron in 2007. At the end of February, on the occasion of the announcement of his departure, the federal government in turn paid tribute to the many merits of Guy Quaden. We take leave of a man endowed with great intelligence, diplomatic skills, an affable personality and an ability to present things affectionately. The governor remains in all circumstances a courteous man, attentive to his interlocutor. Many of those who have worked with him have expressed in recent days their respect for his great professional and human qualities. Our Institution takes leave of a man for whom the Anglo-Saxons have such a telling expression: "a gentleman". The Royal Decree of 27 February 2011 authorises him to bear the honorary title of his duties. Our Institution also wishes to offer him some gifts from the Management Bodies and staff. First, it awarded him the Bank's Gold Medal, the highest distinction she could bestow on resigning members of management. Mr. Governor, I hope that this gold medal will pleasantly remind you of the almost 23 years that you have been a member of the Executive Committee and the Boards of our Institution. It is also traditional for the Bank's Boards and staff to offer the resigning Governor a gift of his or her choice. That of Governor Quaden is original: no work of art or high-tech device, but a stay in New York. Guy intends to rent an apartment in New York to stay longer and discover the city in a more in-depth and relaxed way than he has done so far. We wish him an active stay in "the city that never sleeps". Mr. Governor, dear Guy, may we wish you in the coming years. We are convinced that you will continue to put your many intellectual and social talents at the service of the projects that are close to your heart. We wish you and all those dear to you many more years of happiness. Luc Coene.

text: Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders of 30 May 2011 INTRODUCTORY STATEMENT BY THE GOVERNOR Ladies and Gentlemen, On behalf of the Management Committee, I welcome you to this ordinary general meeting of shareholders of the National Bank of Belgium, which will be followed this year by an extraordinary general meeting to amend the institution's statutes. Amendments are necessary to bring our articles of association into line with the new European and Belgian rules on shareholder rights in listed companies. In addition, the opportunity was taken to propose the deletion or adaptation of other statutory provisions that had become obsolete. As is tradition, I would like to introduce this first Assembly by briefly mentioning some important changes that occurred or were announced in 2010, in particular, the new organisation of the counter-attack of the financial sector in Belgium. But first, I would like to pay tribute to my predecessor, Guy Quaden, who for nearly 23 years, including 12 years as governor, put his many talents at the service of the institution. A brilliant economist, he was appointed Director of the Bank in 1988, already having a rich academic career behind him. Appointed Commissioner-General for the Euro in 1996, he was one of the architects of Belgium's preparation for the single currency. In 1999, he became Governor of the Bank, which he headed for 12 years and whose structures and operations he had to adapt to his new European environment, in particular the creation of the European System of Central Banks. His intellectual and human qualities are unanimously recognized as well as the eminent re that Guy Quaden has played in the monetary and financial history of our country during the last decade. Director Praet will leave his position as Director at the National Bank tomorrow to become a member of the Executive Board of the European Central Bank. Doctor in economics, he has had a brilliant career in the academic and banking world. He was appointed Director of the Bank in 2000, a reappointment renewed in 2006. He was, among other things, responsible for international cooperation and the Financial Stability Department. Peter Praet has always shown in-depth knowledge of the issues he dealt with and great dynamism both in Belgium and in international for a. On behalf of myself and all my colleagues, I would like once again to express our gratitude for the work they have done over the many years. * * * It was following the financial crisis that followed the bankruptcy of the investment bank Lehman Brothers that the Belgian authorities examined the improvements to be made to the organisation of supervision in Belgium. They were therefore an extension of a more global reflection carried out at the international level. The choice fell on a two-pillar model, commonly known as "Twin Peaks", ole vs. prudential financial institutions is entrusted to an institution  usually the central bank  separate from the one that ensures the proper functioning of the markets and compliance with the rules of conduct with regard to customers. The Act of 2 July 2010 thus grants the National Bank the prudential counter-prudential measures, in particular of banks, insurance companies and stock exchange companies, while another institution  the Financial Services and Markets Authority (FSMA), which succeeds the Banking, Finance and Insurance Commission (CBFA)  is in charge of financial market control and consumer protection. This legislation involved the Bank taking over, from 1 April 2011, part of the activities and staff of the CBFA. Such a structure has many advantages. First, it separates two important missions: maintaining the soundness of financial institutions on the one hand, preserving market integrity and protecting consumers on the other. In addition, the centralisation of the micro and macro-prudential components of supervision within a single institution allows for a coherent view of all the risks facing financial institutions and the sector as a whole. This structure also makes it possible to make the most of the assets available to central banks for the counter-risks. I am thinking in particular of their day-to-day relations with the money market, their participation in payment and settlement systems, their economic analyses and their European network. This reform is in line with the dominant model in Europe and the consolidation of micro and macro prudential supervision within central banks is also justified by the function of "lender of last resort" of the latter, a mission that took on its full meaning during the serious liquidity crisis of September 2008. The FSMA, independent of the NBB, will be responsible for the supervision of financial markets and listed companies, as well as the countermeasures of financial products and services placed on the market and the correct application of the rules of conduct by financial institutions vis-a-vis their customers. It will also have more extensive powers in the areas of information and protection of the consumer of financial services. * * * During the past year, the SNB has carried out many other activities arising from the tasks entrusted to it by the Belgian and European legislators. The first part of the Corporate Report that has been given to you presents the most striking ones. It is followed by the presentation of the annual report for 2010 and the annual accounts. The content and presentation of the management report have been modified in accordance with the law of 6 April 2010 aimed in particular at strengthening corporate governance in listed companies and autonomous public companies. Since the 2009 accounting year, the presentation of the annual accounts, for its part, takes into account the law of 3 April 2009 which modified the Bank's income sharing rules. From the same financial year, a new reserve and dividend policy is thus applied. Shareholders receive a dividend equal to half of the net proceeds of the assets that form the counterpart of the reserved profits. The undistributed portion of this product is itself set aside, along with other products, so that a total of one quarter of the profit to be allocated is paid into the available reserve. Shareholders thus have the prospect of a growing yield base for the setting of the dividend, this growth being also financed by monetary income. Only in the last place does the State receive the balance of the annual revenues to which it is entitled as the sovereign State which has granted the issuing privilege. It is specified that this balance may in no case include a drawdown on the reserves or any part of the net proceeds of the portfolio which forms the counterpart of the reserves. * * * I propose that we now turn to the detailed presentation of the annual accounts for the financial year 2010. This presentation will already answer some of the questions we have Received. The remaining questions will be addressed in the question and answer session that will follow. I would like to thank the shareholders who sent us their questions in advance and in writing, thus facilitating the preparation and smooth running of this meeting. The answers to the questions relating to the proposed amendments to the articles of association will be provided during the extraordinary general meeting. Thank you for your attention. I now give the floor to Director De Wachter, who will comment on the annual accounts for the financial year 2010.

Title: Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders
text: Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders of 29 May 2012 INTRODUCTORY STATEMENT BY THE GOVERNOR Ladies and Gentlemen, On behalf of the Management Committee, I welcome you to this ordinary general meeting of shareholders of the National Bank of Belgium. At last year's extraordinary general meeting, the Bank's statutes were amended, on the one hand to bring them into line with a series of Belgian and European rules on the organisation of general meetings, and on the other hand to make some practical changes. One of these changes was to adjust the start time of the assembly, which this year opens for the first time at 2 p.m. instead of 11 a.m. as was the case before. To take part in the general meeting, shareholders are no longer required to have their shares blocked until the end of the meeting. From now on, they must have it established, on a given registration date, that they own their shares, and notify the Bank. As this new rule applies for the first time this year, the Bank has decided to consider with the necessary flexibility requests to participate in today's meeting. I would like to introduce this House by briefly referring to the important changes that the Bank underwent in 2011. It was indeed a year that can be described as historic, since it saw the Bank take full charge of the microprudential supervision business. The financial crisis that has been raging since 2008 has clearly highlighted the need to improve the organization and practice of counter-against financial institutions. At both European and Belgian level, the authorities have had to rethink these in depth. As early as 2010, inspired by developments in several countries of the European Union and based on the recommendations of the Special Commission for the Financial and Banking Crisis and the Lamfalussy Committee, the Belgian authorities decided to change the counterpart of the financial sector, and more specifically the interaction between the Bank and the former Banking Commission, financial and insurance (CBFA), towards a bipolar model, known as the "twin peaks" model. The Royal Decree of 3 March 2011 finally entrusted the Bank with all the functions of macroprudential and microprudential counter-supervision for banks and insurance companies. This order came into force on April 1, 2011. This date therefore marks a major turning point in the history of our company, because it is accompanied by the resumption of a profession of great importance for society as a whole. This is therefore a significant challenge for the Bank. Indeed, by taking over the prudential counter, we had the duty to make it benefit from the expertise, skills and data present at the Bank. We therefore had to promote transversality and the flow of information, which is a crucial issue in this area. In prudential matters, we have, after a collegial reflection, opted for an organizational model based on the application of the principle of double counters, which combines the vertical approach with the horizontal approach. Vertical analyses are conducted by counter-operational teams. These assess the company as a whole and coordinate the cons on the basis of a risk analysis and a counter plan for each establishment. At the same time, the horizontal analysis of the entire sector, and of each distinct type of risk, focuses on identifying risks and vulnerabilities from a cross-cutting perspective. This integrated risk assessment process is also supported by the Bank's other entities, which provide the counter-prudential with their expertise in macroeconomic analysis or their knowledge of financial markets. Concretely, five autonomous services are responsible for the exercise of the counter. The Counter-Prudential and Financial Stability Service defines prudential policy, identifies vulnerabilities, in particular systemic vulnerabilities, and carries out horizontal analyses of the sector and the different types of risks, as well as their interactions. This department is responsible for the horizontal dimension of the counter. The operational counter is exercised by the three autonomous services responsible respectively for the against banks and stock exchange companies, against insurance and reinsurance companies, and against market infrastructures. These services are responsible for the vertical dimension of the counter. A fifth department is responsible for transversal operational functions for the benefit of the other operational services. In order to ensure that the new counter model works effectively and that information flows optimally, three consultation forums have been set up within the Bank. They testify to the effort made to concretize the transversality of approaches, the exchange of information and the basic principle of double counters. The transfer of the prudential counterpart led us to integrate nearly 200 employees previously employed by the CBFA. They were transferred to the Bank to ensure the continuity of the counter. In order to ensure the effectiveness of the new structure, and in view of the new workload, we have carried out reforms, of which - and this is certainly not the least important - the creation of a General Secretariat, which now carries out a large part of the more purely organisational tasks. It should be remembered that this reform affected the Bank at a time when the financial crisis was protracted and the sovereign debt crisis was unleashed. Across Europe, central banks have been in the breach non-stop, deploying the full range of tools at their disposal. All this has contributed to making 2011 a year of exceptional mobilization for the Bank, and this in its multiple sectors of activity, which are detailed in the first chapter of the corporate report that has been given to you. At the Management Committee, since our last General Meeting, the departure of Director Praet has been compensated by the appointment of Director Pierre Wunsch. He is a high-flying economist whose expertise, particularly in financial stability, is particularly timely. I propose that we now move on to the detailed presentation of the annual accounts, which will already answer some of the questions we have received. The remaining questions will be addressed in the question and answer session that will follow. I would like to thank the shareholders who sent us their questions in advance and in writing, thus facilitating the preparation and smooth running of this meeting. Thank you for your attention and now give the floor to Director Pierre Wunsch.

Title: Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders
text: Ordinary general meeting of shareholders of 27 May 2013 Assemblee generale ordinaire des actionnaires du 27 mai 2013 INTRODUCTORY STATEMENT BY THE GOVERNOR EXPOSe INTRODUCTIF DU GOUVERNEUR Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the Executive Committee, I would like to welcome you to this ordinary general meeting of the shareholders of the National Bank of Belgium. On behalf of the Management Committee, I welcome you to this ordinary general meeting of shareholders of the National Bank of Belgium. I would like to introduce this House by briefly referring to some of the important changes that the Bank has undergone in 2012. If we had been able to describe 2011 as historic, because it had seen the Bank integrate a new business with the resumption of the counter-prudential, the year 2012 cannot pass for a year of stabilization. In recent years, the organisation of counter-prudential supervision at European level has seen its architecture change considerably, with the rise of the national central banks and the European Central Bank in this area. Among the major lessons of the crisis was the need for a more integrated economic and monetary union. In December 2012, the Heads of State and Government agreed on the basis for its completion, as well as a timetable. Of these measures, the one that affects and will most directly affect the Bank is the decision to set up what has been called a banking union. This includes the Single Supervisory Mechanism for credit institutions, but should also extend to the creation of a common resolution authority and a common deposit guarantee scheme. The Single Supervisory Mechanism will oversee all credit institutions in the euro area, i.e. more than 4 000 credit institutions. A distinction will be made between significant banks meeting the criteria listed in the text of the European regulation, i.e. about 140 banking groups, which bring together a thousand institutions, whose supervision the ECB will centralize, and the so-called less significant banks, the national supervisors will remain directly competent under the ecb. It is still premature to assess the future impact of the European Supervisory Mechanism on national banking supervisors in the euro area. It is a given that, at this stage, nothing should change in terms of the prudential counter-prudential of insurance and market infrastructures or in terms of the oversight of these infrastructures. For the rest, in Belgium, it is estimated that the direct supervision of the SNB should only be exercised over a limited number of banks. The centralisation of supervision and decision-making in Frankfurt for significant banking groups will, however, require increased collaboration between national supervisors  including the Bank  and the European Central Bank. Some of the Bank's specialists will be offered the possibility of secondment to the European Central Bank. The architecture of the system also leaves a broad competence to the national authorities. This project is therefore very rich in opportunities for supervisors in the euro area, and for the National Bank in particular. However, the detailed development of the banking union project still involves many challenges. This project and its preparations have already mobilized a lot of energy. The Bank has been fully involved in the various working groups organised at Eurosystem level. At the Bank itself, a multidisciplinary working group supports the work carried out at this level. Given the proximity of the deadline, set in 2014, all this work is still expected to accelerate and become clearer in the coming months. The scale of the work and the constraint of deadlines make this task an extraordinary challenge for all the counter-competent authorities. The organisation of prudential supervision in the Bank is also the subject of constant reflection. One year after the integration of this activity, the Management Committee devoted a seminar to it. One of the most important strategic policies formulated was to improve strategic governance in this area. Supervision should be sought which is based primarily on the risks incurred by the institutions, which presupposes that those institutions are classified according to this parameter. We also proceeded to the analysis of the business models of the large Belgian financial groups, taking into account the various challenges they face, such as the difficult macroeconomic environment, the changes in the supervisory framework and the increased competition in the domestic market. The quality of supervision can still be improved, but the IMF has expressed a fairly positive view of the quality of this supervision in the context of its Financial Sector Assessment Programme. The Executive Committee has also launched an ambitious project to methodologically strengthen the function of prudential inspection. The aim is to harmonise and update methods, standardise procedures, automate the follow-up of contracts to a large extent and, finally, revalue the inspection function. This new methodology will be set out in due course in a detailed communication to the sectors concerned. Since the year 2000, the Bank's strategic positioning has been laid down in five-yearly master plans. The rapid and largely unpredictable development of its working environment has meant that a number of hypotheses that formed the basis of the master plan 2010-2015 are currently outdated. For the period 2014-2018, a new master plan was therefore developed. At the end of a special seminar of the Executive Committee, it was decided to convert the master plans into annual action plans that are drawn up by each of the departments and autonomous services. These action plans will in turn serve as a reference framework for both the preparation of budgets and the performance management of the entire staff. The strategic thinking exercise of the Executive Committee also resulted in a number of important decisions regarding the organization of the company. The Committee thus noted that the quota of euro banknotes allocated to the Bank's printing works was insufficient to achieve an adequate volume of activity. Since the search for a partner did not yield any results, the Executive Committee has chosen to phase out production and to stop it in 2020. Until then, every effort will be made to make the service more profitable, while the staff in question will gradually be deployed for other tasks. As far as money circulation is concerned, the processing of banknotes largely depends on the logistical decisions of the commercial banks and of the companies specialising in the transport and processing of cash. In Antwerp, as a result of the closure of the cash centre of a major commercial bank, the processing of values in the Bank's local branch has decreased significantly. The Management Committee has therefore decided to close this site. In this case, too, the staff concerned will be assigned in full to other departments of the Bank. The strategic exercise also made it possible to concretely start a reflection on the Staff Club, the objective being to separate itself from the infrastructure while ensuring the continuation of the sports and cultural activities of the staff. I will come back to this item later in the agenda. The processing of retail interbank non-cash payments in Belgium is also changing. Carried out since 1974 by the Clearing and Exchange Centre, an asbl set up by belgian banks and managed at the National Bank, this activity has now become Europeanised. Indeed, Belgian banks have decided to switch to a pan-European clearing system: the French platform called Technological Exchange and Processing Systems. In March 2013, the CEC therefore terminated its operating contract with the Bank. In other areas, the Bank's position is strengthening on the contrary: the year under review saw the scope of collection of the Centrale des credits aux entreprises expand. The financial and economic crisis has indeed shown that good risk control by financial institutions, particularly those related to bank credit, is essential and that new measures relating to the centralization of credit data can contribute to this. The substantial enrichment of this data will enable the Bank to better understand the risks faced by the financial sector, while participants will benefit from more information during their consultations, which will help them to refine the management of their own risks. These rapid developments need to be responded to with proactive and dynamic management methods. In that context, I have talked about the changes we have made to our management cycle. Among senior executives, we have also introduced a policy of internal mobility that can promote the exchange of experience and make the teams more dynamic. For a company which, like the Bank, wants to be at the service of society, the pursuit of the most efficient organisation possible is a priority objective. The development we are currently experiencing is accelerating the transition from our attitude from a manufacturing company to a knowledge company. It is in this direction that its future must be mapped out. I suggest that we now proceed to the detailed presentation of the annual accounts, in which you will already receive an answer to some of the questions we have received. The other questions will be dealt with during the question time. I would like to thank the shareholders who have provided us with their questions in advance and in writing, which has facilitated the preparation and smooth running of this meeting. Thank you for your attention and I now give the floor to Director Pierre Wunsch.

Ook de organisatie van het prudentieel toezicht in de Bank is voorwerp van constante bezinning. Een jaar na de integratie van deze activiteit heeft het Directiecomit<8e> er een seminarie aan gewijd. Een van de belangrijkste strategische beleidslijnen die er werden geformuleerd, was de verbetering van de strategische governance ter zake. Er moet worden gestreefd naar een toezicht dat in de eerste plaats gebaseerd is op de door de instellingen gelopen risico's, wat veronderstelt dat die instellingen volgens deze parameter worden ingedeeld. Wij zijn overigens ook overgegaan op de analyse van de business-modellen van de grote belgische financiele groepen, waarbij rekening gehouden wordt met de verschillende uitdagingen waarmee deze geconfronteerd worden, zoals de moeilijke macro-economische omgeving, de wijzigingen in het toezichtskader en de verhoogde mededinging op de binnenlandse markt. De kwaliteit van het toezicht is nog voor verbetering vatbaar, maar het IMF heeft zich in het kader van zijn Financial Sector Assessment Program vrij positief uitgelaten over de kwaliteit van dit toezicht. Het Directiecomit<8e> heeft overigens een ambitieus project gelanceerd tot methodologische versteviging van de functie prudenti<91>le inspectie. Het is de bedoeling de methoden te harmoniseren en te actualiseren, de procedures te standaardiseren, de follow-up van de opdrachten in hoge mate te automatiseren en, ten slotte, de inspectiefunctie te herwaarderen. Deze nieuwe methodologie zal te gelegener tijd in een uitvoerige mededeling aan de betrokken sectoren worden uiteengezet. Sedert het jaar 2000 wordt de strategische positionering van de Bank vastgelegd in vijfjaarlijkse masterplannen. De snelle en grotendeels onvoorspelbare ontwikkeling van haar werkomgeving heeft tot gevolg gehad dat een aantal hypothesen die ten grondslag lagen aan het masterplan 2010-2015 op dit ogenblik achterhaald zijn. Voor de periode 2014-2018 werd dus een nieuw masterplan uitgewerkt. Na afloop van een speciaal seminarie van het Directiecomit<8e> werd besloten de masterplannen voortaan om te zetten in jaarlijkse actieplannen die worden uitgewerkt door elk van de departementen en autonome diensten. Deze actieplannen zullen op hun beurt als referentiekader dienen zowel voor de opmaak van de begrotingen als voor het performance management van het gehele personeel. De strategische denkoefening van het Directiecomit<8e> resulteerde overigens in een aantal belangrijke beslissingen wat de organisatie van de onderneming betreft. Het Comit<8e> heeft er aldus akte van genomen dat het aan de drukkerij van de Bank toegewezen quotum eurobankbiljetten onvoldoende was om een toereikend activiteitsvolume te halen. Aangezien het zoeken van een partner geen resultaat opleverde, heeft het Directiecomit<8e> ervoor gekozen de productie geleidelijk af te bouwen en in 2020 stop te zetten. Tot dan zal alles in het werk worden gesteld om de dienst renderender te maken, terwijl het personeel in kwestie gaandeweg voor andere taken zal worden ingezet. Wat de geldomloop betreft, is de verwerking van de biljetten grotendeels afhankelijk van de logistieke beslissingen van de commerci<91>le banken en van de bedrijven die gespecialiseerd zijn in het vervoer en de verwerking van cash. In Antwerpen is, als gevolg van de sluiting van het cash center van een belangrijke commerci<91>le bank, de verwerking van waarden in de lokale vestiging van de Bank fors afgenomen. Het Directiecomit<8e> heeft derhalve besloten deze vestiging te sluiten. Ook in dit geval zal het betrokken personeel integraal bij andere diensten van de Bank worden ingedeeld. L<d5>exercice strat<8e>gique a <8e>galement permis d<d5>entamer concr<8f>tement une r<8e>flexion sur le Club du personnel, l<d5>objectif <8e>tant de se s<8e>parer de l<d5>infrastructure tout en assurant la poursuite des activit<8e>s sportives et culturelles du personnel. Je reviendrai sur ce point plus loin dans l<d5>ordre du jour. Le traitement des paiements scripturaux interbancaires de d<8e>tail en Belgique change lui aussi dpoque. Assur<8e>e depuis 1974 par le Centre dchange et de compensation, asbl constitu<8e>e par les banques belges et g<8e>r<8e>e <88> la Banque nationale, cette activit<8e> s<d5>est d<8e>sormais europ<8e>anis<8e>e. En effet, les banques belges ont d<8e>cid<8e> de passer <88> un syst<8f>me de compensation paneurop<8e>en: la plateforme fran<8d>aise d<8e>nomm<8e>e Syst<8f>mes Technologiques d<d5>Echange et de Traitement. En mars 2013, le CEC a donc mis un terme au contrat d'exploitation qui le lie <88> la Banque. Dans d<d5>autres domaines, la position de la Banque se renforce au contraire : l<d5>ann<8e>e sous revue a vu slargir le champ de collecte de la Centrale des cr<8e>dits aux entreprises. La crise financi<8f>re et <8e>conomique a en effet montr<8e> qu<d5>une bonne ma<94>trise des risques par les institutions financi<8f>res, notamment ceux li<8e>s au cr<8e>dit bancaire, est indispensable et que de nouvelles mesures relatives <88> la centralisation des donn<8e>es sur les cr<8e>dits peuvent y contribuer. L<d5>enrichissement substantiel de ces donn<8e>es permettra <88> la Banque de mieux appr<8e>hender les risques encourus par le secteur financier, tandis que les participants b<8e>n<8e>ficieront de plus d'informations lors de leurs consultations, ce qui les aidera <88> affiner la gestion de leurs propres risques. Op deze snelle ontwikkelingen moet worden gereageerd met proactieve en dynamische beheersmethoden. Ik heb het in dat verband gehad over de wijzigingen die we hebben aangebracht in onze managementcyclus. Bij de hogere kaderleden hebben we ook een beleid van interne mobiliteit ge<95>ntroduceerd dat de uitwisseling van ervaring kan bevorderen en dat de teams dynamischer kan maken. Voor een onderneming die, zoals de Bank, ten dienste wil staan van de maatschappij, is het nastreven van een zo effici<91>nt mogelijke organisatie een prioritaire doelstelling. De ontwikkeling die we thans doormaken, versnelt de overgang van onze instelling van een productieonderneming op een kennisonderneming. Het is in die richting dat haar toekomst moet worden uitgestippeld. Ik stel voor dat we nu overgaan tot de gedetailleerde voorstelling van de jaarrekening, waarin u reeds een antwoord zal krijgen op sommige vragen die we hebben ontvangen. De andere vragen zullen worden behandeld tijdens de question time. Ik dank de aandeelhouders die ons hun vragen vooraf en schriftelijk hebben bezorgd, wat de voorbereiding en het vlotte verloop van deze vergadering heeft vergemakkelijkt. Ik dank u voor uw aandacht en ik geef nu het woord aan directeur Pierre Wunsch.

Title: Les Belges sont riches
text: Mosquito 10.05.2023 Pierre Wunsch, Governor of the NBB - "Belgians are rich" Mosquito - Nicolas Sohy Prices keep rising... To stop them, the NBB is raising rates. Its governor admits that this policy makes access to the real estate market more difficult. But it would be essential to finally relieve the household wallet. Eighty-nine euros. This is the difference in the price of the average shopping cart in March 2023 compared to March 2022. This is an increase of 20.6%. Suffice to say that the automatic indexation of wages at the end of January is no longer making up for the drop in purchasing power... Supermarkets are the shops where prices are rising the most. Average inflation is fortunately lower. For the whole of 2023, it is expected to be around 4.2%. In this context, the National Bank of Belgium is making sure to calm things down to relieve households and businesses. Pierre Wunsch is its governor. Is the purchasing power crisis finally behind us? PIERRE WUNSCH - No. There are "second round" effects. Inflation can be separated into two phases. It was first linked to the explosion in electricity and gas prices. This phase is slowly coming behind us. We hope, for good. Then, it moved to certain goods, particularly food. Inflation is now widespread in the services sector because workers - and this is logical - are asking for compensation. In Belgium, it comes with the automatic indexation of wages. Inflation therefore remains above our 2% target, although it must continue to fall. The cost of living is still expected to rise in 2023 and, more reasonably, in 2024. However, our models have been calibrated over a period of very low inflation. But what we are experiencing now has not been experienced since the oil shocks of the 1970s. As a result, our experience remains limited. What can the NBB do to relieve households? Central banks cannot perform miracles. We cannot say "from tomorrow, energy prices will be lower", because we import energy from abroad and we have no control over it. On the other hand, when inflation spreads to the rest of the economy, we can try to keep it under control. How? By slowing down demand. For this reason, the European Central Bank and the NBB are betting on an increase in interest rates. Citizens sometimes have the impression that they are losing on all fronts: prices are exploding and rates, especially mortgage rates, are soaring. In Belgium, we have become accustomed to periods during which we did not have to be so attentive to inflation. Today, we are forced to intervene quite vigorously to keep it under control. This implies a sharp increase in interest rates, the likes of which have not been seen since the early 80s. We want to bring inflation back to 2% without breaking the machine. The risk is that if we don't do enough, inflation will continue to feed itself. If another shock were to appear, we could then experience slippage. This is visible today in some emerging countries where the cost of living has doubled. Inflation is a pressure cooker under pressure. It must be cooled. That's what we do. Yes, it has an impact. Yes, mortgages are getting more expensive. Yes, access to credit is more difficult... We are in a period of transition: rates are higher and property prices have not really fallen yet. Normally, the market will adjust... Is there a difference between the real drop in purchasing power and the perception of Belgians? Inflation of 10% contains several realities. Workers who are indexed once a year suffer more than those who are indexed every month. Some groups, especially the less privileged, are more exposed to rising energy and food prices. This is why measures have been taken by the government, such as the extension of the social tariff for energy. This measure has made it possible to cushion the social shock. Then there is the debate on indexation and whether or not it is appropriate. It aims to preserve purchasing power. It's positive. On the other hand, it transfers most of the cost to companies. This can lead to competitiveness problems. We were lucky, because gas prices finally collapsed after an explosion in 2022. We will probably just lose competitiveness for two years. But we have seen the limits of the system. Today, the debate must be conducted: is the automatic indexation of wages optimal in its current form? This is an ultra-sensitive issue. However, it would be beneficial to discuss certain adaptations to better protect workers and spare companies. Especially since the long-term consequences are possible bankruptcies, and therefore job losses. Do Belgians still have money? Belgians can be considered to be "rich" thanks to the combined wealth of individuals, one of the highest in Europe. In 2021, it is equivalent to more than 1,100 billion euros. The real estate portfolio is more than 1,700 billion. This is equivalent to about 250% of GDP. That being said, 50% of Belgians have very small assets. Among them, some have very low incomes. The pandemic forced savings. Admittedly, wealth has fallen slightly in recent years, but this is linked to the fall in share values. Some of the money stays in savings accounts. These savings do not sleep, as we sometimes hear, they circulate. There are deposits on one side and loans to households and businesses on the other. The money in savings accounts is therefore useful for our economy. And then people can pick it up whenever they want, if they need it. The collapse of Credit Switzerland and Silicon Valley Bank has worried everyone. What is the state of health of the Belgian banks? Since 2008, we have strengthened regulation. We have more information about banks than we did back then. Banks have higher capital and liquidity buffer requirements. It is therefore difficult to imagine a crisis, but I cannot rule it out either. After the events at Credit Switzerland and SVB, the figures were turned around in all directions. There are no loopholes. At the NBB, we have a culture of great risk aversion. We have always been strict in interpreting the rules. I have only one concern: social networks. Because of a runaway effect, thousands or millions of customers can convince each other to withdraw billions of dollars in deposits at once. If an unfounded rumour appears, and it convinces on social networks, a bank can find itself in great difficulty. This phenomenon is completely new. This is our question of the moment: how sustainable are the deposit bases of Belgian banks? Does NewB's failure show that a "different" bank has no place in Belgium? For me, the question is more global: is there room for a new bank today? Regardless of his positioning... The Belgian market is relatively saturated. The NBB demanded, as it does for all other banking institutions, that NewB raise sufficient capital and equity. This was necessary so as not to endanger customer deposits. NewB has not been able to set up a profitable business. We can also wonder about the nature of the craze around NewB. Perhaps it was mainly media-driven? In any case, it has not turned into a very large appetite on the part of customers to deposit their money. Should we be worried about the digitalization of banks? We live in an increasingly European system of regulation. In this context, it is quite normal to see cross-border digital banks appear. For some generations, the idea of going to a counter, of queuing, is unthinkable. Young people are more likely to use digital channels. That said, the day they want to take out a mortgage, they prefer to have a banker in front of them. Banks are trying to adapt by keeping a physical presence if possible for the important moments in life.
